Two bottleneck choices could be revisited. review#24 and review#25 use PR-CAPS and PR-VERIFYBUDGET where the alias table maps OB15 to B12 and OB17 to PR-FIELDEVIDENCE; the flags admit this. review#20 uses PR-CAPS although REV-B5 aliases to B3-LOOP.

ideas.name: Two refuters per claim: repository and operations
ideas.how: Each falsifiable claim is attacked by two fresh Opus refuters, one reading the repository, one the operations view, with a default verdict of refuted and executed counter-evidence.
ideas.problem: We want every recommendation's premises checked before we build on it, including facts about real hosts and phones that a code-only reader misses.
ideas.stands: In use: 45 panel claims attacked; several premises were refuted or unmeasured and narrowed before the plan [M]. Knowledge store: 1 confirmed, 21 narrowed, 8 refuted [M]; second pass 6 narrowed [M].
ideas.next: Re-run the refuter runs lost to a usage limit if cash and books questions become decisions; re-run on new mechanisms.
ideas.flag: Seven refuter runs on the cash and books claims never happened (usage limit); the older record also cited a lost-runs id that I mapped to the limit-stop item without listing it.

ideas.name: Delta check of a plan revision by fresh critics
ideas.how: Fresh Opus critics read only the changes to a plan, Sonnet re-locates every citation, and findings are tabled and folded into the next version.
ideas.problem: Each plan revision can bring in new defects, so I want a fresh read of what changed before the revision is trusted.
ideas.stands: Tested: the v6-to-v8 delta check found 1 blocker, 20 major, 20 minor [M]; the section 7 amendment critic found 1 blocker, 7 major, 12 minor [M]; 19 accepted, 1 open ruling.
ideas.next: Repeat after any large plan change; rule on managers paying or voiding a closed job before P7a merges.
ideas.flag: Open owner ruling: whether managers may pay or void on a closed job.

ideas.name: Completeness critic over a draft
ideas.how: One Opus critic at high effort reads the draft and its register, lists missing items, unsupported claims, contradictions and readability problems; each becomes a numbered amendment.
ideas.problem: A finished draft can still lack mechanisms, hold contradictions or be hard for me to read, so we want a last read for completeness.
ideas.stands: In use on the knowledge-store design, run twice: 19 missing, 15 unsupported, 19 contradictions, 9 readability items [M]; later 22 contradictions, 15 mismatches, 17 leftovers [M]. All text repair.
ideas.next: Run again after major edits and before owner review.

ideas.name: Assess, refute by default, then judge idea sweeps
ideas.how: Cards are clustered into families; two Opus reviewers score each, a fresh refuter attacks every adopt or trial family by default, and a judge applies the rule.
ideas.problem: We want to judge about 1,900 sweep cards fairly, without the orchestrator scoring them and without one reader's enthusiasm promoting weak ideas.
ideas.stands: In use on two sweeps: Horthy, of 144 attacked families 65 refuted and 79 narrowed, none passed [M]; BAML, adopt 24 to 0 and trial 22 to 4 [M].
ideas.next: Give the next sweep's assessment brief the design text; trial whether refuting by default earns its cost.

ideas.name: Verify a rewrite by content, not commit message
ideas.how: After a plan rewrite, compare the actual text with the intended text instead of trusting the commit message.
ideas.problem: A rewritten plan was reported done by its commit message while content had been lost; we want to catch that before anyone builds on it.
ideas.stands: Adopted as a plan rule, drawn from the program's one recorded state loss [M]. Not measured further.
ideas.next: Apply at every plan version bump; add it to the gate checklists.

ideas.name: Recurring defect shapes in the reviewer brief
ideas.how: The seven recurring defect shapes, plus an eighth for any new stored copy or flag, go in the Opus refute brief with a required line per shape.
ideas.problem: Defect shapes we already know sit in a checklist reviewers never see, so the same kinds of defect keep coming back.
ideas.stands: Trial: moved into the ship plan's top trial 6; not yet tested. First step is a look-back test on known-defect diffs, with and without the line.
ideas.next: Run that look-back test on 3 to 4 known-defect diffs [T]; count cases caught.

ideas.name: Verdict lists suppressions and gate-config changes
ideas.how: The reviewer's verdict lists every added inline suppression and every edit to lint, type, import or CI config with its reason, checked by a diff grep.
ideas.problem: I want to know when a check was made to pass by suppressing it or editing its configuration, instead of fixing the code.
ideas.stands: Suppressions sentence adopted; gate-config naming and the mechanical file list are trials over the first 5 code PRs [T]. Not yet tested; the testbed gate already refuses added skips.
ideas.next: Over 5 code PRs [T], a scripted grep must find nothing the verdict omitted; fix the path set.
ideas.flag: Mixed status: one sentence adopt, the other parts trial; the record's status is adopt.

ideas.name: Deviations-from-Scope report and unrequested changes
ideas.how: A journal heading reports deviations from the plan, and the Opus reviewer lists unaccounted hunks, boxes ticked without a diff, and any change no Scope box requires.
ideas.problem: We want to see when a diff drifts from the planned Scope, or adds unrequested abstractions, since only the implementer checks that today.
ideas.stands: Trial, not yet tested, over the first 3 to 5 Opus-reviewed phase PRs [T]. The compile's refuters narrowed two of the parts to FixFlow-only.
ideas.next: Add to the reviewer brief; count deviations the journal lists against ones the reviewer finds, across three PRs [T].

ideas.name: Reviewer-brief additions with no testbed counterpart
ideas.how: A bundle of eight FixFlow reviewer items: suppression and gate-config lists, deviation report, defect shapes, gate-file list, and a design audit.
ideas.problem: We want FixFlow reviewers to catch plan deviations, unnamed config exceptions, over-engineering and design flaws that the testbed never needed to handle.
ideas.stands: Trial, not yet tested here. The compile's refuters narrowed five of the items to FixFlow-only; one would add a standing owner step.
ideas.next: Use the claims-file script (mechanism 2) for the gate-file list instead.
ideas.origin: Bottleneck compile, after the Dex Horthy sweep
ideas.flag: Overlaps review#37, #38, #39 and #41, which carry the same items individually.

ideas.name: One cumulative-drift audit after ten PRs
ideas.how: One fresh Opus audit after the 10th merged code PR, scoped to the diff from the P1 merge to main, with a pass bar of 2 or more accepted findings.
ideas.problem: Per-PR review cannot see drift that builds across PRs, such as a helper reimplemented twice, and we want one look at the whole.
ideas.stands: Trial, one audit only; not yet tested. Pass bar is at least 2 owner-accepted findings [T] after the 10th merged code PR [T].
ideas.next: Run the audit and count owner-accepted drift findings; if it meets the bar, repeat it.

ideas.name: Review bots, unmeasured-as-failure, hand-back labelling
ideas.how: A per-PR Opus reviewer is in place, gates treat a missing scan as failed, and Claude Code labels a subagent's report as model output with no user authority.
ideas.problem: We want review that adds no noise, no missing scan counted as clean, and no instructions smuggled in through hand-backs.
ideas.stands: Already in place or provided by the platform; nothing new to build or measure.
ideas.next: Keep using it.
ideas.flag: Record says already done or platform behaviour, so no separate evidence of benefit.

ideas.name: Pure prompt-input boundary for the skeptic
ideas.how: A small function returns only claim, evidence and failing condition, with a replay test that the rendered prompt holds no forbidden field. About 10 lines [E].
ideas.problem: The skeptic must see only the claim, evidence and failing condition, but nothing in the code stops other fields leaking into its prompt.
ideas.stands: Trial, not yet tested, not refuted. It is hygiene: no contaminated skeptic is on record.
ideas.next: Add the function and a test that fails when a forbidden field is added; I decide if hygiene alone justifies it.

ideas.name: Numbered evidence ids for verifiers
ideas.how: Evidence handed to verifiers and skeptics is numbered; they cite ids and the script rejects unknown ids.
ideas.problem: We worried a verifier could cite a fabricated URL or quote.
ideas.stands: Parked: it conflicts with the design, where a refuted verdict needs counter-evidence the skeptic finds itself, and the citation check already catches fabrication. No fabricated URL on record.
ideas.next: Would return if a fabricated URL shows up in a verification step.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, after a talk on short ids

ideas.name: List dimensions and covered combinations in review briefs
ideas.how: Add a line asking the reviewer to list the dimensions of the change and the combinations the tests cover, in the next 3 briefs [T].
ideas.problem: Defects can hide in combinations of changes that no test covers, as in BAML's own post-mortem.
ideas.stands: Parked: the refuter found one post-mortem is thin evidence, our briefs already name similar shapes, and the trial had no control.
ideas.next: Would return if several of our defects trace to uncovered combinations.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, after a BAML post-mortem

ideas.name: Skeptic round with forced verbatim citation
ideas.how: A skeptic files counterexamples that must quote the passage; the designer accepts with a diff or rejects citing a verbatim rule; one round, then stop.
ideas.problem: Reviews hand-wave in both directions; we want attacks and rebuttals that point at exact text.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed, once: 21 attacks, 12 accepted, 3 rejected on one ground, 6 on another [M]; 15 design elements revised [M]. Both sides were the same model family.
ideas.next: Adopt the quote-forced attack and rebuttal format in FixFlow gate reviews.

ideas.name: Dated audits by parallel automated reviewers
ideas.how: Three parallel automated reviewers plus an integration review audit a repo, separating hash-verified preservation from substantive review; a static fit audit reads a tool's code.
ideas.problem: We want stale guidance and missing evidence found in a repo before we build on it, and a clear boundary on what a recall tool puts in context.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed, done once: 61 files reviewed [M], 14 findings [M], 641 cached members re-hashed with no failures [M], 5 peer-review corrections closed [M]. Cost not recorded.
ideas.next: Copy the dated-audit format with a stale-guidance table as a CLAUDE.md drift check for FixFlow.
ideas.flag: Automated review, not human; findings are static observations, not reproduced defects.

ideas.name: Hand-written reading-coverage ledger
ideas.how: A file-by-file, page-by-page table records what was read in full or sampled, with access limits and a verification record.
ideas.problem: A report may claim sources were read when they were not, so we want coverage to be visible.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed: 41 coverage rows checked by script on 2026-09-30 [M]. Hand-maintained, so it drifts; effect on rework not yet measured.
ideas.next: Generate the table from agent transcripts instead of writing it by hand.

ideas.name: Specialist reviewers for offline sync, migrations, security
ideas.how: Three sourced skills with paired Opus reviewer agents, each refuting by default and running fixed commands only, never probing a live host.
ideas.problem: Our offline engine, populated-table migrations and security code have FixFlow-specific rules that generic checklists miss or tell agents to wrongly fix.
ideas.stands: Built: skills and Opus agents on draft PR #185, not merged and not yet tested.
ideas.next: Use them on the P1, P2a/P2b, P6a and P7a reviews.
ideas.origin: Skills packages, after TanStack/db and OWASP ASVS

ideas.name: Adjudication record so later sessions can disagree
ideas.how: At G2 we write down the conflicts the orchestrator adjudicated and why, plus the verified register and open risks.
ideas.problem: Without the reasons kept, a later session would have to re-run everything instead of disagreeing with reasons.
ideas.stands: Designed as part of the G2 output in the orchestration design; not yet tested.
ideas.next: Write it at G2.

ideas.name: Blast-radius touch list for a fix
ideas.how: A script lists changed functions, callers, importers, co-changing files and touching tests, and attaches the list to the reviewer's brief.
ideas.problem: Fixes introduce defects in files nobody looked at, and we want reviewers shown what a fix could touch.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 phase 3; not yet run. Zero-token test on ten recorded fix cases [T]: kept if six of ten [T] fall inside and the list stays near 15 files [T].
ideas.next: Run the zero-token test on the ten recorded cases; hubs need a depth limit and grouping.
ideas.origin: Bottleneck compile; Harness v2 design; Graph test
ideas.flag: The compile's verdict was trial; the v2 design records it as designed. I kept designed.

ideas.name: Cross-runtime contract map
ideas.how: A script extracts client URL to backend route, settings keys, the migration chain, slice contracts, outbox kinds and handlers, and invariants tied to files, as review input.
ideas.problem: Silent breaks between web, mobile, backend and configuration live in contracts, not imports, so neither a search nor an import graph sees them.
ideas.stands: Trial, partly built as a script: 65 of 73 client URL literals matched 77 route decorators [M]; 46 settings keys, 46 migration links [M]. Value to review untested.
ideas.next: Test at zero tokens on the recorded defect chains, beside the touch-list test.
ideas.flag: One raw record says idea, one trial; I kept trial. Script is partly built but its value is unproven, so maturity stays 1.

ideas.name: Screenshot capture and rubric scoring of screens
ideas.how: A capture script screenshots every role and screen at 375 and 1280 px with a manifest; an Opus rubric review and refutation score the results.
ideas.problem: We want screen quality and UI changes checked with visible before and after evidence, without a human looking at everything.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed: 130 pages, 260 PNGs [M]; rubric score rose from 64 to 110 of 160 [M]; of 59 findings 16 fixed, 20 partly, 22 not, 1 regressed [M].
ideas.next: Build a Playwright capture for FixFlow's React app; treat model scores as triage only.

ideas.name: Saved script for the PR-review stage
ideas.how: One committed workflow script takes the register ids and head commit, calls the PR-reviewer agent with a verdict schema, and compares commits in code.
ideas.problem: The PR-review stage is prose steps, so commit binding and the per-id fail-and-pass table depend on the agent, and workflows get rewritten each time.
ideas.stands: Trial after P1; not yet tested. Only the deterministic part is scripted; the whole-routine version was refuted.
ideas.next: Run prose review in P1 and audit it, then use the script on the next 3 PRs [T].

ideas.name: Record-only rule checks over returned objects
ideas.how: A node script over the committed evidence JSON checks quote length, listed URLs, unique ids and evidence format, run record-only with no retry.
ideas.problem: Agent outputs are checked by judges or by eye; cheap rule checks could catch violations the gates missed without spending tokens.
ideas.stands: Trial, not yet tested; downgraded from adopt. The refuter's naive pattern flagged 174 of 707 evidence strings [M], mostly legitimate, so the allow-list is the work.
ideas.next: Write it with an allow-list (about an hour [E]); adopt only if it finds a real missed violation.

ideas.name: Pick among candidate fixes by executed test
ideas.how: Generate three candidate fixes per recorded chain; a frozen pre-written test plus a guard-removal check rejects the candidate that causes the defect.
ideas.problem: A single fix often creates a new defect, and choosing among candidates by a test that runs may avoid that.
ideas.stands: Deferred in harness v2, not run unless switched on. Outside, on SWE-bench Lite: 25.7% by vote, 27.0% with a regression filter, 32.0% with a reproduction test [S].
ideas.next: Decide after the fix-round contract's replay (D20); live only if the selector works.
ideas.origin: Harness v2 design, after SWE-bench candidate selection
ideas.flag: Merged record said idea; the v2 design says deferred and the compile said trial. I used deferred.

ideas.name: Design adjudicated by sweep, judges, refuters, owner critique
ideas.how: Four workflows: a research sweep, four architects scored by three judges, refuters plus a completeness critic, then each owner-critique point checked by two verifiers.
ideas.problem: A design from one session carries unchecked claims, and an owner critique is sometimes right and sometimes not, so we neither obey nor ignore it blindly.
ideas.stands: In use on the knowledge-store design: about 15M subagent tokens [M]; scores out of 360: A 292, C 282, D 281, B 222 [M]; critique verdicts partly or mostly right [M]; 20 amendments.
ideas.next: Reuse the pattern for other designs and later critiques.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design, after the Orchestration design
ideas.flag: Judges were lost once to a usage limit and re-run from cached proposals.

ideas.name: Sonnet builds, Opus reviews
ideas.how: The cheaper model builds and the stronger model reviews. Available today with no library.
ideas.problem: We hoped Sonnet at lower effort could match Opus through cached reasoning, but on judgment-heavy work the quality came from review.
ideas.stands: In use: an Opus reviewer found a serious defect in 9 of 14 Opus-built clinic slices [M]. Sonnet-Opus gap 2 to 8 points [M]; parity provable here only within plus or minus 11 to 14 points [M].
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: Audit the phase routine's seven obligations
ideas.how: A fresh Opus auditor sees only artifacts (PR, git log, edit history, results, owner view, closing message) and scores 7 binary obligations per phase.
ideas.problem: Compliance with the phase routine is self-reported, so skipped steps look the same as done ones.
ideas.stands: Trial over P1 and P2a; not yet tested. The source evidence was one confounded anecdote, and a count-and-split version was refuted.
ideas.next: Audit P1 and P2a against the 7 obligations; add a short skill checklist only if a step was missed.

ideas.name: Agents audit run transcripts for wasted calls
ideas.how: An Opus pass reads the six lane transcripts and lists wasted calls and ignored rules; the owner or orchestrator triages.
ideas.problem: We wondered whether briefs waste calls or ignore their own rules without anyone seeing it.
ideas.stands: Parked: the refuter found recorded quota failures came from fan-out size and effort, not waste inside agents; fixed overhead dominates. The earlier transcript audit found nothing that caused a mistake.
ideas.next: Would return if a transcript audit shows waste that caused a failure.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, after a talk on agent testing

ideas.name: Orchestrator decides; subagents only gather and verify
ideas.how: The main session sets hypotheses, routes work, reads every result and makes the calls. Subagents gather, analyse and verify. A cheaper model's verdict can narrow a deeper brief, never remove it.
ideas.problem: We want all judgement in one place, so a cheap agent's first impression never becomes a decision by inertia and never silently cancels a deeper investigation.
ideas.stands: Designed in the orchestration design (v3) as a rule. The gate and review records show the main session judging, but no subagent output has yet been audited for being treated as a decision.
ideas.next: Run the first workflows under this rule and check no subagent output is treated as a decision.
ideas.flag: The gate and review records show the main session judging, but the source reports this as a design rule awaiting the owner's W0 pre-flight, so I kept designed.

ideas.name: Staged workflows with judging gates between them
ideas.how: Owner pre-flight, cheap wide discovery, gate, Opus deep-dive, gate, then the phase plan. At each gate the main session reads results by id and writes a record. No synthesis agent.
ideas.problem: We want cheap wide discovery, narrow expensive deep dives and a recorded decision between stages, so the plan is designed only after a verified picture exists.
ideas.stands: In use for the ship program: both gates written 2026-11-01. Discovery covered 16/16 areas with about 1.67M [M] subagent tokens in 14 min [M]; the deep-dive ran 8 analysts, 139 [M] findings, about 3.3M [M] tokens, 23 min [M].
ideas.next: Keep using a gate record after each later stage.
ideas.flag: The design raw record said designed; the review record shows both gates actually run, so I used in_use. The phase plan itself was designed after the second gate.

ideas.name: Model tiers by role, raise effort before tier
ideas.how: Haiku extracts into closed schemas; Sonnet maps, researches and runs gates; Opus analyses and refutes; the main session judges. Model and effort are named on every start; raise effort before the tier.
ideas.problem: Model choice per agent is our main cost lever. We want the strongest model only where mistakes are expensive, and no agent running at a strength nobody chose.
ideas.stands: In use in FixFlow discovery, deep-dive and review, and the whole clinic build; built as 6 Opus, 5 Sonnet, 1 Haiku agent definitions [M]. No token or cost measurement of tiering yet; every clinic slice still needed 2-4 [M] review rounds.
ideas.next: Record actual spend per tier against the design's cost envelope so the split can be tested.
ideas.origin: Orchestration design; Clinic testbed; Skills packages
ideas.flag: Tier was chosen by slice type and not validated against defect rates. Open owner decision: whether FixFlow slices adopt the rule that invariant-sensitive work goes to Opus.

ideas.name: Coordinator session that never implements
ideas.how: One main session on the plan branch owns the ship plan, results file, owner view, cross-lane contracts and the merge-ready call on every PR. It dispatches reviews and does not implement.
ideas.problem: With many sessions running at once, we need one place that owns the plan, shared results and merge calls without being buried in implementation or token cost.
ideas.stands: In use since 2026-11-13. The coordinator woke and resumed eight [M] lane sessions after the power loss. It lets 8 [M] lanes run at once; no measured effect on speed yet.
ideas.next: Keep the lane board current; dispatch binding reviews as lanes report ready.

ideas.name: Brief contract and CONTEXT block for every agent
ideas.how: A brief names goal, files, branch, hypotheses, settled facts and what done returns, in one paragraph. A fixed context block with rules is prepended verbatim; research agents each own one report file.
ideas.problem: Our agents re-derive project facts, start without a clear task, drift and overstate what was proved. We want every brief complete and every claim cited.
ideas.stands: In use on every brief in the clinic build and in this compile. No before/after of brief quality or rework [M: none]. It does not stop overstated reports: the clinic S11 gate found two record claims the evidence did not support.
ideas.next: Keep the block short and refresh it per run; reuse the three provenance tags.
ideas.flag: Delegation cost was not measured.

ideas.name: Typed output schemas, forced and validated
ideas.how: Each agent returns a fixed JSON Schema object with no extra fields. The workflow tool forces a validated call with retry. A blocked agent returns a named code and questions, not a guess.
ideas.problem: Free prose from agents is costly to read and invites unchecked claims. We want results the orchestrator and scripts can read by a fixed shape.
ideas.stands: In use: twelve schemas written in the orchestration design, referenced by all 11 [M] agent definitions, and forced output is how the harness already works. Strict validation has no silent-drop failure; BAML's lenient repair has a documented one [S].
ideas.next: Validate the schemas against the first real outputs.
ideas.origin: Orchestration design; BAML sweep; Skills packages
ideas.flag: The design's schemas were only designed; the forced-output route is in use. Merged record says in_use, so I kept it.

ideas.name: State kept in the repository, parents judge by diff
ideas.how: Each node keeps one task record with status, next action and evidence; plan and checkpoint files are projections of it. A parent reads the diff and record, and resumes from branch plus record.
ideas.problem: Work state lived in chat context and was lost on compaction or restart. We want a stopped session resumable and parents not trusting a child's own summary.
ideas.stands: In use in the clinic testbed: 37 [M] task folders. It makes resume possible but no real dead-session recovery was timed; resume tooling ran only on a synthetic pilot with no model calls.
ideas.next: Split current state from archive to avoid the 829-line board read; reconsider the single-owner rule.
ideas.flag: For FixFlow the harness review ruled to skip the task tree, because plan, PR body, results file and git already own each kind of state. In use in the clinic only.

ideas.name: Judgement-free discovery
ideas.how: First-stage agents return constants, lines, declared names, commands and exit codes, never a comparison, severity or verdict. Comparing values is left to the gate or the deep-dive analyst.
ideas.problem: We want to stop a cheap first-stage impression from becoming a top-priority finding by inertia, and keep what the orchestrator reads bounded by schema, not prose.
ideas.stands: Designed in the orchestration design and applied to every discovery brief; this compile also states the rule. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: After discovery, check that no map fact carries a severity or verdict.

ideas.name: Return contract: value or null, with coverage count
ideas.how: Every agent run resolves to a value or null. The script returns results, missing, not-started and coverage; the first gate re-runs or waives each gap in writing.
ideas.problem: A missing or crashed agent result must never be read by us as 'nothing found'.
ideas.stands: Designed as a rule at the first gate. Not yet tested as a rule; the discovery stage reported 16/16 [M] coverage.
ideas.next: Implement and test the contract in the discovery script.

ideas.name: Hypothesis table and challengeable settled facts
ideas.how: Hypotheses H1-H18 carry a status, basis and owning analyst. Settled rows go into the agents' args and are taken as given, but an analyst may challenge one with evidence.
ideas.problem: We want open questions tracked with an owner and what would settle each, while agents stop re-investigating resolved points, yet can still correct a wrong settled fact.
ideas.stands: The table is in use, updated at the first gate. The challenge channel is specified in design v3 only. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Update as owner answers arrive; pass the settled rows into args.
ideas.flag: Table in use, but the challenge channel is only specified, so I set maturity 3 rather than 5.

ideas.name: Write the gate record before the next workflow
ideas.how: The gate record, with verdicts and state, is written to the repo and confirmed on disk before the next workflow starts, so every analyst gets the settled facts.
ideas.problem: The deep-dive analysts started without the first gate record, because a shell quoting failure delayed it. We want the decision trail never lost.
ideas.stands: Adopted as a plan rule and stated as a lesson from both gates. No analyst's output depended on the missing file, because the substance was in the brief (qualitative).
ideas.next: Check the file exists before each dispatch; make the gate record a required step.

ideas.name: Plan @ sha in the PR body, with resume fetch and diff
ideas.how: The draft PR body starts with the plan's commit id. On resume, fetch origin, diff from that id to origin/main for the program docs, and re-read only changed sections.
ideas.problem: A session that restarts or compacts does not know which plan version it worked from, and can miss an amendment because git updates origin/main only on a fetch.
ideas.stands: Adopted by the review and lands in the plan's resume section; the fetch line is adopted in its narrow one-line form. Not yet tested. Pass test: each recorded sha equals the remote main head at that moment.
ideas.next: Add the fetch line to the plan's resume section; use it on the first phase draft PR.

ideas.name: Plan on a branch, tagged before lanes read it
ideas.how: Lanes read the primary checkout by absolute path or git show of the plan branch. The coordinator commits, pushes and tags every plan edit before telling a lane to read it.
ideas.problem: The plan, design notes and evidence live on a PR branch, not main, so a lane could read uncommitted text or miss the files.
ideas.stands: In use: tags plan-v9 and plan-v9.1 exist, and the results file cites the plan at v9.1. No measured effect yet.
ideas.next: Tag each later plan edit before briefing lanes.
ideas.flag: Open owner decision: whether to merge the docs-only plan and skills PRs to main.

ideas.name: Root as the only writer of shared documents
ideas.how: Only the root session edits shared documents. Slices write proposed changes in their own record, ideally exact old and new text the root applies by script. Registry files are append-only.
ideas.problem: Several sessions editing the same shared documents conflict and give us divergent truth. We want one source for each.
ideas.stands: In use in the clinic build, and it became a bottleneck itself: board state 221 KB [M], root edits caused failing checks at two slices, and docs were stale at wrap-up.
ideas.next: Replace with slice-written fragments and a generated board; add a test that fails when lock-step edits diverge.
ideas.flag: Open owner decision: whether slices may edit their own CLAUDE.md section, since FixFlow's policy differs.

ideas.name: Wave board as single current-state file
ideas.how: One file holds the current-state table (slice, wave, status, session, branch, tier, gate), dated gate sections, wrap-up, next actions and open questions. Root edits only.
ideas.problem: We want one authoritative place for what is built, in review and next, so any session can pick up the build.
ideas.stands: In use to wrap-up in the clinic: 829 lines, 219,111 bytes [M]. Append-only gate sections let earlier statements go stale, and nothing gave me a live progress view.
ideas.next: Split a short current-state file from an archive of gate sections.

ideas.name: Machine-appliable patches for shared docs
ideas.how: Children write their proposed shared-document edits as a patch that a script applies, so the root no longer rewrites each one.
ideas.problem: Only the root writes shared documents, and that makes the root a serial bottleneck we want to remove.
ideas.stands: Idea only, suggested in a sweep card's transfer note. Not built, not tested.
ideas.next: Prototype it with tests that catch documentation drift.

ideas.name: Scripts before agents
ideas.how: Models find things; scripts decide whether a finding is closed. The gate, audit, planner and parser are scripts that spend no tokens.
ideas.problem: In the testbed, ideas kept as prose lines in a brief or as model re-checks mostly failed. We want a check a script can make never left to a model.
ideas.stands: Standing rule of harness v2. Testbed record: 33 [M] practised dropped ideas worked and 38 [M] failed, mostly as prose. The scripts themselves have not run live.
ideas.next: Build the six no-token scripts in phase 3 order.

ideas.name: One fact, one command
ideas.how: A fact or rule is checked by one command before it becomes a rule, and recorded verified or contradicted. Each first-deploy step carries its command, expected result and a planted-failure run.
ideas.problem: An unchecked agent report once produced a false harness rule, and first-deploy steps can be ticked without proof. We want facts backed by evidence.
ideas.stands: Adopted from phase 1 of harness v2; costs one line in a brief. Not yet tested. Baseline count planned of environment facts in the root's 15 [M] lessons one command could check.
ideas.next: Run the default-mode write probe before that build; add the line to briefs.
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep; Harness v2 design
ideas.flag: The bottleneck compile calls it trial; the harness v2 design adopts it, so I used adopt. Five facts in the original bottleneck list turned out wrong.

ideas.name: Five-phase harness build order with dependencies
ideas.how: Phase 1 machine, 2 check, 3 gate and review scripts, 4 first use, 5 token budget. Phase 1 must precede 2, and 2 precede 4; the token baseline is saved in phase 1.
ideas.problem: We have 21 problems to fix and want to build them in the order the evidence supports.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2; phase 1 has started with read-only work and its findings exist. The order follows the record: machine first (24 [M] power-offs), review third, tokens last.
ideas.next: I take the phase 1 actions that need me.
ideas.flag: The records mark it in_use, but only phase 1 read-only work has run, so I set maturity 3. Owner decision D01 is attached.

ideas.name: Plan-check section in the orchestration document
ideas.how: Add the plan check as a new section after its second gate, lane arithmetic in its cost section and machine limits in constraints; no plan runs before it passes.
ideas.problem: The orchestration document has no dependency graph, footprint check or lane arithmetic, and states capacity facts as rules instead of measured limits.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 section 0. Nothing has changed in the document yet; the edit belongs to the ship plan's PR.
ideas.next: Write it when I say so; this decides whether and when.

ideas.name: Defer phase plan and recipes to Stage 3
ideas.how: Phase plan with one session per phase, Sonnet for well-specified fixes, Opus for outbox, lifecycle, ledger and migration code, and Opus reviewers refuting by default, all designed after the second gate.
ideas.problem: Phase design before verified facts would be built on guesses, so we wanted it designed only after the deep-dive.
ideas.stands: Deferred in the orchestration design on purpose. It was designed later as the ship plan, after the second gate.
ideas.next: Done: the ship plan took this over.
ideas.flag: Deferral was carried out: Stage 3 became the ship plan. The editor may want to show this as delivered rather than deferred.

splits.name: Parallel research agents each own one report
splits.how: A delegation template names question, scope, ownership, return form and stop condition. Research agents each own one report file; four [S] workers at most.
splits.problem: Delegated agents return unfocused or overlapping work. We want each worker with a clear question, its own file and a stop condition.
splits.stands: In use in the clinic testbed. Delegation cost was not measured; more workers is not evidence of better results. The root integrates and cross-checks, not by vote.
splits.next: Verify in the FixFlow tool setup whether subagents can be given a writable path.
splits.reason: The raw record clinicC-14 describes a distinct mechanism (owned-file parallel research with a four-worker ceiling and root cross-check) that the trimmed brief-contract entry no longer carries.

check.notes: Facts, statuses, maturities, bottleneck ids (all in register-ids.md) and work packages checked out; no invented numbers and no must-not-claim breaches. Main issue: nearly every entry overran the word limits (how 24, stands 32, problem 26, name 8), so those fields are given trimmed replacements, each verified by word count at or under the limit. Other changes: method#1 numbers 16/16 and 8 analysts now carry [M]; method#10 origin was not supported by the records (they cite a lesson from the two gates); method#6 now states the FixFlow ruling to skip the task tree; method#25 next reworded. Left as is: method#9 maturity 3 and method#23 maturity 3 (justified by the flags: challenge channel only specified, only phase 1 read-only work run), method#26 kept as deferred, and method#19 was fine. The split carries clinicC-14, which would otherwise vanish when the brief entry is shortened.

ideas.name: Phase opening, precedence and journal rules bundle
ideas.how: Small written rules: a document precedence line, explicit skill start, fetch before resume, pasted opening block, cause tags, a three-push CI stop and live PR body fetch.
ideas.problem: Our phase routine can skip steps or trust the wrong document. I want small written rules so each phase opens, runs and closes the same way.
ideas.stands: Proposed from the Dex Horthy sweep; not yet tested here. Umbrella over many single rules, eight adopt and the rest trial. FixFlow only; no bottleneck record names these skips.
ideas.next: Fold the adopt lines into ship plan section 0, then test each as its own record shows.
ideas.flag: Umbrella record; several of its rules appear as separate entries. Bottleneck ids chosen by the editor, the source lists none.

ideas.name: One-sentence source-precedence rule in ship plan
ideas.how: One sentence in ship plan section 0: owner correction beats plan on main, then Plan @ sha, then design note; CLAUDE.md and code win on stack facts.
ideas.problem: When the journal, the plan, a design note and CLAUDE.md disagree, a fresh agent has no stated order for which one wins.
ideas.stands: Proposed, not yet tested. It stays out of CLAUDE.md on purpose to keep that file short. The test plants two conflicts in the P1 cold-resume fact set.
ideas.next: Plant two conflicts; a fresh Sonnet agent passes if it reports the journal value and stricter rule with source.
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep; refuter split it by domain

ideas.name: Move 'Start here' pointer to ship plan section 0
ideas.how: One-row swap in CLAUDE.md's doc map so 'Start here' points to the ship plan section 0 instead of the July handoff.
ideas.problem: CLAUDE.md still sends a fresh session to the July handoff, so a cold agent starts from the wrong document.
ideas.stands: Proposed, not yet tested. Pushing context into every session was looked at and set aside; only the one-row edit stays.
ideas.next: Fresh Sonnet agent, neutral prompt: pass if it opens ship plan section 0 first in 3 of 3 runs [T].

ideas.name: Phase id comes from the owner, never inferred
ideas.how: One line in the orchestration skill's start step: the phase id comes from my opening message or skill arguments; if missing, the session asks.
ideas.problem: Concurrent phases are allowed and branch names do not name phases, so a session could pick the wrong phase.
ideas.stands: Proposed one-line edit, not yet tested. Pass is zero sessions naming a phase different from my opening message across the next 5 phase sessions [T].
ideas.next: Make the edit, then count mismatches over 5 phase sessions [T].
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep; skills as routine

ideas.name: Paste-to-open-a-phase block
ideas.how: A 5 to 8 line kickoff block in ship plan section 0, with separate first steps for code and operations phases, naming only steps that leave no trace.
ideas.problem: A new phase session can skip the steps that leave no trace, and nobody can tell afterwards.
ideas.stands: Trial, not yet tested. The evidence behind it is a single anecdote, so we test it on our own phases first.
ideas.next: Open the first 4 phases with the block [T]; a cheap extraction plus gh and git checks verify each named step.

ideas.name: Fetch live PR body before every body-file write
ideas.how: One clause in section 0: right before each body-file write, fetch the live PR body with gh and edit that text, never a rebuilt copy.
ideas.problem: Rewriting a PR body from a stale copy silently loses journal lines and ticked boxes.
ideas.stands: Proposed, not yet tested. Check at the close of P1, P2 and P3 by reading each PR body's edit history; pass is zero unexplained losses [T].
ideas.next: Add the clause, then read the edit history of 3 PRs [T].

ideas.name: 'Mirror these files' field in Sonnet briefs
ideas.how: Each Sonnet implementation brief names 1 to 3 existing files to mirror, which the explorer agent can fill in.
ideas.problem: Sonnet implementers write code that does not match the patterns already in the repo.
ideas.stands: Trial, not yet tested. The test is a blind paired probe rather than a PR count: 4 tasks, each with and without the line, 8 sessions [T].
ideas.next: Run the 8 sessions [T]; a blind Opus judge scores each diff. If it helps, the field becomes standard.
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep; refuter narrowed it

ideas.name: Two failed corrections, then a fresh session
ideas.how: After two failed corrections on one box, commit and push the work in progress, journal what failed, and resume in a new session; a failed subagent gets a fresh brief.
ideas.problem: Repeated corrections pile failed attempts into one session's context, and the box still does not close.
ideas.stands: Trial, not yet tested. It also keeps long windows short. Applies to the first 10 phase sessions from P0a [T].
ideas.next: Log each firing; record whether the fresh session closes the box with zero further corrections.
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep; restart rather than correct

ideas.name: Script the mechanical phase-close sequence
ideas.how: Script only the mechanical close steps (Plan @ line, owner view updated, verdict names the commit); a cheap extractor counts omitted steps.
ideas.problem: Phase-close steps are done from memory and some get omitted.
ideas.stands: Gated trial, not yet tested. Six mechanical close steps are counted after the first three phases [T]. A whole-phase driver was considered and set aside.
ideas.next: After P1 and the next two closes, count omitted steps among six [T].
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep; control flow in code

ideas.name: Save-rule, run provenance and skill retirement
ideas.how: Keep a workflow script only after a second use or a recorded failure; save it as run with args and brief; check each skill for retirement.
ideas.problem: Workflows are written per task and not saved, and without the script, args and reviewer brief a run cannot be re-run or audited.
ideas.stands: Adopted in narrowed form, not yet tested. Pass by P10 [T]: every saved script names at least 2 dated uses or a failure id.
ideas.next: Write the rules into the evidence rules; run retire checks at the phase closes the plan names.
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep; ad hoc practice since one commit
ideas.flag: Merged from three overlapping records, including skills and memory themes; calendar-based pruning was not adopted.

ideas.name: Shape block: signatures and call stack in the PR
ideas.how: Before the first code commit, the Opus implementer drafts public signatures and the call stack in the draft PR body. No tool is built.
ideas.problem: On phases that change control flow or add surfaces, design mistakes show up only after the code is written.
ideas.stands: Trial, narrowed, not yet tested. Candidates are the first 4 Opus-owned phases that change control flow [T].
ideas.next: Run it on the first 4 qualifying Opus phases [T]; see whether design mistakes surface earlier.
ideas.flag: Source lists W3 and W4; the editor chose B01 (design mistakes found late feed fix rounds).

ideas.name: Explicit effort on every reviewer and implementer launch
ideas.how: One line in section 0: launch the per-PR reviewer and implementers with an effort from the plan, through a Workflow agent call, never an inheriting path.
ideas.problem: An agent launched with no effort setting silently inherits the orchestrator's effort, so reviewers may run at the wrong level and cost more.
ideas.stands: Adopted in narrowed form, not yet tested. Check over the first 3 phase PRs that every launch shows an explicit effort [T].
ideas.next: Check whether the Agent tool or agent-definition settings accept an effort field.
ideas.flag: Listed under adopt, but both reviewers scored it trial.

ideas.name: Secrets passed by variable name in briefs
ideas.how: In four phase briefs, secrets are passed by variable name; records name the variable, never the value; agents never read a .env file.
ideas.problem: Phases that handle secrets, such as the backup dump and Cloudflare calls, could leak values into records, PR bodies or agent context.
ideas.stands: Proposed for four named phases only; not yet tested. At each close a local exact-value scan of diff, PR body and evidence must find 0 [T].
ideas.next: Accept the clause for the four phases, then run the scan at each close.

ideas.name: Knowledge-store lookup and record steps in the phase routine
ideas.how: About 260 words in ship plan section 0: look up before escalating, diff lookups at first commit and PR-ready, record before PR-ready, close at phase end.
ideas.problem: A store nobody consults helps nothing, and escalating a tier without a lookup pays the top tier for a repeat.
ideas.stands: Designed in the knowledge-store design: proposed text only, not applied, conditional on the pilot saying go. Compliance is self-reported, no hook. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Add the bullet to the ship plan after a pilot go (decision D10).
ideas.flag: The store never blocks a ship phase; the plan change is my decision.

ideas.name: Escalation ladder: Sonnet, then Opus, then Fable
ideas.how: The cheap model tries first; a caught failure gets one cheap retry, then Opus, then Fable. Solve once at the lowest capable tier and store the answer.
ideas.problem: A hard new problem is the point. The cheap model will fail some work outright, and the average gap between tiers hides that hard tail.
ideas.stands: Designed and modelled with guessed inputs. Middle values: 25.7 [G] cost per piece, 21.2% [G] wrong, against 29.9 [G] and 11.2% [G] for the strong model directly. Real cases: ladder not reached in 23 [M].
ideas.next: No fix agreed yet; the gate and ladder are shared by all three ways of working, so report them separately.
ideas.flag: Model figures are outputs of guessed inputs, not measurements. Real sessions skip rungs; two-thirds of recorded tokens ran on Opus or Fable [M].

ideas.name: Thought structures (tree, forest, graph) rejected
ideas.how: Branch and merge several reasoning paths in a tree, forest or graph, with a judge or vote, before answering.
ideas.problem: We hoped structured multi-branch reasoning would improve agent output and fixes over a single chain.

ideas.name: Add description text to output schemas
ideas.how: Test whether a schema property description reaches the model; if so, define each severity and verdict value once in a shared constant.
ideas.problem: Our output schemas carry no description, so P0 to P3 are defined nowhere and word limits live only in script comments the model never sees.
ideas.stands: Trial, not yet tested. Baseline to beat: 8 of 12 skeptic verdicts lowered a severity [M]; 4 of 12 survived [M]. BAML's own rendering evidence was judged not to transfer.
ideas.next: Run the one-agent probe; drop it if descriptions do not reach the subagent, otherwise edit the schemas.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, reframed by the refuter

ideas.name: One constants table for verdicts and buckets
ideas.how: A single table of about 15 lines [E] generates both the schema enums and the bucket mapping, with citation statuses folded in.
ideas.problem: A verdict value could be added to a schema without a matching bucket in the gate script, leaving results unclassified.
ideas.stands: Trial, unrefuted and not yet tested. It would make bucket totality structural: a verdict cannot exist without a bucket.
ideas.next: In the stub harness, add a verdict with no bucket and confirm the test fails.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, structural borrow from exhaustive matching

ideas.name: Fix stale analyst-cap lines in the design
ideas.how: Edit two lines of the orchestration design so they match the current version, which never truncates a P0 or P1.
ideas.problem: The design says findings are sliced to 12 in the script, while a later section says the script never cuts a P0 or P1, so two readings coexist.
ideas.stands: Idea, not yet applied. The BAML structural comparison found the two stale lines; the ruling names them for the design's next edit.
ideas.next: Apply at the next orchestration-design edit.

ideas.name: Give sweep assessors the design text and rules
ideas.how: The next sweep's assessment brief carries the output-schema text and the RT-01 to RT-07 rules, or we expect the refuter to catch overlap.
ideas.problem: Our assessment stage did not read the design documents, so ideas that were already program law were rated as new and only the refuter caught it.
ideas.stands: Idea, not yet tested. Observed cost: 8 of 24 adopt calls were already program law [M]. Fewer wasted assessments are expected, not measured.
ideas.next: Add the note at the next orchestration-design edit and use it in the next sweep brief.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, ruling on the assessment stage

ideas.name: Brief lint and dry-run flag in scripts
ideas.how: A pure in-script check runs before any agent call, and a dry-run flag returns assembled prompts and schemas instead of calling agents.
ideas.problem: I want hand-edits to a brief to be safe and reviewable before we spend: no dropped context block, no leaked tier word, no raw schema pasted into prose.
ideas.stands: Parked: refuted. The agent call already rejects bad schemas, the context block is added by one concatenation, and diffing the saved script gives the text diff. No brief edit has broken anything on record.
ideas.next: Nothing now; it returns if a hand-edit of a brief ever breaks a run.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, after its offline build and parse companions

ideas.name: Categorical rubric instead of numeric likelihood
ideas.how: Replace model-asserted 0 to 1 likelihood numbers in schemas with a defined enum such as slow, medium or fast.
ideas.problem: Fields like likelihood for this fleet carry a number the model asserts and that may mean little.
ideas.stands: Parked: refuted on committed data. 53 values fell over 17 distinct ones, and the top three cover 15 of 53 (28%) [M]. The trial threshold already fails and no script decision reads the number.
ideas.next: Nothing now; it returns if a script decision starts reading the number.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, after a community talk on categorical grading

ideas.name: Evidence fields before verdict in every contract
ideas.how: In each return contract, put explanation and evidence properties before verdict and severity, all required.
ideas.problem: Format-restricted output may lower accuracy if the answer key comes before the reasoning, so we wanted reasoning first.
ideas.stands: Parked: refuted. Our agents already work through a full tool loop before one final structured-output call, and a reasoning-style first field is the known refusal trigger. Supporting evidence came from 2024 non-reasoning models [S].
ideas.next: Nothing now; it returns if agents start answering without a tool loop.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, after a 2024 paper and practitioner threads

ideas.name: Report directive text found in fetched pages
ideas.how: A research-contract rule and field so a reader reports instructions found inside a source instead of acting on them.
ideas.problem: BAML's docs open with an instruction addressed to an AI reader, which is an instruction inside fetched content; we want that noticed and reported.
ideas.stands: Parked: refuted. Subagents already treat tool output as data and handled the notice correctly. We have no injection incident on record.
ideas.next: Nothing now; it returns if a fetched page ever steers an agent.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, observed in its docs

ideas.name: Short stable handles instead of hashes
ideas.how: Agents use short labels such as H-01 and S-07b; long hashes are checked by git in code, so a mis-echo fails loudly.
ideas.problem: Agents echoing long ids or commit hashes can mis-aggregate them silently.
ideas.stands: In use in the harness. An outside measurement on id aggregation had a small sample, two runs per arm [S], so we rely on the practice, not the figure.
ideas.next: Keep using it.
ideas.origin: Harness practice, confirmed by BAML sweep

ideas.name: Same-tier retry; only infrastructure changes tier
ideas.how: Structured-output retries stay inside the same subagent; scripts retry at the tail with the same task and model.
ideas.problem: Silently escalating to a stronger model after a schema failure hides cost and masks a defect in the brief.
ideas.stands: In use by construction: retries already stay on the same model, so the rule holds today. It is not yet written into the design.
ideas.next: Optionally write the rule into the orchestration design.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, after Pydantic AI and DSPy

ideas.name: Escape-hatch values in every schema
ideas.how: Schemas carry values such as UNVERIFIABLE, untestable, UNCLEAR, unknown or empty, and an unknown is recorded as unknown.
ideas.problem: A forced schema can make a model invent a conforming answer when the input does not fit.
ideas.stands: In use: already in the output schemas and a research rule. Agents wrote 'undated' honestly in this run.
ideas.next: Audit the contracts for required fields that have no unknown path.
ideas.origin: Practitioner advice, confirmed by BAML sweep

ideas.name: Briefs in git; contract shapes frozen
ideas.how: Briefs live in git, runs cite commit hashes, and the fixed return contracts keep their shape so only prose is edited.
ideas.problem: We want prompt changes to be reviewable and every result traceable to a version.
ideas.stands: In use and confirmed in the BAML sweep.
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: Invoke the orchestration skill at phase start
ideas.how: A zero-cost habit: call the orchestration skill at phase start and prompt the close step explicitly, with no new phase-start or phase-close skills.
ideas.problem: A skill may not load from its description alone, so a phase's instructions might never be read.
ideas.stands: Trial, not yet tested. It measures whether auto-loading works by checking 3 plain-prompt sessions [T] for a skill call before the first brief or commit.
ideas.next: Open 3 sessions with a plain prompt and count those where the skill loaded first.

ideas.name: Advisory CI check on PR bodies
ideas.how: A separate dependency-free workflow checks the PR body for a plan line that resolves, a task list, a journal heading and a reviewer verdict naming the head commit.
ideas.problem: Whether the phase routine ran is self-reported, so a missing plan line, journal heading or reviewer verdict raises no alarm.
ideas.stands: Trial, not yet tested. Top trial 3 of the Horthy sweep; about 40 lines of YAML [E]; advisory on drafts, failing when ready.
ideas.next: Build in P1-ci; over the first 5 code-phase PRs [T] count real catches against false alarms.

ideas.name: Script-generated document provenance
ideas.how: A script writes metadata frontmatter (git commit and branch) and citations use commit-pinned permalinks; only that script is pre-approved.
ideas.problem: Documents may carry placeholder or unverifiable provenance, so a reader cannot tell which commit a claim was written against.
ideas.stands: Deferred: it went over the sweep's cap, so no refuter has ruled on it and no measurement is defined.
ideas.next: Decide whether to give it a refuter pass; that would settle trial or park.

ideas.name: Gate-script hygiene: tagged results and clean inputs
ideas.how: Tag each agent result as null, error or value; build skeptic inputs with a pure function; compare self-listed reads with the transcript; rename a reasoning field to explanation.
ideas.problem: A schema failure could look like a usage-limit null, a skeptic could get contaminated inputs, and a script could trust an agent's own list of reads.
ideas.stands: Trial, unrefuted and not yet tested. Refuters narrowed all four to FixFlow only: no dead reviewer read as clean and no contaminated reviewer is on the testbed record.
ideas.next: Probe what the agent call returns on schema exhaustion, then a stubbed run with one schema error and two nulls.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, borrows from its typed failures
ideas.flag: Open precondition: what the agent call returns on schema exhaustion is unknown. Owner decides whether these borrows earn an Opus refuter.

ideas.name: Infrastructure failures kept apart from content failures
ideas.how: A null is never a result; the breaker reads fresh nulls as a suspected session limit; zero tests run is never green; coverage must read 16/16 or carry a waiver.
ideas.problem: A flaky provider or a run that tested nothing must not read as a pass, or as a bad brief.
ideas.stands: In use as program law in the orchestration design, and confirmed in the BAML sweep. BAML's own optimiser admits it cannot do this.
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: Verify owner-stated facts inline
ideas.how: The orchestrator checks a checkable fact with a grep or command; the journal records verified or contradicted, and contradictions go back to the owner without spawning a research agent.
ideas.problem: A mid-phase correction from me about code or environment can be wrong, and agents may act on it unchecked or silently override it.
ideas.stands: Trial over phases P1 to P3, not yet tested. The test target is that 100% [T] of checkable-fact entries carry a verified or contradicted line.
ideas.next: Classify every correction during P1 to P3 and count entries with the line.

ideas.name: Models give verdicts; code computes counts and scores
ideas.how: Models give yes/no or enum verdicts; code computes scores and coverage, logs dropped counts and applies no silent caps; each phase has a cheap human-checkable proof.
ideas.problem: Holistic model scores are unreliable and I cannot read all the logic; a script that filters or asks a model to count can lose items without trace.
ideas.stands: In use as program law: enum verdicts roll up into buckets by script, and the findings backlog means nothing is silently dropped. Confirmed in the BAML sweep.
ideas.next: Optionally add a rule to report received and kept counts for any filtering step.
ideas.origin: Orchestration design, Dex Horthy sweep and BAML sweep

ideas.name: Compare structures on the problem case, not pieces

ideas.problem: Fitting BAML's pieces under our structure could hide where its whole structure serves the work better or worse.
ideas.stands: Done 2026-11-04. Our structure serves the case better or equally on all ten dimensions (judged). It corrected one card, found two stale design lines and showed what is copyable in 10 to 40 lines [E] of plain JS.
ideas.next: Decide whether the five borrows earn a refuter pass; none has had one.
ideas.origin: Owner question during the BAML sweep
ideas.flag: No Opus refuter ran, so its borrows are unrefuted; the ten-dimension result is a judgement, not a measurement.

ideas.name: Prompt optimiser (GEPA) over a test corpus
ideas.how: BAML's beta optimiser rewrites prompt text and type descriptions, scored by the project's tests.
ideas.problem: We tune our briefs by hand and would like a way to improve them against a score.
ideas.stands: Parked as premature: it needs a scored test corpus we lack, an install and API keys. Not tested. Its one useful rule is already kept as infrastructure failures apart from content failures.
ideas.next: Revisit once we hold a scored corpus of brief runs.

ideas.name: Planner that sizes lanes just below the knee
ideas.how: Before work starts, compute lanes from the four limits (check, review, merge, token window) and memory; knee is the lowest limit divided by one lane's rate. Run about 0.8 of it.
ideas.problem: We chose how many parallel sessions to run by feel. Past the lowest limit, extra lanes only add queues, tokens and collisions, not speed.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2; plan accepted 11 Nov, nothing installed. In the model, lanes past the knee only wait [I]. The testbed had about three lanes worth running [M] but ran six to nine [M].
ideas.next: Measure check and review times in phases 2-3; the planner then recomputes lane counts for each plan.

ideas.name: Plan check with footprints and collision graphs
ideas.how: Each slice declares files written, interfaces read, prerequisites and shared things. We build a needs graph and a collides graph, refuse two writers of one file, and feed back real touches.
ideas.problem: We ran slices in parallel with nothing checking for collisions. The first checks on merged main failed for the first two slices because of hand edits to shared documents.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2; the spec is complete (8 steps) but untested. The testbed never laid slices out with footprints, so no real plan can be replayed; the sample plan is made up.
ideas.next: Add the plan-check section to the orchestration document when I say so; run the touch-list test on ten recorded cases.

ideas.name: Scheduler that releases two sessions at a time
ideas.how: Turn the wave plan into running sessions, release at most two at a time, keep waiting slices parked outside any session, and bring sessions back after a stop.
ideas.problem: After a stop every session was released at once and waited together, holding context and burning tokens. One check waited 2,030 s [M].
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2, with the resume list; I answered D06 (released two at a time). In the record, two at a time got further: 18 of 48 agents finished in one window [M], a lean run 30 of 31 [M].
ideas.next: Build it with the resume list in phase 1; a waiting lane then burns nothing in the model [I].
ideas.origin: Harness v2 design; answer to the 9 November mass release
ideas.flag: The source also lists B03; it is the owner-away id in the register and fits poorly, so it was left out.

ideas.name: Lane sessions: one phase, own worktree, run together
ideas.how: Each lane is one Claude Code session (Opus lead) with its own git worktree from origin/main. It runs exactly one phase, ends in a draft PR titled with the phase id.
ideas.problem: Version 8 ran one phase at a time, so twelve days passed with nothing built while code phases waited behind my first phase.
ideas.stands: In use in FixFlow: eight lane sessions started 2026-11-13 [M], and PRs #187-#192 opened that day [M]. RAM, not CPU, sets the ceiling [M]; the wave plan has four waves [E].
ideas.next: Start wave B as soon as a wave-A PR is review-passed.

ideas.name: Build ahead by classifying each Entry clause
ideas.how: Each Entry clause is classed code, value, deploy or evidence. Only code can delay a build, and then the lane stacks on the other phase's reviewed branch tip.
ideas.problem: Entry lines mixed code, value, deploy and evidence conditions, so every code phase waited for my work even when it could be built.
ideas.stands: In use in FixFlow: four phases built ahead on 2026-11-13 (P7a, P6a, P9-0a, P12a) [M]; none merged yet. It could free the queue behind P0a for 15+ code phases [E].
ideas.next: Rebase stacks with git rebase --onto origin/main after each squash merge.

ideas.name: Waves of parallel slices from the plan
ideas.how: Waves come from the plan's dependency graph: slice-owned apps and migration numbers, frozen shared vocabulary, own database and port per branch, root holding merge order.
ideas.problem: We need slices to run in parallel safely, never by guess, in an order that empties the queue, without migration or port collisions and within RAM.
ideas.stands: In use: clinic testbed waves 0-5 (S00 on 3 Nov, waves 3-4 done 4 Nov, wrap-up 10 Nov) [M], no serial comparison. FixFlow wave A started eight sessions on 2026-11-13 [M].
ideas.next: Start wave B when a wave-A PR is review-passed; keep a database per branch and frozen contracts before fan-out.
ideas.flag: Merged from a clinic testbed record and a FixFlow ship plan record; no wave shortens my own chain of phases.

ideas.name: File ownership per lane with named shared files
ideas.how: A table gives each lane the folders it owns. Two lanes never edit the same file in a wave, except listed shared files, each with a conflict rule.
ideas.problem: Parallel lanes editing the same files in the same wave cause rebase conflicts and lost work.
ideas.stands: In use: in force for wave A; review findings added shared files such as CLAUDE.md, config.py, conftest.py and specs.py. No conflict count recorded yet.
ideas.next: Watch the first rebases of P6a after P1.

ideas.name: Cross-lane contracts fixed in advance
ideas.how: The plan fixes shared values now: the origin header, a verdict fixture file, a sorted telemetry events array, the queue discard and drain manifest events, and sampler event names.
ideas.problem: Lanes that depend on each other's outputs would otherwise wait on each other or guess names, headers and fixtures.
ideas.stands: In use: the contract values are fixed in the ship plan, section 7.3. No lane has yet reported a wait or a mismatch; not yet tested.
ideas.next: P6a creates the shared contract files; P5a and P6b-2 then consume them.
ideas.flag: The source names no register bottleneck; lanes waiting on each other fits none exactly.

ideas.name: Merge-hold list for built-ahead PRs
ideas.how: A table names PRs that are built and reviewed but stay draft and unmerged until a stated point, such as P4c done or every phone on v2.
ideas.problem: Merge is not deploy only until P4c deploys main HEAD, so building ahead could ship half-finished mobile or accounting work into the fleet APK or the drain window.
ideas.stands: Designed in the ship plan; rule accepted, held PRs not yet reviewed, so not yet tested.
ideas.next: Check each PR against the list before merging; this keeps build-ahead safe.
ideas.flag: Placed with merge rules in WP3; WP4 is the alternative.

ideas.name: No undeclared splits of a one-PR phase
ideas.how: A phase that version 8 made one PR stays one PR. P3a-2 is not started early; the stub and heartbeat stay inside P3a; P6a keeps its web half in its own PR.
ideas.problem: Splitting a one-PR phase across lanes would touch the runbook and ci.yml ahead of their owners and make cherry-picks onto the release branch conflict.
ideas.stands: Adopted in the ship plan; P3a-2 was never launched. Not yet tested beyond that.
ideas.next: State any split in the plan before a lane starts one.

ideas.name: Migration-numbering rule across parallel slices
ideas.how: One slice session at a time writes migrations for a given app; a second branch regenerates after the merge; a graph test enforces a single head.
ideas.problem: Parallel slices pick the same database migration number and collide.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed; it serialises per app. No collision count was recorded, so we have no measured effect.
ideas.next: One writer per wave; keep the single-head test. FixFlow's next free slot is 0047.
ideas.flag: The source lists B01 and B04, which fit poorly; the register id PR-CONFLICTS was used instead.

ideas.name: Flow limits for loops and work in progress
ideas.how: One open PR per loop, automated actors limited to safe directories with batch caps, and wider frequency or batch only after output has been reviewed clean.
ideas.problem: Automated loops can flood review with parallel PRs, overrun review capacity, or touch unsafe areas.
ideas.stands: From the Dex Horthy sweep. The assessment found our work-in-progress bounds already exist in the ship plan and orchestration rules, and we run no scheduled agent loops. No measurement defined.
ideas.next: Keep the existing bounds; apply the one-PR-per-loop rule if we add scheduled loops.
ideas.flag: One listing was deferred with no refuter verdict; the later assessment says the bounds already exist, so in_use was kept. The loop-specific rule is not running.

ideas.name: Knowledge-store phases yield to ship phases
ideas.how: A store session starts only when no ship phase waits on Opus, or when I spend spare quota. A store phase that hits a usage limit yields.
ideas.problem: Knowledge-store sessions would compete with ship phases for Opus usage and for my attention, and I want no store phase to delay shipping.
ideas.stands: Designed in the knowledge-store design, as a rule for every store phase; not yet tested. KS-6a and KS-6b share the one Docker-gate slot.
ideas.next: Apply it at each store phase start.

ideas.name: Pipelined verification as each analyst finishes
ideas.how: Citation checks start as each analyst finishes, not after all are done; the fleet drain analyst runs pipelined after the first analyst group.
ideas.problem: Waiting for all analysts before checking leaves wall-clock time idle, and we want the same checks to finish sooner.
ideas.stands: Designed in the orchestration design as part of the second workflow script's shape; not yet tested.
ideas.next: Implement it in the second workflow script and time it.

ideas.name: PR title as resume key, with a lane board
ideas.how: A lane keeps its session's branch and names it in the PR body; the PR title starts with the phase id. A lane board maps phase, session, branch, PR and state.
ideas.problem: After a stop or crash we could not tell which session, branch and PR belong to which phase when branch names differ from the plan.
ideas.stands: In use: the lane board had 10 rows on 2026-11-13 [M], and all eight lanes resumed from their worktrees after the power loss [M].
ideas.next: Keep the board updated as lanes finish.

ideas.name: Lanes report; the coordinator writes program files
ideas.how: A lane never edits the program folder or the owner view. Its closing message carries its deploy-train row and any plan defect; the coordinator records both.
ideas.problem: Many lanes editing the program documents at once would collide and bury my single view of progress.
ideas.stands: Adopted in the ship plan and in force for all lanes; it replaces the earlier rule that a lane amends the file in its own PR. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Check that the first lane closing message carries the deploy-train row.
ideas.flag: Marked adopt in the record although the rule is in force for all lanes; kept as given.

ideas.name: Gates in their own phase, long agents first
ideas.how: The long test and build gates issue first in a separate Gates phase that reader slices do not wait on; their write set is disjoint from what readers read.
ideas.problem: Test and build gates run 25 to 40 minutes [S] and must not block or collide with the reader agents.
ideas.stands: Designed in the orchestration design as part of the first workflow's contract; not yet tested.
ideas.next: Time the gates alongside readers in that first workflow.

ideas.name: Governor that slows lanes to last the window
ideas.how: Governor share is what the window can still carry divided by what lanes would burn, using measured tokens per lane-hour by model, so lanes slow instead of all stopping.
ideas.problem: At the five-hour window's limit every lane stops at once; we had 14 limit episodes in October [M].
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2, to be built in phase 5 after the baseline. One window covered about 3.4 million subagent tokens [M]; subagents caused 91 of 104 limit errors [M].
ideas.next: Set the written budget from the one measured window (D07), then rerun it on November's tally.
ideas.flag: Owner decision D07, the token budget per window, is open.

ideas.name: Bounded session tree: depth three, fan-out three
ideas.how: Root session holds the board; slice leads, child sessions and subagents sit below; at most three running children per node; each node owns one file set, worktree and branch.
ideas.problem: A large build needs structure so many sessions run without losing work, colliding on files, flooding the reviewing parent or exhausting the shared session limit.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed: 12 slices and about 20 follow-up branches merged in 8 days [M]. No comparison with another structure; the root became a serial gate and the board grew to 219,111 bytes [M].
ideas.next: Move the board off one 219 KB file; reuse file-disjoint ownership and merge-upward order for FixFlow lanes.
ideas.origin: Clinic testbed; adapted from FixFlow's tier guide
ideas.flag: The three-children limit is asserted, not measured; one shared session limit incident occurred.

ideas.name: Per-checkout isolation of worktree, port and database
ideas.how: Each checkout gets its own worktree, branch, compose project, database port and database names suffixed with a hash of its path; a second check of one checkout is refused.
ideas.problem: Parallel sessions collided on branches, ports and test databases; two runs of one checkout dropped each other's test database.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed: it supported 432 commits and 65 merges in eight working days [M]. The recorded failure was 115 errors [M]; 19 worktrees exist [M]; costs a database container per checkout.
ideas.next: Consider one shared database container with per-checkout databases; add a dry-run reaper for finished checkouts.

ideas.name: READY signal: gh pr ready plus coordinator watcher
ideas.how: A lane that reports READY also marks its PR ready for review; a coordinator watcher polls that flag and wakes the binding review.
ideas.problem: The coordinator needs to know a lane is done without polling sessions or being messaged mid-turn, since messages arrive only when a lane's turn ends.
ideas.stands: Designed as a rule in the ship plan; no READY has been recorded yet, so not yet tested.
ideas.next: Run the watcher when the first lane finishes.

condensed.notes: All 21 keys covered. Some numbers carry tags from the source records. A few figures lacked a tag in the source (the 25 to 40 minute gates) and were tagged [S] as outside settings; the editor should confirm.
