splits.name: Write gate against duplicate records
splits.how: Before a record is saved, the store checks for duplicates, refuses self-matches and looks for an already-existing entry.
splits.problem: We want lookups to return the right earlier diagnosis, never a plausible wrong one, so what enters the store must be clean.
splits.stands: Designed in phase KS-2; not yet tested. Sonnet implements and Opus reviews the scrubber as a security boundary.
splits.next: Build it in KS-2 after KS-1.
splits.reason: The write gate (duplicate check, self-match refusal, missed-existing check) is a distinct write-time mechanism from the lookup pipeline and vanished from the merged entry.

check.notes: All numbers and tags otherwise match the records. Checked and left alone. check#26: "three" tests broken is untagged in source; [M] kept as a counted event. measure#37: the merged record's potential field says all-good cost 0.75 while the cited table line and results say 0.82; the entry uses 0.82, matching the cited line. memory#36: the merged record also lists project-wide mutable pointers and private memory as authority (rejected together); the entry omits them, which is acceptable as the same rejection. retrieval#29/#30 bottleneck assignment (LIB-KS-VALUE, none) is reasonable as the source ids B04/B13 do not fit. Word counts were checked with tags counted as words. The split for retrieval#35 may be dropped if another chunk already carries the write gate.

ideas.name: ast-grep syntax-tree reader for code probes
ideas.how: After the pilot, a pinned ast-grep tool anchors checks to code symbols and ignores comments, tested with refactor mutants; unparseable code gives inconclusive.
ideas.problem: Whole-file hashes flag too much, and text checks over code are fooled by moved guards, comments quoting bad code and renames. We want checks that read code structure.
ideas.stands: Designed in the knowledge-store design; not yet tested. It fixes one of four ways a code check can be fooled [M, per source]. A 360 Total Security smoke test is pending.
ideas.next: I rule on it when the pilot gives a go. If I decline, we use no code reader at all.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design, owner critique (syntax trees); ast-grep
ideas.flag: One raw record said deferred, the other designed; kept designed. Both agree it is built only at the second pilot stage.

ideas.name: Real-case walkthroughs through ten design steps
ideas.how: Sonnet agents find real cases in the record; Opus agents walk each through the ten library steps and mark works, strains or breaks.
ideas.problem: We wanted to see where the library design breaks on real problems, not only on thought experiments or one simulated pathway.
ideas.stands: Measured on a chosen sample: 59 cases [M], 590 step judgments [M], 69 limitations found [M]. Most breaks: check 38, use 31, afterlife 29, match 26 [M]. Shows where, never how often.
ideas.next: Agree the limitation list, then weigh each against the guessed conditions before any build.
ideas.origin: Library review, after the owner asked for a diversity of pathways
ideas.flag: Five bottleneck ids were listed in the record; trimmed to four (LIB-S2 left out).

ideas.name: Hand-written code lexer for span anchoring
ideas.how: A zero-dependency lexer for Python, TS/JS, JSON and YAML, with span anchors, planned to let code checks skip comments and strings.
ideas.problem: We wanted code checks that ignore comments and strings and anchor to function spans without installing a heavy parser.
ideas.stands: Parked: withdrawn after the owner critique, because nobody had evaluated it and its spec left out JSX. Never built. Replaced by the ast-grep reader.
ideas.next: None; the ast-grep reader (decision D5b) replaces it. It could return only if a lane evaluates it.
ideas.flag: Merged record says superseded, one raw record says rejected; kept superseded as the source says it was replaced by D5b.

ideas.name: Break-even sweep: how much work must repeat
ideas.how: With reach and entry quality at their good ends, sweep the share of work that could hold an entry and find where library cost crosses the ladder's.
ideas.problem: We want to know what share of our work needs a usable library entry for the library to pay for itself.
ideas.stands: Library model output from guessed inputs [G]: cost crosses at about half the work (middle running cost) or about a fifth (low running cost) [G]. Middle value is a quarter [G]. Not on the page.
ideas.next: Decide whether to add a comes-back slider or break-even chart to the library page.
ideas.flag: Status is measured but figures are model outputs from guessed inputs [G], not field measurements; treat as illustrative.

ideas.name: guarded_refs advisory (allowed-site lists)
ideas.how: An optional author-named list of allowed sites per entry; the diff lookup reads it as a hint that never changes a verdict.
ideas.problem: We can detect a new reference to a guarded identifier, but cannot tell whether an existing check covers it.
ideas.stands: Deferred, default off; to be built at the second pilot stage or later. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Measure its false-alarm rate from git history first; I rule on it at the checkpoint (D22).

ideas.name: Oracle-match trial
ideas.how: On held-out past problems, run Sonnet with and without the best-matching earlier solution and score both by tests.
ideas.problem: We want to learn whether a cheap model given the best earlier solution reaches strong-model quality, before we build the library.
ideas.stands: Proposed, not run. It would test the matching and use steps with no build.
ideas.next: Pick held-out past problems and their best matches, then score by tests. It could settle whether the library is worth building.

ideas.name: Automatic footprint capture for knowledge-store entries
ideas.how: Three captures: what the agent read (hooks or transcript), what the check executed (coverage), and a fixed environment probe.
ideas.problem: Authors may forget to list what an entry depends on, so we want the list captured, not guessed.
ideas.stands: Deferred. The pilot uses only the fix diff, check inputs, environment probes and transcript reads; coverage capture waits (D5) and needs two small dev dependencies. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: I decide on the two dependencies (D5). Coverage capture could then tighten when entries go stale.

ideas.name: Similar-problem coverage labelling
ideas.how: Label about 200 recorded exploration runs by whether an earlier session had already answered the same or a similar question.
ideas.problem: Nobody has measured how much of our work an earlier session already answered, and that sets the ceiling for any library.
ideas.stands: Proposed, not run; needs no build. It decides the ceiling: halving exploration needs about 3 in 4 steps to repeat [E].
ideas.next: Label the runs. The result tells us whether a library can pay at all.
ideas.origin: Library review, refuters' cheapest decisive test

ideas.name: Declarative gate runner with control pairs
ideas.how: Probes read parsed data only. Each needs a control pair (present on a broken commit, absent on a fixed one), mutants, preconditions and a three-way verdict.
ideas.problem: A stored 'this fix applies' claim can be wrong; a probe may match a moved guard or a comment and pass vacuously, and agents copy near matches.
ideas.stands: Designed for phase 3 of the knowledge-store plan; not built or tested. Refuters refuted the first polarity rule [M]. Target: zero acted-on false leads [T].
ideas.next: Build the probes over parsed data first (eas.json, app.json, lockfiles), after the first phase. This guards the config-trap class.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design, after Getafix and SapFix
ideas.flag: Could sit in WP6 (memory) or WP7; chosen by its problem, wrong matches acted on as leads. Enabling scripted checks needs my approval.

ideas.name: Docker test-id gate and Jest/Vitest phase signal
ideas.how: A sandbox with locked dependencies, no network and a per-run database runs named tests; a hook failure in Jest or Vitest is never read as a test failure.
ideas.problem: Entries whose cause lives in code behaviour need a runnable check, and a setup failure must not look like a failing test.
ideas.stands: Designed; not yet tested. Conditional on a pilot go and uses the single Docker gate slot. It would give runnable checks for four examples but largely duplicates CI for several.
ideas.next: I start Docker Desktop at this phase's entry; free-form scripted checks stay off (D18).

ideas.name: Write-through record at solve time, Opus-confirmed
ideas.how: The solving session fills a fixed schema before the PR is ready, only for hard problems; the PR's Opus reviewer tries to refute it and approves.
ideas.problem: Entries written later from a transcript lose the diagnosis path or fill the store with junk, and a self-confirmed entry could be wrong.
ideas.stands: Designed; not yet tested. Estimated cost about 10 to 20 minutes of the solving session per record [E]. It is policy plus review, not a technical lock.
ideas.next: Seed the store, then run the pilot to see whether records get written and hold up.

ideas.name: Trained tree ensemble over recorded episodes
ideas.how: Train a tree ensemble on a few hundred labelled episodes from session records to predict which route a task takes through the design.
ideas.problem: We want predicted routes from our own recorded sessions instead of from guessed rates.
ideas.stands: An idea for a later phase; not started. Members must make different mistakes and need a sampled audit for branches they cannot see. The tool-error scan already exists.
ideas.next: Label a few hundred episodes, then decide whether to build it.
ideas.origin: Library review, the owner's ensemble idea

ideas.name: Do-not-apply entries with a proposed-change check
ideas.how: A check run on a proposed change has four outcomes: applies, protection changed, protection disabled, or inconclusive. The prohibition text is never withheld.
ideas.problem: A rule like 'a locked account must refuse even a correct PIN' needs a check that fires before the forbidden change lands.
ideas.stands: Designed; not yet tested. 3 of 3 past edits to the protective files were legitimate [M], so stops go to the reviewer, never to an automatic verdict.
ideas.next: Write fixtures for an inverted test, a deleted file and a skipped test. This protects the deliberate PIN-lock rule.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design, completeness critic and owner critique

ideas.name: Teardown checklist for a stop verdict
ideas.how: One code PR and one docs PR remove the skill, hooks, CI workflow, ignores and tool, revert the CLAUDE.md edit and leave the journal read-only.
ideas.problem: If we stop an experiment, we want nothing left lingering in the repo.
ideas.stands: Designed; not yet tested. It makes the knowledge-store experiment safely reversible.
ideas.next: Write the checklist into the teardown PR if a stop or retire verdict comes; I merge two PRs.

ideas.name: ks close: anchor, rescan at main, four counts
ideas.how: At phase close one command re-points checks to the merged commit, re-runs probes at origin/main, labels results 'fix not on main' or 'regression', and prints four counts.
ideas.problem: A fix can be pushed after its PR merged and stay stranded off main, and entries drift after refactors. One fix sat stranded for 16 days.
ideas.stands: Designed for phase 3b; not built or tested. Its test must fire at every main tip across the stranded span [T].
ideas.next: Build it in the first knowledge-store phases. It catches stranded fixes without extra effort from me.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design, refuter and critic findings

ideas.name: Blind pilot against two incumbents, with a stop point
ideas.how: A non-seeding session writes 20+ blind queries and 40+ hard negatives; cheap agents run lookups against grep over CLAUDE.md and git log. Verdict: go, go-minimal or stop.
ideas.problem: Nobody has measured whether a lookup beats grep over existing prose for one developer in a young repo, and we should know before spending about five build sessions.
ideas.stands: Designed; not yet tested. Go needs recall at shown of 60 percent or more [T] and zero acted-on false positives [T]. 0 in 40 probes bounds the rate at 7.5% [S].
ideas.next: Run the free git-history audit first (D1); freeze thresholds, then pilot. It decides the build before about ten sessions are spent.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design, judge panel and Graph test lessons
ideas.flag: Thresholds are my proposals; the pilot cannot tune thresholds it is graded on.

ideas.name: Prospective checkpoint on real encounters
ideas.how: After 20 encounters or 8 weeks, read the logged views: verified hits, acted false positives, escalations without lookup, and lookup cost against solve cost.
ideas.problem: A pilot on replayed history says little about new encounters or how much solve cost the store really avoids.
ideas.stands: Designed; not yet tested. Checkpoint at 20 encounters or 8 weeks [S], whichever comes first. It gives the first measurement of the solve cost avoided.
ideas.next: Starts when the first real encounter is logged; I give the verdict and rule on two deferred options (D21, D22).

ideas.name: Retrieval thresholds frozen before the pilot
ideas.how: A leave-one-out replay over seeded entries and hard negatives sets lead 0.5, candidate 0.3 and margin 0.2 [S] as owner-approved settings; the pilot cannot change them.
ideas.problem: If the pilot can tune its own cut-offs it grades itself, and no literature gives thresholds for this kind of store.
ideas.stands: Designed; not yet tested. Values are my inferred parameters, not design facts. Small samples bound only coarsely: 0 failures in 40 means 7.5 percent or less [S].
ideas.next: Run the replay at the end of the seeding phase; I accept the thresholds (D8). It makes the pilot a fair test.
ideas.flag: Raw record cited a raw id that collides with the documents-drift id; not mapped.

ideas.name: Diff-handle selectivity gate and false-fire ceiling
ideas.how: Handles are author-named; each is replayed over about 150 commits [S] when written and refused above about 5 percent [S]. Go needs warnings on at most 1 commit in 10 [T].
ideas.problem: Common identifiers would make the warning fire so often that nobody reads it.
ideas.stands: Designed, built in an early phase. Under the first rule 48.7 percent of commits warned [M]; useState 31 percent, client_id 22 to 28 percent, job 58 to 66 percent [M].
ideas.next: Print each handle's historic fire count when recording. This keeps a go verdict for the diff warning meaningful.
ideas.flag: The ceiling is my parameter (D8).

ideas.name: Edit-time warning hook
ideas.how: A fail-open hook on Edit and Write runs git diff on the edited path through the same lookup and shows one short, de-duplicated warning. It never blocks.
ideas.problem: We want a forbidden edit to warn at edit time, not only in review.
ideas.stands: Deferred, default off; not yet tested. Its known blind spot is edits made through Bash or PowerShell.
ideas.next: I rule on it at the checkpoint (D21), if the warning rate is within the ceiling.

ideas.name: Measure compliance: escalations made without a lookup
ideas.how: The closing message reports escalations made without a lookup; ks close reports whether a diff lookup exists at the final head; reviewers log forbidden changes that merged unwarned.
ideas.problem: With a pull-only store, 'useless' and 'never consulted' look the same from outside, so we cannot tell which one we have.
ideas.stands: Designed; not yet tested. Self-reported and cross-checked against dispatch records; no hook in the first version.
ideas.next: Add the evidence line with the plan bullet after a pilot go.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design, judge panel and critic

ideas.name: Break-even model for the knowledge store
ideas.how: Net saving per hard encounter = h times (S minus lookup cost on a hit), less the miss cost and the build cost spread over use. The audit estimates h, the pilot measures it, the checkpoint measures S.
ideas.problem: A build of about ten sessions needs a stated condition under which it repays itself.
ideas.stands: Designed; owner parameters until the checkpoint replaces them with measurements. Build cost about ten sessions [E]. The decision rests on h times S, with nothing spent on Docker, sync or wiring first.
ideas.next: Fill h at the audit and S at the checkpoint.

check.notes: No numbers were invented or mis-tagged against the records. Most fixes were over-length fields (how, problem, stands, next, origin), a few inflation fixes where a design was written as if it already did something (check#45, method#45, check#46, measure#47, measure#49), and one status/maturity downgrade (measure#40, a model run on guessed inputs [G]). 'Second pilot stage' in retrieval#41 and in the flag of retrieval#39 is wrong: the source puts the build in a later phase after the pilot (KS-6b or later). Untagged design parameters in how fields (20+ queries, 40+ negatives, about 200 runs, about five or ten sessions) carry no tag in the records and were left as is. measure#39 trimmed bottlenecks to four ids; that is acceptable, since LIB-S2 (trigger) is a lower-ranked break. No raw record describing a distinct mechanism was lost: the allowed-site list, the Docker half, the prospective log and the thresholds each have their own entry. One minor omission left: measure#48 does not mention the recalibration near about 1,000 entries.

ideas.name: Typed symbol-level graph of the repo
ideas.how: A model-free script extracts about 2,500 symbols and 19+ edge kinds [M] from each task's parent commit; queries rank neighbours within hop budgets.
ideas.problem: We want a short ranked answer to what else must change with this code, following typed links across web, mobile and backend that flat search cannot follow.
ideas.stands: Tested on held-out commits: recall in an 8,000-token [S] answer 0.700 [M] vs 0.625 [M] for a scripted search. The gain is on mobile seeds (+0.151 [M]). No agent was run.
ideas.next: Decide on the agent pilot, to see whether the graph helps an agent.
ideas.origin: Graph test; owner's objections to the first test
ideas.flag: The research-results doc still says held-out not yet run; the held-out run has happened, so the newer record sets the status.

ideas.name: Co-change floor (files that changed together)
ideas.how: From earlier commits only, count files changed in the same commit, rank by support, confidence and recency, and return the top files within the token budget.
ideas.problem: We need a cheap baseline for what else changes with this file, taken only from git history, that any graph must beat.
ideas.stands: Measured on held-out commits: recall 0.638 [M] (tuning split 0.752 [M]). Typed graph beats it by +0.063 [M], but only on mobile seeds; on backend seeds 0.709 [M] vs 0.699 [M].
ideas.next: Keep reporting every graph result beside this floor and its sensitivity checks.
ideas.origin: Graph test; strongest signal in the research round

ideas.name: Same-directory floor
ideas.how: Return the other files in the seed file's folder, packed to the token budget, with no graph and no history.
ideas.problem: We want to know whether our vertical-slice folder layout already carries most connection information, so any graph must beat files in the same folder.
ideas.stands: Measured on held-out commits: recall 0.549 [M] (tuning split 0.719 [M]). Typed graph beats it by +0.151 [M]; on web seeds same-directory scored 0.773 [M] vs 0.664 [M], interval includes zero.
ideas.next: Keep as a floor in every future retrieval test.

ideas.name: PageRank and community priors for ranking
ideas.how: Personalised PageRank from the seed file, optionally with a stored community grouping, orders neighbours; iterations run in our code, only grouping comes from the engine.
ideas.problem: We want the most relevant neighbours of a changed file first inside a token budget, using ranking a flat table lacks natively.
ideas.stands: Tested on held-out commits: no gain of 0.05 or more; +0.015 [M] on the main task, interval spans zero. Five community draws moved recall as much as the effect (sd 0.008 [M]).
ideas.next: Revisit only on a larger task set or in an agent pilot.
ideas.origin: Graph test, after Aider's repo map
ideas.flag: Word as no gain of 0.05 or more, never as graphs add nothing.

ideas.name: Hop sweep with per-edge-kind budgets
ideas.how: On the tuning split only, sweep hop depth, direction, per-edge-kind budgets and hub cuts; pick the simplest setting within one standard error and freeze it.
ideas.problem: One global hop limit returns either too little or a flood. We want depth, direction and hub handling chosen per kind of link.
ideas.stands: Tested on tuning commits: import neighbours reach recall 0.38, 0.72 and 0.87 [M] at 1, 2 and 3 hops, with 9, 45 and 90 [M] files. Hop depth moved the score most.
ideas.next: Report whole curves, never one point.
ideas.origin: Bottleneck compile; owner's question on hop count

ideas.name: Output form and token-budget packing
ideas.how: One shared packer and tokenizer return the same output forms (paths, signatures, line ranges, snippets) at 2k, 4k, 8k and 16k [S] token budgets.
ideas.problem: We want to score an answer by value per token, not stored size, so the form the model receives is itself tested.
ideas.stands: Tested on held-out commits: typed beats search by +0.070 and +0.102 [M] at 2,000 and 4,000 [S] tokens; recall at 16k [S] is 0.832 [M]. Every answer filled its budget.
ideas.next: Measure tokens in an agent run, not only in the packer.
ideas.origin: Graph test; owner's point on how facts are stored

ideas.name: SQLite as the relational arm
ideas.how: SQLite with typed node and edge tables, covering indexes, full-text search, a co-change table and depth-capped recursive queries.
ideas.problem: We want the graph engines to face a strong established relational opponent, and a possible plain home for the facts, so the test is fair.
ideas.stands: Tested on held-out commits: recall 0.700 [M], identical to both graph engines; 0 mismatches on 7,040 [M] random configurations. First test: 0.05 ms [M] per query.
ideas.next: Report engine speed, size and effort from the timing run.

ideas.name: LadybugDB embedded graph engine arm
ideas.how: The same facts loaded in LadybugDB 0.22.3, a maintained fork of the archived Kuzu, queried with Cypher and its PageRank and Louvain extension, in one Linux image.
ideas.problem: We want to test an established embedded graph engine with native typed paths and ranking, not graph against relational by hand-built code.
ideas.stands: Tested: 0 mismatches in 47,244 [M] comparisons against the reference; recall 0.700 [M] on held-out, equal to the relational arm. Native ranking slow, about 0.7 s [M]. About 16 MB [S] install.
ideas.next: Report engine speed, size and effort from the timing run.

ideas.name: DuckDB with DuckPGQ graph layer arm
ideas.how: DuckDB 2.0.0 with the DuckPGQ extension loaded with the same facts; one edge table per kind, since edge filters are unavailable inside paths.
ideas.problem: We want to test a graph query layer on a relational engine, holding the engine fixed and changing only the query layer.
ideas.stands: Tested on held-out commits: shown answers identical to the relational arm on 770 of 770 [M] tasks; recall 0.700 [M]. No PageRank or Louvain, so rankings fall back to SQL. About 63 MB [S] install.
ideas.next: Report engine speed, size and effort from the timing run.

ideas.name: Neo4j and other server graph engines
ideas.how: Neo4j Community, FalkorDB or Postgres with Apache AGE run through Docker, loaded with the same typed facts.
ideas.problem: We want to know whether the market-standard graph database is a better home for the repo graph and its algorithms.
ideas.stands: Deferred: not installed, not tested. A server adds 1 to 2 GB [E] of memory on a PC short of memory, and I chose embedded engines instead.
ideas.next: Revisit only if the agent pilot shows graphs help and an embedded engine proves too small.

ideas.name: Embedding-search arm (vector index)
ideas.how: A vector index over code and docs, queried by similarity; needs a model download.
ideas.problem: We want the strongest non-graph baseline from the literature in the test, so graph gains are not credited to the index.
ideas.stands: Deferred: not in the frozen protocol and not tested. It needs a model download, which is my decision to approve.
ideas.next: Add to the wider test if I approve the download.

ideas.name: Model-built knowledge graph and graph database
ideas.how: A model reads code and docs and writes entities, relations and cluster summaries, possibly served from a graph database server or paired with embeddings.
ideas.problem: We want semantic relations parsers miss, so an agent fetches small context fast and recalls facts through a rich graph.
ideas.stands: Deferred, not tested here. Outside, model-built graphs cost about a thousand times [S] vector indexing and often lose to plain retrieval; the one big gain was against full context.
ideas.next: Test inside the wider test via graphify; index replay decides whether a small index earns a trial.
ideas.origin: Bottleneck compile; Harness v2 design; GraphRAG-style systems
ideas.flag: One source says rejected, another deferred; the owner challenged the do-not-build rule as too narrow, so deferred.

ideas.name: Graphify outside code-graph tool
ideas.how: A PyPI package builds a knowledge graph from code and mixed corpora with tree-sitter; extraction may send file contents to a model API; a hook nudges graph queries.
ideas.problem: We search code by grep and a hand-written map. I want to know why this popular tool looks good while our graph experiments looked flat.
ideas.stands: Built in the clinic testbed over an 11-file snapshot: 92 nodes, 127 edges, 10 communities [M]; no query result. Its 71.5x [S] token claim is self-measured. Not installed for FixFlow.
ideas.next: Run it as shipped in the wider test: throwaway clone, isolated install, version 14+ days old, ten fixed questions against grep.
ideas.origin: Clinic testbed; Harness review; raised by the owner
ideas.flag: The 2026-11-01 review said skip for FixFlow; I asked again on 2026-11-13. Install and model-API use need my decision.

ideas.name: File-level connection graph (first test)
ideas.how: A model-free script builds a file-to-file graph from imports, test mocks and doc citations, held as JSON or SQLite, and answers everything that depends on this file.
ideas.problem: We wanted one small answer to what depends on this file, instead of several search rounds or reading many files.
ideas.stands: Parked: I rejected it as naive and its verdict was withdrawn. It had 618 files and 1,119 links [M]; answered 1 of 200 [M] searches fully. Replaced by the typed graph test.
ideas.next: None; the idea lives on in the typed graph and the contract map.

ideas.name: Traversal cache for what-depends-on-this
ideas.how: A cache over graph traversal results for dependency lookups.
ideas.problem: We wanted to avoid recomputing what-depends-on-this-file queries, if they were slow enough to be worth caching.
ideas.stands: Tested on the first graph: all 477 [M] dependency queries together take about 1 ms [M], so there is nothing to save. The replacement test did not re-test the cache question.
ideas.next: None. It would return only if lookups became slow at larger scale.
ideas.flag: Sources differ on tag (M vs E) and one marks it rejected; the evidence comes from the first test, whose verdict was withdrawn.

ideas.name: Slice fragments generate board and true-now view
ideas.how: Each slice writes a small state fragment; tools generate a short board and a view of each fact with the commit it became true; the board diff is a check step.
ideas.problem: Slice status and findings go stale and get re-read; one writer edits an 800-line board by hand and sessions carry a 221 KB document.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 phase 3; nothing built. Target: board from 221 KB [M] to under 20 KB [T]; root edits at merge zero [T].
ideas.next: Write the fragment format and generator; add SQLite tables only if a query needs more.
ideas.origin: Harness v2 design; Bottleneck compile; knowledge-store design
ideas.flag: Could sit in WP7 as a what-is-true-now view; placed in WP3 because its problem is the board's single writer (B13). Decision D15 covers board editing by script.

ideas.name: Pull graph output, never push; build per worktree
ideas.how: Return graph output only as a tool result, never in the system prompt or CLAUDE.md; build the graph per worktree at query time.
ideas.problem: We want to stop a graph or memory layer from breaking the cached start of every window or describing the wrong working tree.
ideas.stands: Designed as a rule for any future retrieval build; not itself built or tested. Agents work in five [M] worktrees with uncommitted files, so a shared graph would mislead.
ideas.next: Write into the design of any retrieval tool we build.

ideas.name: Existing code maps: import contracts, CODE-MAP, Haiku locator
ideas.how: Import-boundary contracts (import-linter on the backend, ESLint on the web), a hand-written code map document and a Haiku locator agent.
ideas.problem: Agents need to find where a feature lives without a call-graph tool.
ideas.stands: In use in FixFlow. Not measured. Mobile code has no boundary enforcement yet.
ideas.next: Add mobile boundary rules with dependency-cruiser.

ideas.name: Slow grep-and-model search over optimised retrieval
ideas.how: Prefer reliable agentic search, grep plus a model, over optimised retrieval; a learned reranker was passed over.
ideas.problem: We want to pick a retrieval design for code understanding that is reliable rather than clever.
ideas.stands: In use: it matches what the harness already does. A learned reranker is a skip. Taken as a stated preference, not a measured result.
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: Corpus map of typed edges for planning documents
ideas.how: A versioned map of 11 planning files as typed edges with exact line spans, one status per record, a coverage ledger and hash-based refresh.
ideas.problem: Planning documents are hard to navigate. Fresh agents need bounded, source-cited context from the plan with known gaps, not whole documents.
ideas.stands: Built in the clinic testbed as design plus prototype; no coding agent used it. 3,361 records for 167 KB [M]; extraction recall 0.52 [M] against an earlier reading; validation never run.
ideas.next: Run the frozen validation contract before building any map; carry over the status discipline and recompute-from-base rule.
ideas.flag: One source says abandoned at P9-4 with trials not started; adoption is my pending decision.

ideas.name: Context packet query with frontier and gap lists
ideas.how: Breadth-first expansion from a named start within a token budget; each record carries a quote and file lines, plus unresolved, frontier and coverage lines.
ideas.problem: We want to give a fresh agent a small, cited evidence packet by named start, not whole documents.
ideas.stands: Built in the clinic testbed; never compared with routed reading, so delivered tokens and task quality are unknown. Extraction recall 0.523 exact, 0.588 loose [M].
ideas.next: Run the validation contract before building a packet tool for FixFlow.

ideas.name: Coverage ledger and stale-label freshness
ideas.how: A ledger lists read and unread chunks per file version; queries check file hashes, label changed records stale, and refresh supersedes rather than deletes.
ideas.problem: A derived index silently goes out of date when source files change, and we cannot tell what was actually read.
ideas.stands: Built in the clinic testbed as a manual command, tested on synthetic cases only; the changed-source case was not run. 4,053 dangling endpoints at levels 1 and 2 [M].
ideas.next: Wire chunk-hash plus stale labelling to a hook or CI, to catch CLAUDE.md drift.

ideas.name: Candidate index: similarity proposes, never decides
ideas.how: Similarity and alias proposals sit in a separate candidates file that no query reads; a test deletes it and checks packets are byte-identical.
ideas.problem: Similarity retrieval can leak guesses into answers that are meant to carry evidence. We want guesses kept apart.
ideas.stands: Built in the clinic testbed with its deletion test; precision not measured. 1,906 candidates [M] in the store, 93 [M] open for one file.
ideas.next: Copy the separation rule into any FixFlow recall tool.

ideas.name: Doc-context small language model with hash staleness
ideas.how: A local small model builds a bounded doc-state summary with a source pointer on each statement; stale summaries are flagged by source hash, not model judgement.
ideas.problem: Our evolving documentation goes stale and costs context to read.
ideas.stands: Designed in the clinic testbed; nothing run. Premises: one task-state file 17,174 chars [M] against a 9,000 [S] budget (one case); docs about 1.36 MB [M].
ideas.next: Build the cheap, testable part first: hash-based stale detection.

ideas.name: Same-facts cross-check between engines
ideas.how: Given identical facts and algorithm, two engines must return the identical answer; best designs are re-implemented across engines and an in-memory reference. A mismatch is a bug.
ideas.problem: We want score differences to come from facts, algorithm and output form, never from an engine bug.
ideas.stands: In use in the graph test: typed arms identical on 770 of 770 [M] held-out tasks; the two hypothesis differences were exactly 0 [M].
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: Code-reading question set (50 questions)
ideas.how: 50 [S] structured questions answered by one reader with evidence lines and checked blind by a second; 20 for tuning, 30 held out.
ideas.problem: We want to score structured lookups, such as which tables a screen writes, with truth read from the code rather than from the extractor.
ideas.stands: Tested on 30 held-out questions: typed minus search +0.100 [M], interval spans zero, so inconclusive. On 23 untouched questions +0.189 [M]. Median answer 31 vs 695 [M] tokens.
ideas.next: State both token views and name the typed side's uncounted costs.
ideas.flag: Token figures compare answer size with what search read, not like for like.

ideas.name: Agent-in-the-loop pilot
ideas.how: Replay 24 to 30 [E] historical fix commits with a fixed agent given grep only, plus SQL, a graph tool, or BM25 or embeddings; record tokens, calls and success.
ideas.problem: I want to know whether a graph or knowledge layer lets an agent finish with fewer tokens, calls and mistakes than ordinary search.
ideas.stands: Deferred, not run; it needs model tokens and many agents. One outside study cut tokens 17 to 39 % [S] on two benchmarks and raised them on a third.
ideas.next: I decide on the pilot and its token budget; start with the wider-test protocol.
ideas.flag: No agent was run in the held-out graph test.

ideas.name: Wider graph test protocol
ideas.how: Five research lanes, an assumptions audit and strongest-architecture design, a refuter, a protocol draft and a design check; no installs.
ideas.problem: I want to test the architecture I described, with knowledge layer, time, caching, an agent and graphify as an arm, not only the scorable part.
ideas.stands: Idea stage: research and protocol draft were in progress when last recorded; nothing tested. The page must state the narrow scope of the earlier test on its first screen.
ideas.next: Read the draft protocol and bring owner decisions on graphify and the agent pilot.

ideas.name: Podcast RSS feeds for transcripts
ideas.how: Read the feed's transcript tag; otherwise fetch the audio enclosure.
ideas.problem: Show pages expose only part of a podcast's transcript, so research on outside ideas is incomplete.
ideas.stands: In use for two podcasts: one feed gave a 12,100-word [M] transcript against 1,800 words [M] from the site.
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: X timeline via fxtwitter; charts read as images
ideas.how: Page the fxtwitter timeline endpoint for a user's posts and self-replies; give chart images to a reader agent.
ideas.problem: X posts could not be read (HTTP 402) and benchmark numbers sat only in chart images.
ideas.stands: In use: 197 statuses since 1 September [M], 159 [M] the author's own, plus 7 [M] charts read. Replies under posts are not captured.
ideas.next: Keep using it.

Statuses kept as in merged records; flags note source conflicts for retrieval#0, #11, #12, #14 and #23. check.notes: Checked all 30 entries against the merged records, the bottleneck register and the package list. Maturity, status, wp and bottleneck ids are all valid and correct per the mapping, and no raw record describing a distinct mechanism was lost, so no splits are proposed. Most fixes are word-limit overruns in "how" fields (words only, no facts changed). Substantive fixes are retrieval#12 problem (the must-not-claim rule on graphs adding nothing), measure#11 stands (not like-for-like token comparison) and retrieval#1 and retrieval#2 (disambiguating which score belongs to which method). Left unchanged but noted. (1) retrieval#7 "about 0.7 s [M]" and retrieval#18 "800-line" appear untagged in the records, so the tags are unconfirmed. (2) retrieval#14 tags the 477 queries at about 1 ms as [M], while one source tags them [E]; a refuter note says the figure comes from the first, withdrawn test's in-memory graph. (3) retrieval#9 "1 to 2 GB [E]" is untagged in the records. (4) retrieval#10 says not in the protocol, while protocol.md:46 mentions an embedding arm; the entry follows the record's status note. (5) retrieval#4 says the hop figures were measured on tuning commits; this is inferred from the status note "swept on TUNE". (6) The sourced figures for retrieval#0, #5 and #8 are consistent with the records.

ideas.name: Token tally from session transcripts
ideas.how: Read-only scripts parse every transcript, count each call once per message id, and total calls, tokens and compactions per group and per slice session.
ideas.problem: We did not know where our tokens went or why usage limits hit, so any cut would have been a guess.
ideas.stands: Measured for both months: 4,252.9M [M] cache-read tokens over 184 files; slice sessions 66.4 % [M] by one count; a re-measurement agreed within 0.3 % [M].
ideas.next: Rerun the October script on November for per-slice figures, and again after any lever to see its effect.
ideas.origin: Clinic testbed; Bottleneck compile; Harness v2 design; Token report
ideas.flag: Sources differ on the slice share: 66.4 % in the compile, but three slice sessions 42 % [M] with roots and subagents 24.4 % [M] in the phase 1 file. Check which grouping the PDF quotes.

ideas.name: Window-fill analysis: what fills the context
ideas.how: Classify each context token from growth between calls, weighted by re-reads: fixed start, own output, fetched content, summaries. Also count lookup-only calls.
ideas.problem: Knowing the token total is not enough; we did not know what content fills the windows, so claims about levers were guesses.
ideas.stands: Measured, checked by two refuters: FixFlow fetched content 27-28.5 % [E], 43.6 % [E] re-read by lookup-only calls; testbed own output 53-69 % [M] of growth. Exposures, not savings.
ideas.next: Replay recorded windows with an index; rerun the fill after any lever; run the testbed breakdown on FixFlow orchestrator sessions.
ideas.origin: Bottleneck compile; Token report; Clinic testbed
ideas.flag: The re-measurement put fetched content at 22.3 % [E] against 26-28.5 % [E]; quote the range, not one figure.

ideas.name: Fixed context overhead measurement
ideas.how: A usage tool breaks down each agent's overhead (tools, MCP, skills, system prompt, memory); a script measures how documentation grows.
ideas.problem: Every session or subagent carries tokens before doing any work, and we did not know how large that fixed start is.
ideas.stands: Measured in the October testbed: about 70k [M] tokens before work (system tools 33,968, MCP 16,599, skills 9,059 [M]). Docs about 338,816 tokens [E].
ideas.next: Trim MCP servers and skills in agent sessions; keep the routed pre-read small.
ideas.flag: October snapshot from one subagent breakdown; docs grew in November.

ideas.name: Number tags on every figure
ideas.how: Tag every number as measured, estimated, guess or outside figure, with target and illustrative tags added by the harness.
ideas.problem: Readers could not tell a measured number from a guess, so a guess could pass as a result.
ideas.stands: In use across the program documents: [M] measured, [E] estimated, [G] guess, [S] outside figure, plus [T] target and [I] illustrative.
ideas.next: Keep tagging.

ideas.name: Record unknown as unknown, never zero
ideas.how: Store an unmeasured value as unknown, and write decisive checks with explicit if-and-raise rather than bare assert.
ideas.problem: If we record missing data as zero, a gap looks like a measured absence and we draw the wrong conclusion.
ideas.stands: Adopted as a stated lesson from the CureFound research results; it matches the repository rule that an unknown evidence value is not zero. Not separately measured.
ideas.next: Apply to every tally and check script.

ideas.name: Pre-registered, sealed held-out test protocol
ideas.how: Fix the protocol before any arm exists: split commits by date, tune on one part only, one main metric, a smallest difference worth acting on, named wording.
ideas.problem: We want every test to settle something, so tuning, the held-out set and the scoring rule are fixed first and wording cannot overclaim.
ideas.stands: In use on the graph test: 140 commits split 65 tune and 75 held-out [S]; held-out run clean; smallest detectable difference about 0.09 recall [E]; every arm lost 0.06 to 0.17 [M] from tune to held-out.
ideas.next: Reuse the same rules for the wider test and each new experiment.
ideas.origin: Graph test, from the owner's critique
ideas.flag: At this size inconclusive is likely and reads as no evidence either way; do not word it as graphs adding nothing.

ideas.name: Replacement graph test with a real engine
ideas.how: Vary facts, algorithm, output form and engine separately; sealed tasks from 140 commits and 50 questions; hops 1 to 6; a search baseline; a SQLite arm.
ideas.problem: Our first graph test used the weakest query and no real engine, so it could not tell us whether a repo graph helps.
ideas.stands: Tested on held-out commits: run clean, with a scripted search arm and no agent run. Hop 1 recall 0.38, hop 2 0.72, hop 3 0.87 [M]; typed path 4 tables against 254 nodes [M].
ideas.next: Owner chooses which graph engine to install; then run an agent arm in the pilot.
ideas.flag: Merged record says designed, build under way; sibling records say the held-out run completed, so status raised to tested. Confirm which hop figures belong to the held-out run.

ideas.name: Scripted search baseline arm
ideas.how: A fixed script does text search for the task's names, paths and route strings, in one and two rounds. It is not an agent searching.
ideas.problem: We need to compare every graph against what our sessions do today, which is plain text search.
ideas.stands: Tested on held-out commits: recall 0.625 [M] one round, 0.634 [M] two rounds, median 6 to 8 [M] lookups; tune 0.759 [M]. No agent was run.
ideas.next: Replace it with an agent using ordinary search tools in the pilot.
ideas.origin: Graph test, after the Aider repo map
ideas.flag: Must always be called a scripted search, never an agent search.

ideas.name: Frozen validation contract for any map or store
ideas.how: Sealed: 5 cases, 3 arms (map, routed reading, Graphify), 2 runs each, equal budgets, blind scoring; better needs a 0.10 gap in 4 of 5 cases.
ideas.problem: We built maps and stores without testing whether they beat the routed reading we already have, so we want a fair A/B first.
ideas.stands: Designed and frozen in the testbed, never run: 30 runs [S], 16,000 tokens [S] per run; the runs folder is empty. Work moved to context-admission research.
ideas.next: Run it, or a FixFlow copy, before building any map, store or graph; it gives a reusable A/B template.
ideas.flag: Owner decision pending: run the 30-run comparison or retire the map.

ideas.name: Replay before live
ideas.how: Accept a mechanism by replaying it on the recorded history where possible, and run it record-only before it may refuse anything.
ideas.problem: A gate or review mechanism could refuse good work or miss defects, so we want proof on the record before it can block us.
ideas.stands: Adopted as a standing rule of harness v2, to apply to mechanisms 1 to 6. No mechanism has yet run live under it.
ideas.next: Apply the rule to mechanisms 1 to 6 (decision D15).

ideas.name: Zero-token import-and-caller index replay
ideas.how: At each recorded window's start commit, build an import-and-caller index, count lookups it would answer, and check it lists the files the window later edited.
ideas.problem: Our sessions spend many calls only reading; we want to know cheaply whether a code index would have answered them before spending agent tokens.
ideas.stands: Designed, not yet run: 54.7 % [M] of calls only read or search. Co-change half is weak, only 432 commits [M]. Proposed pass marks 3 % of tokens, recall 0.8 [T].
ideas.next: Owner sets the pass marks (D23); then run the replay in phase 3 and go live only if it passes.
ideas.flag: Merged from two records; the 27 to 28.5 % [E] and 43.6 % [E] figures are exposures, not savings.

ideas.name: Measured-rates table feeding planner and governor
ideas.how: The check, merge queue and transcript tally write measured rates (check time, waits, tokens per lane-hour, rounds per slice); every wave updates them.
ideas.problem: We lay out plans on guessed times and an unknown token window, so we cannot tell which limit comes first.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2; not yet tested. First rates are the check timings 367 s and 230 s [M]; the planner and governor depend on it.
ideas.next: Take phase 2 container gate timings, then the phase 5 per-slice baseline.

ideas.name: System-dynamics model of the harness
ideas.how: Eleven stocks with flow equations, nine switchable controllers and four limits; assumptions listed. It shows behaviour, not a forecast.
ideas.problem: Which limit binds first depends on rates, so we want to see how each controller changes the machine before building it.
ideas.stands: Built in the harness v2 page; a refuter checked claims. At October's window of about 2.5 lane-hours [E], tokens are the first limit at any lane count [I].
ideas.next: Replace guessed inputs with measured rates.
ideas.flag: Outputs rest on guessed inputs; label them illustrative. It leaves out power-offs, owner away time and memory.

ideas.name: Fit-screen the idea sweeps against bottlenecks
ideas.how: Opus mappers placed kept ideas, Sonnet readers screened dropped ones, adjudicators ruled on flagged ones, refuters attacked claimed fits, and a script checked every id.
ideas.problem: Both idea sweeps scored ideas against the FixFlow ship plan, never against our 21 bottlenecks, so their verdicts could not carry over.
ideas.stands: Tested in three workflows with 19 agents, models reading documents only: 87 kept ideas gave 29 fits [M]; 868 dropped gave 142 flagged and 1 promoted [M].
ideas.next: Compile the surviving mechanisms into the build order.
ideas.flag: One Sonnet pass screened the dropped Horthy families, so a missed idea stays missed.

ideas.name: Pre-registered evaluation plan with gates and staged budgets
ideas.how: Four arms, gates written in advance, staged budgets with caps, inconclusive at budget exhaustion, and all overhead charged to the treatment.
ideas.problem: We want to stop a harness declaring its own win, so gates and budgets are settled before anything runs.
ideas.stands: Designed in the testbed; stage 1 and a screen ran, stages 2 to 4 did not. Gates of minus 50 % and minus 25 % input were not met (adapter +10.31 % [M], +17.02 % [M]).
ideas.next: Copy the template for the next FixFlow memory or token experiment; it accepts the simpler workflow as a valid result.
ideas.flag: Stage 1 and the final study actually ran (984,984 [M] input in stage 1; 4,350,448 [M] in the final study), so tested is arguable; kept as designed per the record.

ideas.name: Trial harness: transcript accounting and blind scoring
ideas.how: Scripts build per-arm workspaces, read agent transcripts for tokens and peak context, check citations, and blind the arm labels before scoring.
ideas.problem: We want per-agent tokens, tool calls and file reads measured after the fact, and runs scored without knowing which arm they came from.
ideas.stands: Built in the testbed; not yet run on trials, only an extraction comparison exists. Its token figures are characters divided by 4 [E].
ideas.next: Adapt the measuring script to Claude Code's transcript format; it could give FixFlow sub-agent cost per task.

ideas.name: Pilot of the attested-only map on four files
ideas.how: Four frozen files read under the design by a skeptic and an independent annotator; counts compared, then re-applied under a revised design.
ideas.problem: We wanted to check whether a strictly sourced map recovers the dependency chain a human annotator saw.
ideas.stands: Tested in the testbed: first design 427 attested edges [M], chain not reproduced; revised design 692 edges [M] with 1,166 dangling endpoints [M]. Links through a shared value cannot be joined.
ideas.next: Use grep plus a drift check for repeated constants such as the money limit and Alembic head.

ideas.name: Evaluation protocol with Amdahl bound
ideas.how: Measure accepted tasks per active human hour; freeze the real baseline; change one mechanism at a time; randomise order; keep all attempts; bound the gain by Amdahl's rule.
ideas.problem: We had no agreed way to judge whether a workflow change is an improvement.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed; no 3x or 5x claim is established. 20 % avoidable effort gives at most 1.25x [I]; 8 [M] run records are schema-valid but carry null telemetry.
ideas.next: Size the review and orchestrator bottlenecks with the bound before building.
ideas.flag: The 1.25x figure is illustrative arithmetic, not a measurement.

ideas.name: Measurement ledger and pipeline M00-M06
ideas.how: An append-only log with hash manifests and an identity hierarchy, an optional rebuildable SQLite index, and seven build slices.
ideas.problem: We had no standing way to measure whether harness changes help; all eight exports had null tokens, effort, cost and resume time.
ideas.stands: Parked: designed in the testbed, never built. The owner ruled it low priority and the review rated it skip, as a month of research showed no gain. Eight [M] exports lack tokens.
ideas.next: Log per-session wall time, usage and rework in a small append-only file, with no pipeline.
ideas.flag: Sibling records disagree (designed, deferred, rejected); set to deferred as the owner ruled low priority. Owner may raise the priority.

ideas.name: Tool qualification and G0-G8 gates
ideas.how: Qualify maintained tools (Promptfoo, Langfuse, Phoenix) before writing a runner; use independent oracles, hold-out inaccessibility and a trap list for green-but-empty results.
ideas.problem: Measurement tools can report green or zero when nothing was checked, so we want to catch that before trusting a number.
ideas.stands: Designed in the testbed; no tool installed or run. Registers cover 27 methods and 44 tool source groups [M]; four Promptfoo traps were read from source, not reproduced.
ideas.next: Audit FixFlow's gates for zero tests, skipped tests and defaulted cost fields.

ideas.name: Effectiveness review F01-F10
ideas.how: Four separate measures (quality, context, productivity, cost), a context freshness test, a frozen baseline, and a throwaway synthetic deployment with backup and restore.
ideas.problem: A claim of 3x measures productivity, not quality, and we lacked early proof the system runs and restores.
ideas.stands: Designed in the testbed as proposals only; not yet tested. The illustrative hosting cost was $7.79 [I] against an $8 [S] cap.
ideas.next: Walk a clean install and restore early.
ideas.flag: Also overlaps WP9 (first use); placed in WP8 for its measurement framing.

ideas.name: Throughput record from git history
ideas.how: Count commits per day on all branches and first-parent merges onto main with light git log commands, and note gap days.
ideas.problem: We had no before-and-after baseline of how much work lands per day.
ideas.stands: Measured in the testbed: 426 [M] commits since 1 Nov, peak 150 [M] on 6 Nov, 36 [M] first-parent merges onto main. Commit counts are not a quality measure.
ideas.next: Compute before and after any harness change; pair with per-slice token counts.

ideas.name: Slow-path diagnosis: Windows to Docker port
ideas.how: Measure machine, worker and VM CPU during a parallel pass, and per-query latency from Windows against inside the container.
ideas.problem: Adding test workers stopped helping, and we wanted to find where the time actually went.
ideas.stands: Measured in the testbed: machine at 42 % [M] of 24 processors; six Python workers used 2.45 [M] cores; a trivial query took 0.63 ms [M] from Windows against 0.13 ms [M] in the container.
ideas.next: Check whether workers wait on a network hop before adding more; it points to running tests beside the database.
ideas.flag: The cause is inferred; the container run is the closest A/B.

ideas.name: Worker sweep and per-second load sampler
ideas.how: Sweep worker counts (6, 9, 12, 16) while a dependency-free sampler writes machine CPU and free memory to CSV; test a pair before approving a second slot.
ideas.problem: We want worker and slot counts chosen from measurement, and memory and CPU visible during checks and drills.
ideas.stands: In use on checks and the rig VM: 6 workers 137.5 s [M], 12 workers 104.7-135.1 s [M]; knee between 6 and 12. Two container checks took 266-267 s [M] against 220 s [M] alone.
ideas.next: Run the sampler on the Windows PC itself to diagnose shutdowns and idle-session memory.
ideas.flag: Not yet used on the developer PC for crash diagnosis.

Bottleneck ids B12, B14 and others were chosen by the idea's own problem where the raw ids had no register match. check.notes: Main substantive fixes: (1) measure#7 attributed the hop recall figures (0.38, 0.72, 0.87) and the 4-tables-against-254-nodes figure to the held-out run. Those come from earlier research lanes and the first test (HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS-2026-11.md lines 253 and 255). The held-out result is in docs/program/GRAPH-TEST-RESULT-2026-11.md, so I replaced them with the held-out figures: +0.076 typed minus scripted search, and engines identical on 770 of 770 tasks. The search arm was a scripted search and no agent was run. The raised status "tested" (maturity 4) for measure#7 is supported, since that file shows the held-out run completed with SQLite, LadybugDB and a DuckDB graph layer. (2) measure#0 gave the November token total as if it covered both months. (3) measure#32's name said per-second, but the sampler runs every 5 s (2 s on the VM). (4) measure#26 had an unsupported LIB-EVAL bottleneck. (5) Several fields were over the word limits, counting bracket tags as words: measure#6, 7, 10, 14, 17, 21, 22, 26, 31 and 32. I trimmed these and kept every number and tag. If the program that applies these corrections does not count tags as words, the trims lose a few words of detail but nothing else. Checked and left alone: measure#0's flag about 66.4 % versus 42 % is two different groupings (the phase-1 file gives root plus subagents 24.4 % and three slice sessions 42 %), and the entry's wording "by one count" already hedges it. measure#22 stays at designed/2 as the record says, although stage 1 and a screen did run. measure#27 stays deferred/1. No split proposals: in every merged record, the raw records describe the same mechanism (measure#0 Oct and Nov tallies, measure#17 the two index-replay descriptions, measure#27 the three ledger records). All figures and tags in the remaining entries match their records. The decision references (D15, D23) are owner decision ids, not raw card ids, so I left them in.

ideas.name: Send-back repeat share
ideas.how: Count the share of review send-backs that repeat a class of finding already found earlier.
ideas.problem: We do not know how often a review send-back repeats a finding class we have already seen, so we cannot tell if lessons are being captured.
ideas.stands: Proposed in the library review; not run, so no repeat share exists yet.
ideas.next: Count repeats across the recorded review rounds.

ideas.name: Recurrence audit before any knowledge-store build
ideas.how: Sonnet classifies 72 [M] fix commits, counting a repeat only under three strict tests; an Opus refuter rechecks every counted repeat.
ideas.problem: We have not shown that the same cause ever hits twice in a way a symptom-keyed store could serve, so a build might repay nothing.
ideas.stands: Designed in the knowledge-store design; not yet run. A raw count already shows 3 to 5 same-cause repeats among 48 fix commits on main [M].
ideas.next: I answer D1 (run the audit); Sonnet extracts, Opus refutes. It gives the prior that decides whether to build.
ideas.flag: Records name two ids (KS-C10, KS-K18) that are not in the register; mapped to the knowledge-store value id.

ideas.name: Missed-existing detector with blind re-rule
ideas.how: At record time the author lists prior lookups; detectors flag roster matches; author rules same/related/new; reviewer re-rules blind. Unknown stays NULL, never zero.
ideas.problem: A miss of an entry that existed looks the same as a store nobody consulted, so we cannot measure recall or whether embeddings are needed.
ideas.stands: Designed in the knowledge-store design (built in KS-2 and KS-3, read at KS-9); a lower bound by construction. Not yet tested; expected under about 0.2 per 8-week window [E].
ideas.next: Build with the write gate (KS-4/5), fixtures in KS-2; counts then give the embedding decision (D16) a real denominator.
ideas.flag: One raw record maps the store-recall id to W2 (compliance) through the alias table; I chose the recall and value ids by the idea's own problem.

ideas.name: Transcript tally at phase close
ideas.how: A read-only Node script scores 8 [T] routine steps from session transcript tool calls and compares them with the closing message.
ideas.problem: Routine steps that leave no git or GitHub trace look the same whether done or skipped, so we cannot check compliance from outside.
ideas.stands: Trial from the Dex Horthy sweep (top trial 2); about 100 lines [E]. Not yet tested. Must run within 7 days [S] of a phase close, before transcripts are pruned.
ideas.next: Run after the first three phases within seven days; shows whether an outside compliance check works without hooks.

ideas.name: 'Sessions:' line in the PR journal
ideas.how: One plain line listing session ids, copied from the scratchpad path, goes into the existing PR journal.
ideas.problem: Transcripts of resumed or multi-session phases are hard to find when we want to audit them.
ideas.stands: Trial from the Dex Horthy sweep, run alongside the transcript tally; not yet tested. Audit at least 7 days [S] after close.
ideas.next: On the first 3 [T] closed PRs, check the transcript is found from the branch alone and every session is listed.

ideas.name: Cause tag on owner-correction journal entries
ideas.how: A one-word tag (harness, plan or product) on each owner-correction journal entry; count harness-tagged shapes that repeat.
ideas.problem: When I correct an agent, we cannot tell a harness failure from a plan or product error, so repeats stay invisible.
ideas.stands: Trial from the Dex Horthy sweep; a weekly trace-mining loop was dropped. Not yet tested. Covers the first 5 [T] executed phases.
ideas.next: Tag every correction at each close; it passes if at least one harness shape repeats.

ideas.name: Per-PR rework rate as health metric
ideas.how: Track the share of each PR's diff changed after review; under 5% [T] is the quality bar.
ideas.problem: We have no measure of whether review is converging or code keeps changing after review.
ideas.stands: Parked: deferred in the Dex Horthy sweep. No refuter verdict, reviewers split between trial and skip, and no measurement is defined. Not tested.
ideas.next: Decide whether to send it to a refuter; defining how to measure it would bring it back.
ideas.flag: Records tag it W2 and L3; I added B01 (fix rounds) as the nearest register id for review convergence.

ideas.name: Honest cold-resume trial with hashed answer key
ideas.how: Record a hash of the answer file in the PR journal first, commit the file after judging, run on a checkout without it, then check the read log.
ideas.problem: The one test of whether a fresh session can resume our work could pass just by the agent reading the answer file.
ideas.stands: Adopted for phase 1 (P1), narrowed after refuter review; n=1 [S], one rerun if contaminated. Not yet run. Pass: hash first, zero reads of the key.
ideas.next: Apply it in the P1 cold-resume trial; it makes that single resume test trustworthy.

ideas.name: Re-run CLAUDE.md probes on model change
ideas.how: At a recorded model change, run 10 [S] probes with the full CLAUDE.md on a frozen commit, old against new model, 3 [S] fresh sessions each.
ideas.problem: A new model behind the Sonnet or Opus tier may follow CLAUDE.md rules differently, and nothing would show it.
ideas.stands: Trial from the Dex Horthy sweep, narrowed by the refuter; runs only after the first CLAUDE.md probe set has run once. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: At the first model change, run the 10 probes with a frozen rubric, old against new.

ideas.name: Medium-vs-xhigh effort trial, pass bar first
ideas.how: Replay 12 [S] frozen verifier briefs at medium and xhigh, 3 times each, with an xhigh repeat as noise floor; write the pass bar first.
ideas.problem: Choosing a model effort for reviewers and verifiers is guesswork, and without a rule fixed in advance a comparison can be bent to its result.
ideas.stands: Trial from the Dex Horthy sweep, one-off: 12 [S] briefs plus 5 [S] fixtures from closed defects, blind-graded. Not yet tested; the testbed has no effort benchmark.
ideas.next: Select 12 briefs and build 5 fixtures, once I decide FixFlow runs its effort decision.
ideas.flag: Merged from four records; the standing re-run on every model was refuted, only the one-off trial remains.

ideas.name: Symmetric reading rule for single-run gaps
ideas.how: A zero-cost reading rule: a single-run gap of a few strict passes counts as no detectable difference for either effort level; cost and task fit then decide.
ideas.problem: One benchmark run per setting cannot separate an effort effect from noise, so we risk over-reading small gaps.
ideas.stands: Adopted for this review's effort decisions only. Source: medium 28 against xhigh 25 of 196 [S] strict passes, one run each, read as no detectable difference.
ideas.next: Apply when the effort dispositions are written; pass is zero statements treating a single-run gap as evidence.

ideas.name: One provenance line in each evidence README
ideas.how: Each evidence README gets one line: exact model id, ids the aliases resolved to, tool version and run date.
ideas.problem: Someone re-running or disputing an evidence folder later cannot tell which model and tool build produced it.
ideas.stands: Adopted, narrowed to one line; standing re-runs on every release were dropped. Not yet tested; pass is 2 of 2 [T] next folders carrying the line.
ideas.next: Add the line to the next two evidence READMEs.

ideas.name: Rerun knowledge-store refuter set at high effort
ideas.how: Rerun the committed refuter workflow on frozen inputs at Opus high effort twice and compare with the xhigh outcomes.
ideas.problem: We do not know whether verifiers run at xhigh need to be that expensive.
ideas.stands: Trial from the Dex Horthy sweep, conditional: runs only if xhigh verifier spend is at least 20% [T] of use. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Wait for the usage-recording figure; if spend clears 20% [T], run it.

ideas.name: Judge models by corrections per conversation
ideas.how: Judge a model by loop or goal outcomes and the corrections needed per conversation, not one-shot answers.
ideas.problem: One-shot answers are a poor way to judge a model for loop-style work.
ideas.stands: Parked: skipped in the Dex Horthy sweep; owner corrections are already journalled and tallied elsewhere, and land on the orchestrator, not a routing tier. Source's five-to-two figure is illustrative [I].
ideas.next: None.

ideas.name: Standing regression re-runs for briefs and models
ideas.how: Run 10-30 [S] past inputs on old and new brief 3 times each, score with deterministic checks, review only disagreements; re-run on each model release.
ideas.problem: Editing an agent brief or changing a model could silently change results, with no test to show it.
ideas.stands: Parked: not now. Inputs are live repo and web, not fixed cases; cost about 60-180 [E] agent runs per brief edit; the standing re-run is the skipped measurement pipeline again.
ideas.next: Reopen only after a recorded brief edit flipped a verdict; none is on record. Useful parts live in the effort trial.
ideas.flag: Merged from a BAML-sweep record and a Dex Horthy-sweep record.

ideas.name: Schema-retry count as a brief-quality signal
ideas.how: Log structured-output rejection counts per brief over 3 [S] runs; flag any brief above a 10% [G] retry rate.
ideas.problem: A brief that makes agents fail the output schema often may be defective, but our scripts cannot see retry counts.
ideas.stands: Parked: refuted in the BAML sweep because the program has never recorded a schema rejection; its failures are usage and session limits. The 10% [G] threshold is arbitrary. Not tested.
ideas.next: None.
ideas.flag: Record names an id (BML-4) that is not in the register; mapped to the brief-test id.

ideas.name: Medium-effort verifiers via blind paired shadow runs
ideas.how: A blind medium-effort shadow reruns each non-P0 verifier's brief; 30+ [T] pairs, pass bar set first, 3 repeats per arm, scored against final adjudication.
ideas.problem: Most of our verifiers run at xhigh effort, which costs more, and one outside report says medium often matched or beat it.
ideas.stands: Trial, top trial 1 in the Dex Horthy sweep; not yet tested. Targets: agreement within 1 of incumbent [T], medium tokens at most 0.6x [T]. Outside evidence is weaker than first read.
ideas.next: Start in the next review workflows; costs about 30 [E] extra agents; decides whether the xhigh default stays.
ideas.flag: Needs my yes to trial the effort test and accept the extra agents.

ideas.name: Record weekly-window usage per phase
ideas.how: At phase open and close, the closing evidence line records weekly-window percent from usage data, plus subagent tokens and agents lost to a usage limit.
ideas.problem: Outside dollar figures do not fit a flat subscription where weekly limits bind, so we do not know the verifier spend share.
ideas.stands: Trial from the Dex Horthy sweep, narrowed to phases 1 to 3; not yet tested. Its figure decides whether the high-effort refuter rerun runs (threshold 20% [T]).
ideas.next: Record at the next phase open.
ideas.flag: Records tag the second id L2, which the alias table maps to context growth; I used the usage-accounting id by the idea's own problem.

ideas.name: Record true peak context and reversal positions
ideas.how: For 5 [T] phase sessions a Haiku extractor sums input, cache-creation and cache-read tokens per call, records the peak, and logs where reversed decisions sit.
ideas.problem: A 40% [S] context rule is untested here, and the on-screen percentage includes the autocompact buffer, so we mislocate decisions made at high context.
ideas.stands: Trial from the Dex Horthy sweep; the counting method was corrected in its 2026-11-09 addendum. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Run on the first 5 [T] phase sessions.

ideas.name: Transcript-derived read audit of analysts
ideas.how: A short Node script compares an analyst's self-listed extra reads with the Read and Grep calls in its subagent transcript.
ideas.problem: Analyst reading rules are brief text and extra reads are self-reported and unenforced, so we cannot tell whether an analyst obeyed them.
ideas.stands: Trial from the BAML sweep, unrefuted. Feasibility shown: one lane reader's transcript holds 115 [M] tool-call entries. Mismatch rate not yet measured.
ideas.next: Measure the mismatch rate on one analyst from a committed run; make it standing only if self-reports under-count.
ideas.flag: Needs my yes to commission the one-analyst measurement.

ideas.name: Limitations first, no fixes until agreed
ideas.how: List and weigh limitations first; the record and map carry no fixes; we discuss using the ranking.
ideas.problem: Fixing before we agree the limitations would hide which ones matter.
ideas.stands: In use in the library review: 69 [M] limitations listed and weighed, no fixes agreed. A nine-agent solve round was started and stopped at my request.
ideas.next: Agree the limitation list with me, using the ranking.
ideas.flag: A working rule rather than a tool; no register bottleneck fits.

ideas.name: Lean-workflow reassessment
ideas.how: Nine dispositions on a proposal I pasted: keep root authority, reject no-docs, treat size triggers as review triggers, reject a hook allowlist; primary sources checked.
ideas.problem: We wanted to know whether a minimal-surface setup would beat our documented workflow.
ideas.stands: Parked: no change adopted; comparison never run. Root instruction file is 28 lines, 6,709 bytes [M]; outside: context files raised cost over 20% [S].
ideas.next: Measure before trimming; one owner per rule.
ideas.flag: Records tag B04 and B13; I mapped it to the instruction-file-size id by the idea's own problem.

ideas.name: Adoption audits of reference repositories
ideas.how: Source-first audits of six outside projects; adopt small fields (code-shape block, boundary trace, fail-before/pass-after, error retirement) and reject installing runtimes.
ideas.problem: We needed to know which ideas from outside agent projects are worth adopting.
ideas.stands: Adopted narrowly in the clinic testbed; runtimes, webhooks and vector databases rejected. 1,658 [M] files rehashed, none missing; no upstream tests run.
ideas.next: Do not equate a stored token field with spend; verify instruction loading.
ideas.flag: The four-repo reassessment of the same material is recorded as researched and rejected.

ideas.name: Sealed replay with read log
ideas.how: Replay in a clone with no later refs, answer key hashed first, read log from the transcript, one head commit and brief per arm.
ideas.problem: Replaying an old fix chain to test a review method is unfair if the agent can peek at the later fix, finding tables or board.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 phase 3 (mechanism 1), first script at zero tokens; never run. Proof planned: one recorded fix chain, sealed clone against plain worktree.
ideas.next: Write the clone-and-read-log script and test it on two [T] runs; makes replay evidence for B01, B12 and B17 fair.
ideas.origin: Harness v2 design; Dex Horthy sweep
ideas.flag: Merged with a stub-run idea; the Dex Horthy sweep rated parts adopt and trial, while the design files it as designed.

condensed.notes: All 24 entries written. Mapping choices: ids absent from the register (KS-C10, KS-K18, BML-4, BML-6) were replaced by the nearest register id; a few alias-table mappings (W2 for the store-recall record, R2 for L2, B04/B13 for the lean-workflow record) were overridden by each idea's own problem, noted in flags. Tags: the 10% retry threshold is tagged [G] because the record calls it arbitrary; counts of commits, files and limitations are tagged [M]; targets and sample sizes of planned trials are [T] or [S].

corrections.value: Designed in the knowledge-store design (build planned in KS-2 and KS-3, read at KS-9); a lower bound by construction. Not yet tested; expected under about 0.2 per 8-week window [E].
corrections.reason: The records file this as designed; 'built in KS-2 and KS-3' reads as already built, but those are planned build steps.

corrections.value: Top trial 1 in the Dex Horthy sweep; not yet tested. Targets: agreement at least incumbent minus 1 [T], medium tokens at most 0.6x [T]. Outside evidence is weaker than first read.
corrections.reason: The record's target is 'agreement at least incumbent minus 1'; 'within 1 of incumbent' could be read as plus or minus 1.
