ideas.name: Turn sourced skills into pinned project agents
ideas.how: Each sourced skill is distilled into a .claude/agents file with prompt, tool list and pinned model; workflows and sessions call it by agent type.
ideas.problem: Our subagents lack domain knowledge (Android background work, Odoo, recovery, security review), and outside skills must reach them at the right price tier without each session loading everything by hand.
ideas.stands: Built: applied to 11 agent definitions [M] on draft PR #185, not merged. Not yet run, so no results. The design notes Haiku could take extractors, scans and table generation.
ideas.next: Decide on merging PR #185, call the agents from workflows and measure; source the four priority-1 skills.

ideas.name: Agent file: pinned model, tools, preloaded skill
ideas.how: Frontmatter sets name, tools, model (haiku, sonnet or opus), preloaded skills and effort; the body is a read-only, cite-everything system prompt with a named return schema.
ideas.problem: A subagent inherits the session's model and loads nothing unless told, so its role, price tier and tool access need to be fixed in one file.
ideas.stands: Built: 11 fixflow agent definitions [M] plus the explorer on draft PR #185; fields checked against the Claude Code docs on 2026-11-03. Not yet run.
ideas.next: Call the agents from a workflow and measure.
ideas.origin: Skills packages; Claude Code subagent feature

ideas.name: Skill package layout with provenance files
ideas.how: Each package has a SKILL.md, an UPSTREAM.md (repo, commit, paths, licence, taken/changed/rejected), the verbatim licence and references, kept under about 150 KB [S].
ideas.problem: Skills copied from other repos must stay traceable, licensed and small enough to load, so a maintainer can tell what was taken, changed and rejected.
ideas.stands: Built: applied to all 13 packages [M] on draft PR #185, conventions written 2026-11-03/04. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Check each package against the size and layout rules before merge.

ideas.name: Three skill statuses: sourced, authored, researched
ideas.how: Every package carries one status word in the index: adapted from an upstream repo, written here, or written here from fetched web sources with URL and date.
ideas.problem: A reader needs to know whether a skill's facts came from an outside repo, were written by us, or were gathered from the web.
ideas.stands: Built: the index on draft PR #185 lists 10 sourced, 1 researched and 2 authored packages [M]. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Keep the index current as packages are added.

ideas.name: FixFlow facts first, cited to path and line
ideas.how: Generic advice shrinks to a rule and its reason; space goes to repo specifics. Every claim is cited to path and line, web facts to URL and fetch date.
ideas.problem: Generic outside advice wastes tokens and can mislead agents on this repo, and stale line numbers or vague dates make claims impossible to check.
ideas.stands: Built: the rule set is applied across the packages on draft PR #185; facts were re-read on 2026-11-04. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Spot-check the cited lines after the next rebase.

ideas.name: Skills never contradict CLAUDE.md
ideas.how: Any upstream conflict with CLAUDE.md gets a 'Where upstream disagrees' block in the skill and a 'Rejected' line in the provenance file.
ideas.problem: Imported skills carry rules, such as deleting failed queue writes, that would break our project's invariants if an agent obeyed them.
ideas.stands: Built into three skills (offline sync review, Expo release, self-hosting) on draft PR #185. Example: an upstream rule to delete failed queue writes was rejected, since our outbox never deletes a write. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Keep using it as new skills are added.
ideas.flag: Record states no next step; next-step text is an editorial default.

ideas.name: No secrets in skills: key names and fingerprints
ideas.how: Files holding real values are cited by path and key name only; a committed value is shown as a 12-character hash fingerprint. Agents may not open .env files.
ideas.problem: Agents reading config files such as eas.json or .env could copy real tokens or keys into skills, briefs or outputs.
ideas.stands: Built: written into every agent definition read in this lane (draft PR #185). Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Keep using it.
ideas.flag: Record maps to SK-3 (B12 by alias); PR-SECRETS fits the problem better.

ideas.name: Read the skill first, even when preloaded
ideas.how: Every agent body opens with an instruction to read its SKILL.md and references first, even though the skills field already preloads it.
ideas.problem: A host that does not preload skills would leave the agent without its rules, so the agent must fetch them itself.
ideas.stands: Built: present in every agent definition read (draft PR #185). Not yet tested. CLAUDE.md loads into custom subagents by default.
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: Orchestration skill and repo-conventions skill
ideas.how: One project skill carries the context block, schemas, reading rules and routing table; a second packages CLAUDE.md and the deploy traps for implementation sessions.
ideas.problem: Every session's agents need identical briefs, and implementers need the deploy traps, migration numbering and slice boundaries put in front of them.
ideas.stands: Built in part: the orchestration skill is authored on draft PR #185 (see the main-session contract skill). The repo-conventions skill is not confirmed built. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Confirm whether the repo-conventions skill exists; merge decision on PR #185.
ideas.flag: Record says idea, but another record shows the orchestration half authored on PR #185; status raised to built. Overlaps method#42.

ideas.name: fixflow-explorer Haiku-pinned locator agent
ideas.how: A read-only agent pinned to Haiku greps first, reads at most 40 lines [S], and reports path and line for each match, with no verdicts.
ideas.problem: The built-in Explore agent inherits the session's model (Opus here), so a simple where-is-X lookup runs on our most expensive tier.
ideas.stands: In use: the agent file exists in the repo and predates PR #185. No usage or cost figures yet.
ideas.next: Measure its cost against the built-in Explore agent.
ideas.flag: Sources show the file exists but no usage figures; kept as in use.

ideas.name: Android background-execution skill and analyst
ideas.how: A sourced skill on library internals and phone-maker autostart settings, paired with an Opus read-only analyst that returns cited findings and never claims field reliability without device evidence.
ideas.problem: The geofence, on-duty ping and job-travel tasks can fail silently on Android 12-15 and maker-customised phones, and analysts need cited facts on library internals.
ideas.stands: Built: skill and analyst on draft PR #185, not merged. Covers expo-location 18.0.10 [S], expo-task-manager 12.0.6 [S] and expo-modules-core 2.2.3 [S]. Not yet run.
ideas.next: Run it on plan phase P5-spike.

ideas.name: Odoo import and Pakistan accounting skills with analyst
ideas.how: A sourced Odoo skill (JSON-2, external IDs as idempotency key, reversals) plus a researched Pakistan books skill; an Opus analyst preloads both.
ideas.problem: Money postings must reach Odoo exactly once with Pakistan tax records right, since wrong guesses double-post or drop entries.
ideas.stands: Built: two skills and one agent on draft PR #185, not merged. Every Pakistan fact carries a URL and date. Not yet run.
ideas.next: Use it in phases P9-0a and P9-0b; owner and accountant decide the tax position.

ideas.name: CI check for skill and agent frontmatter
ideas.how: A Node CI step fails on bad skill frontmatter (name must equal folder, description present, at most 1024 characters [S]) and agent fields, and flags a stale head literal.
ideas.problem: Skill files can rot silently: a missing name, a name that differs from its folder, a stale Alembic head number.
ideas.stands: Adopted in the Horthy sweep, to be added to P1-ci or P1. Not yet built; a one-off version of the gate was run once.
ideas.next: A test commit dropping the name must fail CI; adopt for good if at least 1 [T] real rot is caught.

ideas.name: Phase-scoped skill trigger tally
ideas.how: At each phase close, search the session transcripts for skill calls and agents that preload a skill, and tabulate them against the phases each skill's description names.
ideas.problem: Skills may never load in the phases their descriptions name, and nothing shows it.
ideas.stands: Trial: to run over the first six phase sessions [T]. A cap and pruning were refuted in the sweep. Not yet run.
ideas.next: Tally across P0a, P0b, P1, P2a, P2b-1 and P2b-2 against the plan's phase table.

ideas.name: ks command-line tool plus skill as the agent interface
ideas.how: A zero-dependency Node command-line tool called through Bash (lookup, verify, show, outcome, claim, record, close), with a skill carrying the procedure.
ideas.problem: Subagents and workflow agents need one way into the knowledge store that works with no configuration or approval prompt.
ideas.stands: Designed in the knowledge-store design; nothing built. No hook in v1. A skill description at its ceiling would add about 620 tokens per call [E].
ideas.next: Build the tool in KS-2, the skill after; owner decides D15 (MCP wrapper) and D21 (edit-time hook).

ideas.name: Hooks: stop hook and tool-event heartbeat
ideas.how: Settings-based Claude Code hooks: a stop hook blocks a session on a failed claim check, and a heartbeat is fed by tool events.
ideas.problem: We want claims checked and progress shown automatically; today nothing blocks a session on a failed claim check or shows progress from tool events.
ideas.stands: Deferred: harness v2 keeps hooks off for now (decision D17). Root-gate versions of the same checks need no hook. No gain shown yet.
ideas.next: Owner decides D17 on reopening hooks for two uses.
ideas.flag: Could also sit in WP2 (heartbeat); placed in WP3 for the claim check.

ideas.name: Install BAML language and CLI in the harness
ideas.how: BAML generates a typed client and parses replies with schema-aligned parsing; the Claude Code route needs a canary-only client running one claude -p call per turn.
ideas.problem: We hoped for typed prompt functions, lenient parsing of agent outputs and built-in tests.
ideas.stands: Parked: not an install. Three grounds: a second billing path or opaque orchestrator, no resume in its runner, and its parser drops list elements silently. Its distinctive ideas are already done here more strictly.
ideas.next: Would come back only with a client running Claude Code subagents with tools and a recorded failure class it addresses.
ideas.flag: Record cites BML-1, which the alias table maps to B3-LOOP; that does not fit the typed-output problem, so left empty.

ideas.name: BAML for the FixFlow product's LLM features
ideas.how: The proof would pit pinned BAML v1 against the plain Anthropic SDK with strict tool output on 50-100 [S] real customer messages, scored on accuracy and dropped rows.
ideas.problem: If we ever approve a product LLM feature, such as reading customer messages, we would want its outputs structured reliably.
ideas.stands: Deferred: moot while no product LLM feature is planned. Not tested.
ideas.next: Nothing until an LLM feature is approved.

ideas.name: Android field-debugging skill and device debugger agent
ideas.how: A sourced skill for read-only adb, dumpsys and logcat capture; a Sonnet agent returns a device-evidence table and never installs, clears, force-stops or judges reliability.
ideas.problem: The truth about geofencing and offline queues lives on phones, and the field APK is older than main, so reading code gives only candidates.
ideas.stands: Built: skill and agent on draft PR #185, not merged. Not yet run on a device.
ideas.next: Use it in drain sessions P4a and P4b.

ideas.name: Wrap conditional CLAUDE.md rules in 'important if'
ideas.how: Conditional rules are wrapped in important-if tags and always-true content left bare, as one arm of the CLAUDE.md adherence trial (E1), with 3 oblique probes [S].
ideas.problem: Long CLAUDE.md files get skimmed, and rules that matter only for certain tasks dilute the always-true ones.
ideas.stands: Trial: only as one arm of E1; the technique alone fell to the ruling that keeps every rule. Its adherence claims carry no measurements. Not yet run.
ideas.next: Run E1's wrapped arm with 10 direct and 3 oblique probes [S]; compare pass rate with the bare file.

ideas.name: Split CLAUDE.md by runtime with nested files
ideas.how: Move one-runtime material to backend and mobile CLAUDE.md files, keep every cross-runtime rule and a pointer index in the root. Test briefs and diff-only reviewers too.
ideas.problem: Our CLAUDE.md is 390 lines [M], about twice the length where adherence is known to fall, so every task pays for detail it may not need.
ideas.stands: Trial: a split arm of E1 on a branch. A nested file was seen attaching in a workflow subagent on Read here. Pass rate not yet compared.
ideas.next: Compare probe pass rate, split versus full, with the frozen probe set plus 3 oblique probes [S].

ideas.name: One-off sweep for contradicting instructions
ideas.how: One fresh Opus sweep after the 13 skills land, over CLAUDE.md, MEMORY.md, ship-plan section 0, orchestration sections 3 and 5 and each skill; a refuter checks every hit.
ideas.problem: Always-loaded instructions can contradict each other (CLAUDE.md points fresh sessions to the July handoff, not the ship plan), and fact-drift checks do not catch that.
ideas.stands: Trial: run once, no standing check. Each hit quotes both texts and the different action an agent would take. Not yet run.
ideas.next: Count refuter-confirmed contradictions and fix each at its source.

ideas.name: Local GPU speech-to-text for blocked recordings
ideas.how: Download audio-only streams and transcribe them with faster-whisper distil-large-v3 in a throwaway uv environment on the RTX 5070. Nothing is installed system-wide.
ideas.problem: YouTube blocks caption requests from this machine's address, so talks cannot be read from captions.
ideas.stands: In use: 9 recordings, about 7 hours, 172 MB [M], transcribed in about 12 minutes [M] on GPU at 19-45x real time [M]; CPU with other sessions loading managed 2.7x [M].
ideas.next: Reuse it for the 12-Factor Factories talk when published.

ideas.name: Recovery runbook skill and recovery operator agent
ideas.how: A sourced runbook covers dump inventory, paused-project restore policy and a restore into a throwaway Postgres 17 with count and sequence checks; a Sonnet agent runs only local steps.
ideas.problem: Production is down; we must find which database backups survive and prove a dump restores before rebuilding anything.
ideas.stands: Built: skill and Sonnet agent on draft PR #185, not merged. R2 listing and live restores stay with the owner. Not yet run.
ideas.next: Run it on P0a; I run the R2 listing and restores.
ideas.flag: Concerns the FixFlow product recovery rather than the PC; WP1 chosen as closest (work kept safe).

ideas.name: Self-hosting skill and architect agent
ideas.how: A sourced skill (restore-and-triage, tunnel guardrails) plus FixFlow's own design content; a Sonnet high-effort agent drafts compose files, owner step tables and local restore drills.
ideas.problem: Moving production to my own box needs compose, tunnel, backup and power-loss steps drafted and checked without agents touching the host.
ideas.stands: Built: skill and Sonnet agent on draft PR #185, not merged. I run every host step. Not yet run.
ideas.next: Use it for P3a.
ideas.flag: Could sit in WP1 (backups, power loss); placed in WP9 as a real-host rehearsal.

ideas.name: A ks guide command printed from command definitions
ideas.how: The guide command would print guidance from the same command definitions as the tool, with a test that every subcommand appears.
ideas.problem: We worried knowledge-store documentation could drift from the tool's real commands.
ideas.stands: Parked: the tool and its skill live in one repo and one commit, so version skew cannot arise; the store is also unbuilt. Not tested.
ideas.next: Nothing; would return only if the tool and its skill were ever shipped separately.
ideas.flag: Return condition is an inference from the refutation, not stated in the record.

ideas.name: [owner] stop markers in agent procedures
ideas.how: Steps only I may do are marked [owner] in skills; the agent stops there, hands over the exact command or table, and resumes only from output I paste back.
ideas.problem: Agents must never deploy, restore over live data, rotate keys, message people or install on a phone; those steps need me.
ideas.stands: Built: used in all 13 skills [M] and the agent definitions on draft PR #185. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: Orchestration contract skill for the main session
ideas.how: An authored skill the main session loads each phase: routing table, agent registry, context block, schemas, reading rules, script contract and plan rules. Not preloaded into subagents.
ideas.problem: The main session must recall tier routing, output schemas and session rules each phase without re-reading long design documents.
ideas.stands: Built: authored on 2026-11-04 from the design and ship plan; on draft PR #185, not merged. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Keep using it.

check.notes: Checked all 28 entries against chunk-skills-1.md, register-ids.md and packages.md; no cited source line was opened because every number and claim was confirmable from the records. Most corrections are word-limit trims (how, problem, stands, next). Substantive corrections are as follows. skills#9 status and maturity were lowered from in_use/5 to built/3, since the records show only that the agent file exists, with no usage figures and 'not yet tested'. skills#18 bottleneck W1 was dropped in favour of LIB-S5, because W1 does not fit the access-path problem. memory#27 'known to fall' was softened to 'said to fall'. memory#38's next step had an invented return condition; the record says 'None'. Several 'Keep using it' next steps implied current use of untested items. Third-person 'owner' phrases were changed to first person. Numbers and tags matched the records throughout; the only untagged figure found was skills#6's 12-character fingerprint, now tagged [S]. No raw record describing a distinct mechanism was lost in any merge, so there are no splits. The only dropped detail is that slash-path citations only warn in the skills#12 CI check, which is minor. skills#8 was left at built/3 with its partial-build wording and its flag, because method#42 confirms the orchestration half is authored; the repo-conventions half is still only designed. skills#8 overlaps method#42.

ideas.name: Zero-seed first-use walk in every gate
ideas.how: Each gate runs install, first user, tills, a real-shaped import, one transaction and close of day on a fresh container database with no seeder.
ideas.problem: Gaps surfaced only on the last day: nobody walked a clean install, so the app refusing real data and missing tills stayed hidden.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 phase 4; not built. Adds 2 to 3 minutes [E] per gate and needs phase 2. Half of B02 was closed on 11 November.
ideas.next: Build the journey on a fresh container database, then replay it on the 11 November gap after phase 2.
ideas.origin: Bottleneck compile; Harness v2 design; Clinic testbed
ideas.flag: Sources differ (designed vs idea); I took designed because harness v2 phase 4 specifies it. Target [T]: the walk fails on the commit before the 11 November merge and passes after.

ideas.name: Rented-host rehearsal
ideas.how: Free steps first with me present for one administrator prompt (restore, deploy checklist, off-site push, planted alert), then one rented-host day on made-up data.
ideas.problem: Nothing we built has run on a real host, so certificates, off-site backups, alerts and restore are unproven outside my PC.

ideas.name: Local staging VM rig with fifteen drills
ideas.how: Script-built Hyper-V Debian VM (2 vCPU [S], 2 GB [S]), versioned releases, fifteen re-runnable drills: deploy, upgrade, backup and restore, load, security probe, reboot.
ideas.problem: We had never tested restore, deploy, upgrade or failure behaviour outside development, and had no production-like host to rehearse on.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed, synthetic data: fresh VM serving in 109 s [M], upgrade 7 s [M], 781,505 rows restored in 14 s [M], security probe 99 pass, 0 fail [M].
ideas.next: Run the fresh-VM restore and first-deploy checklist with me present; reuse clean-install-first and restore row-checksum compare in FixFlow.
ideas.flag: The Hyper-V rig does not transfer to FixFlow; the drill structure does. Each VM start needs an administrator prompt. Drills also found their own harness faults.

ideas.name: Volume load and page-speed drill
ideas.how: Grow synthetic data through the app's services, time each persona's pages, make reads set-based, count queries at two sizes, hash page bodies before and after.
ideas.problem: Pages were slow at volume, it was unknown whether 12 concurrent users worked, and an optimisation had to be proved not to change figures.
ideas.stands: Measured in the testbed: pages 9-13 s down to 0.1-0.5 s at 75,016 documents [M]; queries on one page 29,346 to 28 [M]. The 12-clerk load run was not repeated after the fix.
ideas.next: Rerun the 12-clerk drill on current main, then a bulk generator to 250,000 [T] stock movements, then the rented host.
ideas.flag: The 12-clerk drill failed before the fix: 11,000-110,000 ms over 809 requests [M]. Real limits are provable only on a rented host. The query-count method applies to FastAPI N+1 loops.

ideas.name: List of what never ran on a real host
ideas.how: A 'cannot be proven here' list: off-site store, certificates, hosted CPU speed, alerts, second-host restore, second maintainer, each tied to a closing drill.
ideas.problem: We want to stop assuming that local rehearsal proved how things behave on a real host.

ideas.next: Keep the list in the handoff and name one closing command per drill; I choose a host and pilot frame.
ideas.flag: Records also tie it to B03 (second maintainer); I kept to the two closest ids. Off-site and second-host restore are the items most likely to be missed again.

ideas.how: A native emulator (Windows Hypervisor Platform) runs three scripted protocols: drain rehearsal, adb field steps, offline matrix. Lab builds cannot reach a real server.
ideas.problem: Drain logic and field-reliability steps meet a real phone with real data without any earlier rehearsal, and Docker has no /dev/kvm to run an emulator.
ideas.stands: Designed; L3a started 13 November, stacked on L2. The emulator boots on this PC with the lab app installed. No check run yet; each must be shown failing once.

records.potential: First-use failures caught at every gate instead of on the last day; the walk should fail on the commit before 11 Nov and pass after.
records.first_step: Add a zero-seed journey against a fresh container database to every gate: install, first user, tills, import, transaction, close.
records.state_note: Real-data switch merged; walk unbuilt (v2 phase 4)
records.verified_note: Compile §1 confirms the 11 Nov merge and synthetic drill; machine-facts saw it staged earlier that day. Dropped the five-flag figure: it belongs to the corpus map.

records.name: The PC powers off without warning
records.what: The PC shuts down unexpectedly and stops all agent work. Most events leave no crash code and many came with no Claude activity; the cause is not yet found.
records.evidence: 24 since 7 Oct, 23 without crash code [M] (compile); 25 since 1 Oct, 15 with no Claude call ten minutes before [M] (phase 1). 13 Nov: off 28 minutes, eight lanes cut [M].
records.potential: The next event leaves a trace naming its cause; zero sleep-related events in 14 days [T]; push checkpoints make every stop cheap to recover.
records.first_step: Turn off sleep on mains, add a temperature, power and memory logger, decode the 7 Oct dump, note mains cuts.
records.state_note: Join done; logger awaits owner install; v2 phase 1
records.verified_note: Checked machine-facts.md:7-8, phase-1 FINDINGS.md:27-38 and ship plan §7.4. Both counts kept with their windows; build load explains at most 6 [M].

records.name: The check is slow on Windows
records.what: On Windows the test runner reaches the database through Docker Desktop's published port, so workers wait on that network hop instead of using the CPU.
records.evidence: 0.63 ms vs 0.13 ms per trivial query; workers about 40 % busy [M]. Whole check 367.2 s on Windows vs 230.1 s in the Linux container, 1.6x [M].
records.potential: A median gate near 230 s [T], about 1.6x faster than the Windows gate [M], with Linux parity (B18) in the same move.
records.first_step: Decide D09: make the container run the gate; run Windows only when Windows-side tools change.
records.state_note: Container run built, not the gate; waits on D09
records.verified_note: Corrected 1.5x to 1.6x per compile §2.1 (367.2 vs 230.1 s); the clinic task record says about 1.5x against 350 s. Port-hop cause confirmed (§1, card A3-10).

records.name: Checks queue behind each other
records.what: Check capacity is slots divided by run time; past that, lanes queue. The second slot opens only with 8 GiB free, so in practice there is one.
records.evidence: 19 recorded waits: median 409 s, longest 2,030 s [M]. 8 GiB never free in about 980 samples [M]. Two slots measured at 1.8-1.9x throughput [M].
records.potential: Median wait under a minute [T]; a second slot open on at least half the polls [T]; up to 1.8-1.9x check throughput [M].
records.first_step: Measure one check's peak memory, set slots from it, add a fair queue with a printed position.
records.state_note: Memory guard only; harness v2 phase 2
records.verified_note: Median 409 s is design.json's median of 19 waits; 2,030 s and 980 samples in compile §1. Refuter's 3-742 s range and the list's 34 minutes remain conflicts.

records.name: Memory is short on this PC
records.what: RAM, not CPU, sets how many check slots, sessions and lanes can run at once; nobody has yet split memory use by process group during a build.
records.evidence: Clinic: 2-6 GiB available, lows 0.0-0.8 GiB with two checks [M]; browser 6.1, WSL2 5.2, Claude 3.2 GB [M]. FixFlow, 13 Nov: 5.5-7.7 of 31 GB free, eight lanes [M].
records.potential: A table of who holds memory when under 2 GB [T] is free, so slots, caps and lane counts come from evidence.
records.first_step: Run one build day with a per-process-group memory sampler, then choose a shared test database, a WSL2 cap, or closing apps.
records.state_note: Open in clinic; FixFlow capped at eight sessions
records.verified_note: Checked map-full.txt:291, machine-facts.md:22 and ship plan §7.4. Idle sessions and 26 containers were not shown to be the main consumers (25 stopped).

records.name: A check hung with no named cause
records.what: A parallel check pass stalled and the watchdog killed it, with no signal naming the running test. The stall has not been reproduced.
records.evidence: Stall limit 600 s [S]. The one real stall was killed after 961 s, whole check 1,116 s [M]. A 754 s run was a planted dying-worker demo, not a second hang [M].
records.potential: The next stall names its test and cause; the stall limit can drop to about 120 s [T] once 20 loaded runs [T] show no false kills.
records.first_step: Make the heartbeat record the running test, dump worker stacks on a stall, check Windows sleep/wake records.
records.state_note: Bounded by watchdog; not reproduced; v2 phase 2
records.verified_note: map-full.txt:326 and card A3-09 confirm 961 s/1,116 s; sweep-cards:247 shows 754 s was a demo. Dropped the 14,227 s gap: a Codex-eval host sleep.

records.name: Nothing restarts after a reboot
records.what: After a restart, Docker and the databases stay down until started by hand; in FixFlow a stopped Docker engine blocks every backend gate and dump restore.
records.evidence: Docker AutoStart off; 31 of 34 containers have restart policy 'no' [M]. Restarted by hand on 9 Nov (clinic) and 13 Nov (FixFlow, after the power loss).
records.potential: Databases healthy within 3 minutes [T] of sign-in with no command; backend gates and restores no longer wait on a person.

records.name: The work exists only on this PC
records.what: The clinic repository has no remote and no off-machine copy, and parts of its work are uncommitted; the planned knowledge store would also start on one disk.
records.evidence: 432 commits, 19 worktrees, 36 branches, 55 MB packed, no remote, only drive C: [M]. Six untracked paths a bundle would miss [M]. No second drive attached (11 Nov).

records.potential: Worktree and container counts return to the active slices plus one after each merge [T]; no session lost to clean-up.

records.name: Docker network address pools exhausted

records.verified_note: Ship plan §7.4 and §7.8 (be2e27a). Appendix C still creates a network; verify-dump.sh is its working form.

records.name: Antivirus blocks toolchain files

records.name: Unfair gate queue starved FixFlow lanes
records.what: Random retries let later arrivals jump the gate queue, and exclusive Android builds at the head held up short runs. This is FixFlow's version of B07.
records.evidence: One lane waited 20 minutes while later arrivals were served; two exclusive Android builds held eight short runs for most of an hour [M].
records.potential: Predictable first-come waits for every lane; a heavy job cannot starve once it has waited 900 s [S].

records.verified_note: ff-slot.sh header lines 21-27 confirm both measurements and the 900 s patience default.

records.name: Gate runs take minutes
records.what: The backend gate stack is the slowest check a lane runs, and it queues for a slot; gates also set the elapsed time of discovery workflow W1.
records.evidence: Backend 7 min 23 s cold with 757 tests; web 33 s; mobile 29 s warm [M]. W1 gate wall-clock estimated at 25-40 min [E].
records.potential: Short inner loops that run only the tests in hand, with full gate runs kept for merge-readiness.

records.state_note: Accepted; inner runs limited by arguments
records.verified_note: Ship plan §7.8 L1 baseline table and orchestration design §7 cost row checked.

records.name: No native Android compile gate

records.evidence: Native compile time not yet measured. 0 testID or accessibilityLabel hits in technician-app/src [M].
records.potential: A compile check in minutes instead of an EAS queue, answering the SDK 52 background-location build question before any phone is involved.

records.verified_note: Ship plan §7.5 L2 (unticked) and SKILLS-PACKAGES line 921 (0 hits, verified by command).

records.name: No Android emulator inside Docker

records.evidence: 0 svm flags in the Docker VM [M]. A native emulator booted Android 14 on 13 Nov, holding 3.8 GB of host RAM [M].
records.potential: A device lab on this PC, using an RTX 5070 that has no other job in the program.

records.state_note: Native emulator boots under WHPX (13 Nov)
records.verified_note: Updated: ship plan §7.5 records the boot at 14:38 on 13 Nov with the lab app installed, so the boot proof is done.

records.evidence: One major refuter finding on 13 Nov [M]; the handoff (§2.4) records the deadlock.

records.potential: Fewer false defects, and gates that reproduce what production actually ran.

records.evidence: Not sized. The folder would make EAS treat the app as bare and skip config plugins.

records.verified_note: Orchestration design §8 line 599 and ship plan §7.5 L2 (prebuild inside the container) checked.

records.evidence: Tool timeout 600,000 ms per command [S].
records.potential: Safe retries after a timeout, with no duplicated containers, writes or runs.

records.state_note: Rule plus fixed names make second starts fail
records.verified_note: Orchestration design §8 lines 619-622: re-check rule and fixed container names that fail a second start.

records.verified_note: Horthy doc line 418 (G5-F024) checked in the extracted branch copy.

records.what: When other sessions run test suites on all cores, CPU side jobs slow sharply; GPU work was the one thing not slowed.

records.evidence: Fixed with a 1.26 GB Linux image [M]; 172 MB of Windows copies sit unused [M]. Timing aborted twice under CPU load; the session died twice.

register.notes:
I checked all 37 records against the sources they cite, in the repository, in the extracted branch documents and in the memory notes. Corrections:
- B06: the speed-up is 1.6x, not 1.5x (compile §2.1: 367.2 s vs 230.1 s). The clinic task record's own "about 1.5x" compares against 350 s.
- B20: the page timings were p50 109-468 ms with no page above 524 ms at p95. The figure "drill e 11,000-110,000 ms" is in no source, so I replaced it with the last 12-clerk run, which predates the fix: posting p50 3.4-7.5 s, p95 up to 16 s.
- B09: the 754 s run was a planted dying-worker demo, not a second hang. I removed the 14,227 s gap (a host sleep during a Codex evaluation) from the evidence.
- B02: I removed the five "claim without attested premise" flags. They belong to the corpus-map ledger, not to B02.
- B3-LOOP: "14 in October" and "14 in 15 days" are the same 6-20 Oct count (CR-03), so there is no conflict.
- PR-FIELDEVIDENCE: main is 10 commits past the handoff. The field APK is older than main, but by how much is not recorded.
- MC-NOEMU: the emulator booted on 13 Nov (ship plan §7.5), so the boot-proof step is done and the record is closed.
- MC-SHAREDDB: the fix was proved by a refused second run (exit 4), so the record is closed.
- MC-TOOLS: the orchestration design states both "no Python on PATH" and "one exists at the Codex path", so this is not a conflict. The Android tools were installed on 13 Nov.

records.name: Fix rounds that create new defects
records.what: Our fixes added new stored state (a hold, lock, marker or cutoff) whose endings nobody tested, so each fix round produced fresh P1s and rounds never converged.
records.evidence: Round one: 19 P1 [M]; fixes then made at least 5 more P1 and 10 P2 [M]. 64 % of reviews sent a slice back, 2.8 rounds per slice [M].
records.potential: Review rounds that converge under a stop rule, shown as fewer fix-made defects per fixed finding than the testbed's rate.
records.first_step: Replay a fix-round contract (two-round cap, revert, fresh reviewer, state-ending table) sealed against the recorded defect chains.
records.state_note: Harness v2 phase 3; replay not run
records.verified_note: 19 P1, 5+ P1, 10 P2, 64 %, 2.8 checked in compile 3.3 and v2 loop R1. Dropped the 1.25x bound and context-system counts (other work).

records.name: Everything stops when I am away
records.what: Nothing restarts without me: Docker and sessions stay down after a power-off, parked sessions wait for my message, and a resumed session can drift from its record.
records.evidence: About three days idle after the 6 Nov power-off at 14:58 [M]; no commits 7-8 Nov [M]; three more power-offs followed [M]. A 1 Oct limit stall lasted 3 h 06 min [M].
records.potential: Idle time between 'could resume' and the next commit falls from about three days [M] to under three hours [T].
records.first_step: Build the restart chain and a resume list at sign-in; release sessions two at a time.
records.state_note: D06 answered; harness v2 phase 1 not built
records.verified_note: Power-off 14:58:23 after the 14:57 commit, three later power-offs and the 1 Oct 3 h 06 min stall confirmed in compile and bottleneck map.

records.name: One orchestrator is the serial gate
records.what: One root session reviews, merges, edits the board and runs checks, so it caps how fast work leaves, and its window keeps overflowing and being summarised.
records.evidence: Root compacted at 574k, 974k, 967k and 970k tokens [M]; a second reading counts three [M]. Root is 15.3 % of November tokens, about 499k per call [M].
records.potential: No compaction across a wave of five gates [T]; the gain is bounded because the root is 15.3 % of tokens [M].
records.first_step: Move review into a gate workflow with a typed verdict naming the head SHA; merge through a locked local queue.
records.state_note: Harness v2 phase 3; gate workflow not built
records.verified_note: Compactions, 15.3 % and 499k confirmed in compile and tally; three-versus-four conflict kept. Dropped October session peaks; 300-400k is an aim, not a result.

records.name: Agent reports overstate what was done
records.what: Session and agent reports claimed tests, evidence or runs that did not exist or did not match, and model re-checks did not stop it.
records.evidence: 20-plus recorded overstatements, with no denominator [M]. S11 round 2 had two claims its cited evidence did not support [M]. Owner reviews corrected model counts three times [M].
records.potential: Claims anyone can recheck by script, flagging recorded overstatements with false flags under 10 % [T], so the root stops re-verifying by hand.
records.first_step: Build a claims file checked by script, record-only with an allow-list, and replay it over recorded gates.
records.state_note: Harness v2 phase 3; claims script not built
records.verified_note: 20-plus, S11 round 2 and three owner corrections confirmed. Removed '4 of 579 quotes': those were an unfetchable source, not overstatements.

records.name: Shared documents have one writer
records.what: The root hand-edits one large board at every merge, and routing documents and model-written state files go stale.
records.evidence: Board 829 lines, 219,111 bytes at sweep time; 838 lines on 11 Nov; 221 KB in the compile [M]. AGENTS.md grew from 6,709 to 10,698 bytes [M].
records.potential: Board under 20 KB [T] and zero root edits at merge [T], from per-slice state fragments and a generated board.
records.first_step: Write per-slice state fragments, a board generator, and a merge script that applies the generated board diff.
records.state_note: Harness v2 phase 3; not built
records.verified_note: Board and AGENTS.md sizes checked in sweep cards and map; 221 KB likely the later board. Removed 4,053 endpoints, which belong to a corpus map.

records.name: I cannot see progress
records.what: During long calls I get no sign whether work is waiting, running or stalled, nor its queue position or the test running.
records.evidence: A check may wait up to 2,700 s [S] for a slot before a 5-18 minute run; one 49-minute foreground polling loop is on record [M].
records.potential: The longest gap between heartbeats under 60 s [T]; I see waiting, running or stalled at a glance.
records.first_step: The check writes a heartbeat file with queue position; checks run in the background, never polled in the foreground.
records.state_note: Harness v2 phase 2; not built
records.verified_note: 2,700 s is check.py's slot-wait cap, so tagged [S]; 49-minute loop confirmed. The 'frozen display' was most likely one long call.

records.name: Agent reports flow through the orchestrator
records.what: Subagents' full reports return into the root's context instead of files, so the root fills; the 'subagents cannot write' belief was itself an unchecked report.
records.evidence: Root runs about 499k tokens of context per call [M]. Subagents made 82.4 % of 4,155 October calls [M]. A probe showed a subagent writes and reads back a file [M].
records.potential: Zero refused writes over 20 runs [T]; a smaller root window, and gate decisions that fit in it.

records.state_note: Premise corrected; harness v2 phase 3; D13 pending
records.verified_note: Write probe, 499k (November root) and 82.4 % (October, 4,155 calls) confirmed in compile and map; dates added to separate the two periods.

records.name: Nobody reads the final commit
records.what: All review is a model reading a model's code, and high-risk branches merged with their final head commit unread by anyone.
records.evidence: 4 of 5 merges on 10 Nov unread [M]; 5 of 6 high-risk final heads unread [M]. Round three was the root alone in 9 of 11 gates [M].

records.state_note: Harness v2 phase 3; FixFlow reviews bind head SHA
records.verified_note: Counts confirmed in compile 1 and v2 table (different merge sets). Dropped '21 attacks, none closed by a human': that came from a corpus-map review.

records.name: Minor findings pile up uncounted
records.what: Low-priority P3 findings were carried forward with no status column, so nobody can count how many are still open.

records.verified_note: 111 and 183 confirmed in compile 1 and harness v2 mechanism 4.

records.name: The pile-up after a stop
records.what: A waiting lane keeps holding its context; after a stop every lane is released at once and all queue again for the same check slot.

records.potential: Lanes released two at a time with waits parked outside sessions, so a restart no longer recreates the queue.

records.what: A refuted fix or known defect pattern raises no error and can merge silently; a warning joined on file paths alone fires too often to read.

records.verified_note: Ship plan 7 and owner view confirm; 16 items, done needs 1-4, 6, 10, 12. Kit orders item 1 first, owner view item 10.

records.name: Agent work waits on my actions

records.verified_note: BAML card D-13 confirms 8 of 12 and the probe; orchestration design confirms the inertia guard.

records.verified_note: Design changelog accepts the critique; BAML confirms two design lines still stale against v3.

records.what: A brief's inputs are the live repo and the web, so regression-testing a brief edit costs many Opus runs, our scarcest resource.
records.evidence: 60-180 agent runs per brief edit [E].
records.potential: A cheap regression path, so we can edit briefs with confidence.

records.state_note: Parked; no brief edit has flipped a verdict
records.verified_note: BAML line 74 confirms the 60-180 runs estimate and the parking condition.

records.name: Agents start without the settled facts
records.what: Agents were briefed before settled facts existed: G2 analysts fell back on hypotheses, sweep assessors lacked design rules, and a lane could read uncommitted plan text.

records.verified_note: Harness review line 265 confirms; docs/program/evidence holds w1, w2 and manifest.sha256.

records.potential: Entries can still lead when I paste the build or deploy log, and races become checkable through tests that encode them.
records.first_step: Let ks lookup --log accept pasted logs; write a race-encoding test per such entry.
records.state_note: accepted limit; designed as candidates only
records.verified_note: KS design lines 515-516 checked.

records.name: Word lookup misses reworded symptoms
records.what: A word-matching lookup misses a symptom sharing no word with any stored handle, and misses are counted only when a later record examines them.
records.evidence: Expected below about 0.2 [E] counted misses per 8-week window. The zero-shared-terms classifier misclassed 6 of 7 [M] measured paraphrase misses.
records.potential: Recovers vocabulary misses and gives a measured trigger for adding embeddings (D16).
records.first_step: Build the missed-existing writer with the KS-2 fixtures.
records.state_note: accepted limit; writer and classifier designed
records.verified_note: KS design lines 522 and 915 checked.

records.name: Each store lookup costs time and tokens
records.what: Checking the index against the journal each call takes time; each Bash lookup re-reads the caller's context, and the skill description rides every call.
records.evidence: 23-35 ms [M] at 5k entries, 57-87 ms [M] at 20k; 49-55 ms [M] with 4-8 callers. 2,000 characters cost about 860 [M] tokens; skill description about 620 [M].
records.potential: Lookups cheap enough to run routinely; the routine adds about three fixed turns per phase.
records.first_step: A benchmark test that fails above 50 ms [S] at 5k entries; one total output cap.
records.state_note: bound benchmarked; store not built
records.verified_note: KS design lines 789 and 794 checked; 49-55 ms with concurrent callers exceeds the 50 ms bound.

records.name: Private data reaches the model provider
records.what: Everything an agent reads reaches Anthropic under my account terms, and customer names and addresses slip past local pattern scrubbing.
records.evidence: A documented known miss for names and addresses. The design assumes a consumer account with 30-day [S] retention until I state otherwise.
records.potential: A safe store by structural rule: no raw production data, only templates with typed placeholders.
records.first_step: I state the account type (D7); keep a known-miss fixture in every test run.
records.state_note: mitigated by rule; D7 awaits my answer
records.verified_note: KS design lines 211, 550, 584 and D7 (line 706) checked.

records.name: Cross-runtime contracts break silently
records.what: Client calls to routes, settings keys, the migration chain, slice contracts, outbox kinds and file-bound invariants are not imports, so search and import graphs miss them.
records.evidence: A script matched 65 of 73 [M] client URL literals to 77 [M] route decorators; 46 [M] settings keys; 46 [M] migration links.
records.potential: A scripted contract map as a review input could show what a change might break; its value is unproven.
records.first_step: Zero-token test of the contract map on the recorded defect chains.
records.state_note: partly mapped by script; value unproven
records.verified_note: HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS section 6, contracts bullet, matches.

records.name: Hub files make impact lists too long
records.what: The files that change most are hubs with many dependants, so a raw list of everything downstream is too long to use.
records.evidence: 42 % [M] of code-file changes and 73 % [M] of code commits touch a file with reach over 15; median reach is 2 [M].
records.potential: Depth limits, grouping and a hub cut keep touch lists near 15 [T] files, small enough for a reviewer.
records.first_step: Add a depth limit and grouping to the touch list; check list size on recorded fixes.
records.state_note: measured; partly handled in graph tuning
records.verified_note: HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS section 6, reach bullet, matches; 15-file bound from the touch-list test rule.

records.name: Test sets too small for small gains
records.what: Our graph test's held-out set can detect only large differences, so 'inconclusive' is a likely and honest result rather than a failure.
records.evidence: 75 [M] held-out commits; smallest detectable recall difference about 0.09 [E]; detecting 0.05 needs about 110 [E] paired commits.
records.potential: A larger or rolling-origin task set would let the test resolve the 0.05 [T] difference we care about.
records.first_step: Rerun rolling-origin over several split dates; report 'inconclusive' as no evidence either way.
records.state_note: handled in the frozen protocol; limit remains
records.verified_note: HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS section 6, CureFound line 67 and research critic.txt line 33 (110 commits) checked.

records.name: Graph gain is concentrated in mobile
records.what: On held-out commits the typed graph's lead over search comes from mobile-app seeds, and every arm lost recall from tuning to held-out.
records.evidence: Typed minus search on T1: mobile +0.151 [M], backend +0.012 [M], web +0.025 [M]. Mobile seeds rose from 17 % to 36 % [M]; every arm lost 0.06-0.17 [M].
records.potential: Knowing why mobile seeds gain shows where a typed graph pays, so we can use it there first.
records.first_step: Split every graph report by seed runtime and study the mobile cases.
records.state_note: measured 2026-11-13; unexplained
records.verified_note: Grader held-out notes lines 109-117 and result.json refuter detail checked.

records.name: Folder layout is already a strong baseline
records.what: In our vertical-slice layout folders already encode much connection information, and co-change history is thin, so any method must beat both simple floors.
records.evidence: On tuning no arm beat the co-change floor (0.752 [M]) by 0.05; directory floor 0.719 [M]. Held-out: typed beat co-change by +0.063 [M], fragile without five best commits.
records.potential: Fusing signals helped a few points (top-10 precision 0.28 vs 0.26 [M]); the floors keep every claim honest.
records.first_step: Always report results beside both floors.
records.state_note: floors built into every graph report
records.verified_note: Added held-out result from grader notes and result.json. '10,000 commits lost 13 points' is an outside study [S], not ours.

records.name: Graph-test answer keys can mislead
records.what: Using co-change history as the answer key favours arms that use co-change, and many changed files were new in that commit, so no store could return them.
records.evidence: 33-36 % [M] of changed files were added in the same unit; 15-19 % [M] of the rest lie beyond 5 hops.
records.potential: Questions read from the code give an answer key independent of the extractor, so arms are compared fairly.
records.first_step: Score only reachable answers and report the unreachable share for each arm.
records.state_note: mitigated in the frozen protocol
records.verified_note: graph2 research critic.txt line 37 checked.

records.name: Context aids never tested with an agent
records.what: No context aid (graph, map or recall journal) has run with an agent in the loop, so we do not know whether an agent finishes faster or with fewer mistakes.
records.evidence: 0 [M] agent runs; the held-out graph test (2026-11-13) used a fixed search script. A quality comparison was forecast at 156M-512M [E] tokens.
records.potential: Answers my real question: whether a graph, map or recall layer saves an agent work.
records.first_step: Agent-in-the-loop pilot on 24-30 fix commits, with a plain-notes control.
records.state_note: held-out scored by script; no agent run
records.verified_note: Addendum 6 line 63, sweep-cards 541/597/704 checked. State updated: held-out graded 2026-11-13. '0 of 30 map runs' not found.

records.name: Research sources blocked or still unread
records.what: YouTube captions, X posts and podcast transcripts were blocked, research agents can lack web tools, and some talks, threads and slides are still unread.
records.evidence: YouTube answered 429 [M] for five days; X returned 402 [M]. Nine recordings, about 7 hours, transcribed in about 12 minutes [M] of GPU time. 29 [M] items unread first pass.
records.potential: Fuller research coverage; the verifiers talk and the Twelve Factor Factories talk may bear on review backpressure (L3).
records.first_step: Reuse the routes that worked (local GPU transcription, fxtwitter for X); read the Twelve Factor Factories talk when available.
records.state_note: audio solved locally; X replies, LinkedIn, slides unread
records.verified_note: Horthy sweep lines 499, 609, 845-851, 887-899 checked. Five unread groups listed, not six.

records.name: Agent skills rest on unchecked facts
records.what: Some skill packages rest on unchecked facts: PostgreSQL lock-level claims come from FixFlow code comments, and Odoo-side unknowns stay open until fetched or answered.
records.evidence: Not measured. The skill packages mark both as UNVERIFIED or OPEN.
records.potential: Trustworthy migration review and exactly-once Odoo postings.
records.first_step: Fetch the PostgreSQL manual pages; I answer the Odoo questions in P9-0b.
records.state_note: open; no manual page fetched yet
records.verified_note: SKILLS-PACKAGES lines 420 and 773 checked.
