terms.definition: Open-source Python tool that builds a knowledge graph from a mixed corpus using tree-sitter. Its 71.5x [S] claim compares tokens per graph query with reading every raw file. Used as a comparator arm.
terms.origin: Outside project safishamsi/graphify; PyPI package graphifyy.
terms.note: Figure tagged [S] as an outside claim.

terms.term: Call graph / blast radius / touch list
terms.definition: A call graph maps which functions call which. Blast radius, or touch list, is the set of functions, callers, importers, co-changing files and tests a fix could affect, attached to a reviewer brief.
terms.origin: General software practice; the script is proposed in HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS section 6.

terms.definition: tree-sitter is a local code parser covering about 40 [S] languages. ast-grep searches code by syntax tree, built on it.
terms.origin: Outside open-source projects.
terms.note: Count tagged [S].

terms.definition: Tools that fail the build when code crosses forbidden module boundaries: dependency-cruiser for JavaScript, import-linter for Python.
terms.origin: Outside open-source tools.

terms.definition: A hand-written map of where each capability lives in each runtime of the FixFlow repository.
terms.origin: FixFlow repository docs (docs/CODE-MAP.md).
terms.note: Kept as the harness review treats it as the baseline map; flagged marginal.

terms.definition: Prompting schemes where the model writes several partial answers, then branches, votes or merges them. Reported gains were on puzzles with a 2023 model; not yet re-tested on current models.
terms.origin: Outside research papers.
terms.note: Replaced 'showed no gain on current models' with what the compile states: gains were old and untested on current models.

glossary.notes: Checked against the Horthy and BAML documents. Confirmed: backpressure blog date (2025-12-09), Ralph/Geoff Huntley, software-factory talk dates, fxtwitter and distil-large-v3, reasoning_extraction (Anthropic docs, so category changed from claude-code to models), GEPA from the DSPy authors, TypeChat from Microsoft, Collector added in BAML 0.79.0, card and family counts. Only 149 (Hypotheses H1-H18) dropped, as a FixFlow product item; no duplicates. Not verified in our sources, kept as general knowledge: Simon Willison coining "lethal trifecta" (confident), Amdahl's law, Hyper-V, METR figures (outside number, tagged [S]). Record 115 says G1-G4 but family ids run to G5; flagged in its note. Tags were added only where a number is from our own count [M], a setting [S], a target [T] or an estimate [E]; I did not invent any numbers.

terms.definition: An outside benchmark of real GitHub issues for coding agents. We cite it for fix-selection methods: voting alone among candidate patches resolved 25.7 % [S].
terms.origin: Outside benchmark, cited from the papers in our bottleneck research.
terms.note: Tagged the 25.7 % figure as an outside figure [S].

terms.definition: Spatial: a thing's neighbourhood in code and work. Temporal: when a fact became true and when it was replaced. Both are ways to look things up.
terms.origin: Coined by us in HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS-2026-11, section 6, 2026-11.
terms.note: Origin dated; wording simplified.

terms.definition: How often two files change in the same commit, used as a hint that they belong together. In the graph test it reached precision 0.26 [M] in a list of ten.
terms.origin: Software-evolution research; measured in our graph test.
terms.note: Source gives 0.26 as precision in a list of ten (tune commits), not recall; corrected and tagged [M].

terms.definition: A ranking that scores a node higher when well-linked nodes point to it. The personalised version restarts from a seed file so scores favour its neighbourhood. Aider's repo-map uses it.
terms.origin: Google's web-search ranking algorithm; used in the Aider tool.

terms.definition: Recall: share of true items found. Precision: share of returned items that are true. recall@8k: share of reference items inside an 8,000-token [S] answer, the graph test's main score.
terms.origin: Information-retrieval field.
terms.note: Tagged the 8,000-token budget [S].

terms.definition: One link step in a graph; three hops reaches things three links away from the starting point.
terms.origin: Graph theory.

terms.definition: Hub: a file many others depend on. Metapath: a typed route through the graph, such as calls, client URL, route, handler, then table write.
terms.origin: General graph field.

terms.definition: A graph whose nodes and links each carry a kind and evidence (file and line). Symbol-level means nodes are functions, classes and components rather than whole files.
terms.origin: General graph-database and code-analysis field.

terms.definition: A graph where a model reads text and code and writes meaning into it. A TKG also records when each fact became true and was superseded. Our parser-built graph was neither.
terms.origin: General AI field; outside systems such as Graphiti and Zep implement it.
terms.note: Category changed to general-cs: it is a general field term; outside tools are named in the origin.

terms.term: Graphiti / Mem0 / Letta / Zep / Copilot Memory
terms.definition: Outside agent-memory products we studied for ideas (two clocks, retire rather than delete, re-check when used) and for their failure modes.
terms.origin: Outside companies and open-source projects, studied in the knowledge-store research.
terms.note: Removed the aside about Graphiti elsewhere on this PC; not needed for the reader.

terms.term: GraphRAG / HippoRAG / RepoGraph / LocAgent / Aider repo-map
terms.definition: Outside systems that use graphs to help models retrieve or locate code, cited as prior art with mixed results. Aider's repo-map is a tree-sitter outline ranked by personalised PageRank.
terms.origin: Outside research papers and the Aider tool, as cited in our graph-test research.

terms.definition: LadybugDB 0.22.3 [S] is an embedded graph database, a maintained fork of Kuzu, whose upstream was archived in 2025. It was one graph-engine arm of the test.
terms.origin: Open-source projects; archive status as read in our graph-test research.
terms.note: Tagged the version [S].

terms.definition: DuckDB is an embedded analytical SQL database; DuckPGQ is its extension that adds property-graph queries.
terms.origin: DuckDB project and a community extension.
terms.note: Origin made plainer; the foundation claim was not in our sources.

terms.definition: A widely used graph database server (runs on the JVM). It was a candidate engine for the graph test but was not installed.
terms.origin: Neo4j, Inc.

terms.definition: SQLite is a small file-based database. FTS5 is its built-in full-text search with BM25 ranking. A recursive query follows links over several steps.
terms.origin: Open-source SQLite project.

terms.definition: The Linux Docker image, 1.26 GB [M], in which every graph-test arm runs so the arms share one environment.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the graph test engines-linux recipe, 2026-11.
terms.note: Tagged size [M].

terms.definition: The seed is the changed file or symbol given as the query. The reference is the other files and definitions the same commit changed.
terms.origin: Coined by us in graph2/protocol.md, 2026-11.

terms.term: T1 / T1x / T2 / T3 / T4 / T5 / TQ
terms.definition: Graph-test task sets: T1 change completion; T1x its cross-runtime subset; T2 changed code to tests; T3 documented chains; T4 defect register; T5 document lookups; TQ code-reading questions.
terms.origin: Coined by us in graph2/protocol.md, 2026-11.

terms.definition: Hypotheses declared before scoring: H1 and H2 engines equal; H1b community prior; H3 typed graph against baselines; H4 questions; H5 engine speed and size.
terms.origin: Coined by us in graph2 protocol addendum 3, 2026-11.

terms.definition: The 65 [S] June commits used to choose settings (tune) and the 75 [S] July-August commits scored once for the verdict (held-out).
terms.origin: General machine-learning practice; split defined in graph2/protocol.md.
terms.note: Tagged the commit counts [S].

terms.definition: A cheap baseline (same directory, plain co-change, or scripted search) that any graph method must beat to count as a gain.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the graph test protocol addendum 2, 2026-11.

terms.definition: The search baseline run as a fixed script. No agent decided what to search, and no agent was run in the held-out test.
terms.origin: Wording fixed by us in graph2 protocol addendum 6, 2026-11.
terms.note: Added the must-not-claim point: the search arm was a script, not an agent.

terms.definition: A stored grouping of related nodes, found by Louvain community detection, added to the ranking as a prior.
terms.origin: General graph-algorithm field.

terms.definition: A 95 % [S] interval from 10,000 [S] resamples by commit, and a permutation test for paired differences between arms.
terms.origin: General statistics.
terms.note: Tagged settings [S].

terms.definition: Rank-quality scores: mean reciprocal rank, normalised discounted cumulative gain at ten, and area under the recall-against-tokens curve.
terms.origin: Information-retrieval field.

terms.definition: Many random re-runs of a model, with unknown settings drawn from their ranges, to get a spread and a ranking instead of one answer.
terms.origin: General statistics.
terms.note: Closely related to n=271 (Ensemble / many runs); kept both, not exact duplicates.

terms.definition: A statistic showing how steadily one number rises or falls as another rises across runs; used to rank which unknowns move a result most.
terms.origin: General statistics, named for Charles Spearman.

terms.definition: Bounds on a rate from few trials: zero failures in n trials puts the true rate under about 3/n, so 0 in 40 gives 7.5 % [S]. Clopper-Pearson gives the exact one-sided bound.
terms.origin: Statistics field.
terms.note: Tagged the worked figure [S].

terms.term: P@1 / recall at shown / acted false positive
terms.definition: P@1: precision of the top result. Recall at shown: how many true entries appear in what is displayed. Acted false positive: a wrong lead someone acted on.
terms.origin: Information-retrieval metrics; applied in the knowledge-store design.

terms.definition: A calibration that removes one lookup key from an entry and checks the entry can still be found.
terms.origin: Information-retrieval evaluation style; named in knowledge-store research lane T-03.

terms.definition: A planned local database and command-line tool where agents record solved hard problems, traps and failed approaches and later look them up by symptom. Designed in PR #183, not built or proven.
terms.origin: Coined by us in KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md, 2026-11.
terms.note: Added 'or proven' to keep the designed-not-proven rule.

terms.definition: The journal is an append-only folder of immutable event files in git, the source of truth. The index is a disposable SQLite database rebuilt from it for fast lookups.
terms.origin: Event-sourcing pattern; chosen as proposal D in the knowledge-store design.

terms.definition: Entry: one stored lesson. Handle: a key it is found by (error template, symbol, paraphrase). Footprint: the files, settings and versions it depends on, used to notice staleness.
terms.origin: Coined by us; footprint adapted from build-system dependency tracking.

terms.definition: Lookup outcomes: a lead is a confident, gate-checked match; a candidate is a weaker one; a miss is nothing found. Abstention means answering nothing when unsure.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the knowledge-store design, 2026-11.

terms.definition: Planned retrieval thresholds: lead at 0.5 [T], candidate at 0.3 [T], margin 0.2 [T]. They decide lead, candidate or miss and are to be frozen at KS-4.
terms.origin: Coined by us (decision D8) in KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md.
terms.note: Tagged the thresholds as targets [T]; they are design values, not measured.

terms.term: Trace / early cutoff / control pair / inject-control
terms.definition: Trace: fingerprint of the footprint at the last passing check. Early cutoff: keep an entry if its check still passes after a dependency changed. Control pair: two commits where the check must read present, then absent. Inject-control re-applies the failing pattern.
terms.origin: Trace and early cutoff from Build Systems a la Carte (ICFP 2018); controls coined by us.
terms.note: Definition slightly over 30 words in sense only; kept tight. Outside origin confirmed in KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN T-01.

terms.term: Probe / mutant / probe-in-lookup / valid_when / tri-state verdict
terms.definition: A probe is a small automatic check that a root cause is present; a mutant is a harmless edit it must ignore. valid_when is a precondition. Verdicts: applies, not_applies, inconclusive.
terms.origin: Coined by us; mutant idea from mutation testing in software testing.
terms.note: Folded probe-in-lookup into the probe sentence's meaning (runs inside the lookup) by keeping the term name.

terms.term: Entry kinds (do_not_apply, open_defect, trap, unverified_seed, pending_anchor)
terms.definition: A forbidden change, an unfixed defect, a gotcha, an entry awaiting its executable check, and an entry whose fix sits on a branch, in that order.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the knowledge-store design, 2026-11.
terms.note: Added 'in that order' so the list maps to the five names.

terms.term: Write gate / diff lookup / false-fire ceiling / caller-pin test / second door
terms.definition: Write gate: checks on recording. Diff lookup (ks lookup --diff): warns when a PR touches protected code. False-fire ceiling: one commit in ten [T]. Caller-pin test: fixes allowed callers. Second door: a path that skips a guard.
terms.origin: Coined by us (KS-2, D8, D17; owner critique, 2026-11-03).
terms.note: Tagged the ceiling [T].

terms.definition: The knowledge store's planned build phases, one session each: audit, journal core, retrieval, gate, seed, pilot, Docker gates, wire-in, second host, checkpoint. KS-6b is the executable gate; KS-T is teardown.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the knowledge-store design, 2026-11.

terms.definition: Id prefixes in the design: rulings (R), adjudication (A), refuted claims (C), refuter amendments (F), critic amendments (K), owner critique O1..O20, refuter pass P1..P27, second-pass claims (V).
terms.origin: Coined by us in sections 12.1-12.8 of the knowledge-store design, 2026-11.

terms.definition: Numbered owner decisions, each with a default: D1 run the free audit, D1b build go-ahead, D16 embedding trigger, D17 CI caller-pin test, D22 guarded_refs.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the knowledge-store design, 2026-11.

terms.definition: Eight real past defects reconstructed from git history as first entries and test cases: ex6 correct-PIN lock, ex3 payment duplicate, ex4 dispatcher cursor, ex7 and ex8 Expo build traps.
terms.origin: Coined by us in knowledge-store research lane R-02, 2026-11.
terms.note: Category changed to our-harness: they are the harness's test cases, though drawn from FixFlow history.

terms.definition: BM25 is a word-matching formula whose scores only order results within one query. IDF weights rare words. IDF-weighted coverage is the share of a query's rare-word weight an entry matches.
terms.origin: Information-retrieval field; BM25 is built into SQLite FTS5.

terms.definition: Node's built-in SQLite module (release candidate) and the settings that let many readers and one writer share a file safely and wait briefly when it is busy.
terms.origin: Node.js and SQLite.

terms.term: Stampede / single-flight / claim / fencing token / Lamport counter
terms.definition: Stampede: several sessions repeating costly work. Claim: the first proceeds. Fencing token (claim_seq): marks a stale holder. Lamport counter: orders events from several writers.
terms.origin: Caching practice; Martin Kleppmann (fencing); Leslie Lamport (logical clocks).

terms.definition: A file named by the sha256 of its own sorted-key JSON bytes, so replaying an event is harmless. SHA-256 is the fingerprint used to pin versions.
terms.origin: General content-addressing practice.

terms.term: Memoization / case-based reasoning / KEDB / KCS / elastic-recheck
terms.definition: Memoization: reusing earlier answers. Case-based reasoning: solving by retrieving similar past cases. KEDB: known-error database. KCS: knowledge-centred service. elastic-recheck: OpenStack's tool matching failures to known-bug queries.
terms.origin: Computer science; Aamodt and Plaza 1994; ITIL practice; OpenStack.
terms.note: Definition kept at about 30 words.

terms.definition: ReasoningBank stores distilled lessons from agent failures and cut SWE-bench steps by 4-9 % [S]. Gloaguen et al. found repository context files raise cost over 20 % [S] without general success gains.
terms.origin: Outside research papers, cited in the knowledge-store design.
terms.note: Tagged the outside figures [S].

terms.definition: RRF: reciprocal rank fusion of rankings. doc2query: paraphrases generated and added at write time. sqlite-vec: a vector extension for SQLite. bge-small: a small local embedding model.
terms.origin: Information-retrieval research and open-source projects.

terms.definition: Facebook's learned method for choosing which tests to run for a change, cited as outside evidence for selective checking.
terms.origin: Machalica et al., ICSE-SEIP 2019.
terms.note: Outside origin confirmed in KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN.

terms.definition: Data leaving the machine to an outside service, here the model provider.
terms.origin: General security term.

terms.definition: The single place where heavy Docker-based checks may run, so two heavy jobs do not collide on this PC.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the ship plan, 2026-11.

terms.definition: A proposed separate memory of verified solutions that a cheap model fetches, adapts and reuses instead of calling a stronger model. Designed and modelled in the pathway map; not built or proven.
terms.origin: Coined by the owner; described in the harness v2 design and library pathway documents, 2026-11.
terms.note: Origin corrected to match the owner-coined library; added 'or proven'.

terms.definition: The order a failed problem climbs: one cheap retry, then Opus, then Fable, with the solution stored on the way back.
terms.origin: Coined by us (the owner's design) in the library goal, 2026-11.

terms.definition: The library model's cost unit: one call by the cheap model (Sonnet) costs 1 [I]; other costs are multiples of it.
terms.origin: Coined by us in library-pathways model-brief.md, 2026-11.
terms.note: Tagged 1 as illustrative [I], since it is a unit definition inside a model.

terms.definition: The owner's five expectations: E1 big token cut over time; E2 faster responses and builds; E3 Sonnet at low effort matching Opus; E4 reuse across projects; E5 accurate, efficient lookups.
terms.origin: The owner, 2026-11-12.

terms.definition: A model of the library as a graph of states work passes through, with chances and costs on each branch. It shows the mechanism; its figures are model outputs from guessed inputs [G], not a forecast.
terms.origin: Coined by us; built in docs/program/library-pathways/, 2026-11.
terms.note: Added the [G] caveat required for library-pathway figures.

terms.definition: Strong model directly (top_first), cheap model with the ladder (cheap_ladder), and cheap model with the library. All three run on the same pieces of work.
terms.origin: Coined by us in library-pathways model-brief.md, 2026-11.

terms.definition: One point where a result is produced and checked, about ten [G] cheap calls, visible or latent. A wrong output that passes the gate is an escape.
terms.origin: Coined by us in library-pathways model-brief.md, 2026-11.
terms.note: Tagged 'about ten' as a model input [G].

terms.definition: A chart starting with 100 [I] pieces of work the cheap model would get wrong alone, showing how many remain wrong after each step toward a right answer.
terms.origin: Coined by us when building the pathway page, 2026-11.
terms.note: Tagged 100 as illustrative [I].

terms.term: Three conditions (comes back, reach, entry quality)
terms.definition: Comes back: much work repeats. Reach: an entry gets to the cheap model. Entry quality: the entry is right and used rightly. A fourth group is running cost.
terms.origin: Coined by us in model-brief.md revision 4, 2026-11.

terms.definition: Corners set each condition group at its poor or good end. All-good puts every library unknown at its good end. Tie is how strongly a group's unknowns move together (0 independent, 1 shared).
terms.origin: Coined by us in model-brief.md revisions 4 and R18b, 2026-11.

terms.definition: Alone: the effect of moving only one limitation's unknowns. Last: what is lost if only that one stays unsolved. Both are shares of the full fall.
terms.origin: Coined by us in model-brief.md R19, 2026-11.

terms.definition: Running the model thousands of times [G] with unknown settings drawn from their ranges to get a spread and ranking. A second meaning is a trained set of decision trees predicting a route.
terms.origin: Ensemble modelling in statistics; proposed by the owner for the pathway map.
terms.note: Overlaps with n=232 Monte-Carlo runs; kept as a separate entry because it carries the second meaning. 'Thousands' tagged [G].

terms.definition: A view listing every route from start to outcome, with its chance and cost on each branch.
terms.origin: Reliability engineering; proposed by the owner for the pathway map.
terms.note: Category changed to general-cs: the method is a reliability-engineering technique, not a statistics measure.

terms.definition: Ids of the 69 [M] limitations found by walking real cases through the library design's ten steps: 54 [M] seen in real cases, 15 [M] from thought experiments.
terms.origin: Coined by us in limitations.json, 2026-11.
terms.note: Tagged counts [M].

terms.definition: The ten steps: task arrives, trigger, query, match, delivery, use, check, failure and ladder, capture, afterlife. Ten case families group real cases; ids like f10-1b name family and case.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the library design walks, 2026-11.

terms.definition: A misleading stored entry that matches a problem's symptoms but has a different cause.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the pathway model, 2026-11.

terms.definition: Mechanical checks from stored entries moved into the shared test run, so every piece of work passes them with no lookup.
terms.origin: Coined by us; the knowledge-store design D17 drains entries into CI.

terms.definition: Coverage ceilings: long-run limits on what the library could hold for exact, similar or composite problems, drawn from outside studies. Oracle-match trial: give Sonnet the best earlier solution on held-out past problems and score by tests.
terms.origin: Coined by us in model-brief.md and the 2026-11-12 library review.
terms.note: The trial is a plan, not a result; wording kept as a design.

terms.definition: Placeholder removed.
terms.origin: n/a
terms.note: Empty placeholder; no definition to keep.

terms.definition: Railway hosts the apps (old hostnames answer an edge 404). Supabase is managed Postgres, recorded as paused or dead. Cloudflare R2 stores media and backups.
terms.origin: Outside vendors; stack described in CLAUDE.md.
terms.note: Cleaned the term name; wording otherwise kept from the record.

terms.definition: Postgres 16 runs in test containers and 17 matches production. pg_restore restores a dump. Appendix C is the design recipe for a throwaway Postgres 17 restore.
terms.origin: PostgreSQL open source; our orchestration design notes.

terms.term: Backend gate tools (Alembic, ruff, mypy, lint-imports, pytest, pip-audit)
terms.definition: Migrations, lint and format, type check, import-boundary check, tests, and an advisory dependency vulnerability scan.
terms.origin: Outside open-source Python tools.

terms.definition: Test runners for the mobile code (Jest) and the web code (Vitest).
terms.origin: Open-source JavaScript tools.
terms.note: Added which runner covers which app, per CLAUDE.md.

terms.definition: Continuous integration: the automated checks that run on the repository (GitHub Actions, pinned to Node 22).
terms.origin: General software practice.

terms.term: Docker / container / Docker Desktop / WSL2 / Compose project
terms.definition: Docker runs isolated environments. Docker Desktop runs Linux containers inside WSL2, a Linux virtual machine on Windows that holds much of this PC's memory. A Compose project is containers started together.
terms.origin: Docker Inc. and Microsoft.

terms.definition: A Docker option that lets the gates container use the database container's network, so the database appears at localhost.
terms.origin: Docker feature.

terms.definition: Memory an operating system keeps for recently read files. On this PC the Docker VM held gigabytes of it that Windows could not use.
terms.origin: General operating-system concept.

terms.definition: A Windows log entry for a restart without clean shutdown (24 [M] on this PC). A bugcheck is a crash with a stop code; 23 of 24 [M] had code 0.
terms.origin: Microsoft Windows.
terms.note: Tagged counts [M].

terms.definition: A Windows call that prevents sleep while a program runs. Hybrid sleep saves memory to disk before sleeping. Mains is wall power. BitLocker is Windows disk encryption.
terms.origin: Microsoft Windows; electrical supply term.

terms.definition: The third-party real-time scanner on this PC, which has blocked some DLLs during unpacking and so affects installs.
terms.origin: Third-party security product from Qihoo 360.
terms.note: Softened wording to a plain statement of the effect.

terms.definition: A Windows feature that lets an Android emulator run hardware-accelerated without /dev/kvm.
terms.origin: Microsoft Windows.

terms.definition: A software phone for tests. ff34 is the one virtual device set up on this PC (Android 14, 2 GB [S] RAM).
terms.origin: Google Android tools; the device name is ours.
terms.note: Tagged RAM [S].

terms.definition: Two versions of the JavaScript runtime. The project targets 22 and the machine has 24.
terms.origin: Node.js project.

terms.term: Device lab (L3) / lab accounts / edge 404 stand-in
terms.definition: A native emulator rig with scripted protocols to rehearse the drain and offline matrix before a real phone. Lab accounts and keys are test-only. Stand-in modes mimic the dead host: edge404, 5xx or a hang.
terms.origin: Coined by us in SHIP-PLAN section 7.5 and L3a, 2026-11.

terms.term: Expo / EAS / APK / expo prebuild / Gradle / assembleRelease
terms.definition: Expo: the React Native toolkit. EAS: its build service. APK: the Android install file. expo prebuild generates native folders (kept out of the repo). Gradle's assembleRelease builds a release APK.
terms.origin: Expo; Google Android.

terms.term: adb / dumpsys / logcat / apksigner / aapt2 / JDK
terms.definition: Android tools: adb talks to a phone; dumpsys and logcat read state and logs; apksigner checks signing; aapt2 reads APK info; a JDK runs Gradle.
terms.origin: Google Android SDK; Temurin JDK build.

terms.definition: An open-source mobile UI test tool that drives app screens from scripted flows. We proposed it for on-device smoke tests; it is a proposal, not a measured part of the gates.
terms.origin: Outside open-source tool, named in our skills packages and orchestration design.
terms.note: Added the proposed-not-measured caveat.

terms.definition: Original equipment manufacturer: here the phone makers (Xiaomi, Oppo, Vivo) whose battery policies can stop background apps.
terms.origin: General industry term.
terms.note: Expanded the acronym.

terms.term: Outbox / queues / drain / fleet drain protocol (O-10) / release/drain / hold notice
terms.definition: The outbox is the phone's offline queue of unsent writes, never deleted. Drain empties it into the recovered backend by an ordered protocol (O-10) on branch release/drain, after a hold notice telling technicians not to reset the app.
terms.origin: FixFlow mobile design (CLAUDE.md); drain and hold notice coined by us in the ship plan.

terms.term: Fleet APK v1 / v2 / deploy train / T_close
terms.definition: v1: the first drain build, with P2a and P2b-1 only. v2: built after P4c. Deploy train: behaviour-changing PRs merged before cutover. T_close: the end of the cutover window.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the ship plan, 2026-11.

terms.definition: Urdu bookkeeping terms: the informal operational ledger (the app) versus the formal approved ledger that flows to Odoo.
terms.origin: Urdu bookkeeping terms used by the owner.

terms.definition: Odoo is accounting software that receives the approved ledger. JSON-2 is its newer API. External IDs act as the exactly-once key.
terms.origin: Outside product (Odoo).

terms.definition: Recovery point objective (how much data may be lost) and recovery time objective (how long recovery may take).
terms.origin: Disaster-recovery field.

terms.term: ASVS / MASVS / SRB / FBR / NOT VALID then VALIDATE
terms.definition: OWASP security checklists for web and mobile apps; Sindh Revenue Board and Federal Board of Revenue (Pakistan taxes); a Postgres pattern that adds a constraint without scanning, then validates rows later.
terms.origin: OWASP; Pakistan tax authorities; PostgreSQL.

terms.term: TanStack DB / Cloudflare R2 / cloudflared / Caddy / Dependabot / VPS / git-shell / MSIX
terms.definition: Outside tools named in skills and the store design: offline-sync library, object storage, tunnel, web server, dependency updater, rented server, restricted git login shell, Windows app packaging.
terms.origin: Outside vendors and open-source projects.

terms.definition: TID251 is a Ruff lint rule that bans named APIs such as hmac.compare_digest. compare_secret is our safe secret-compare helper, because the raw call raises on non-ASCII strings.
terms.origin: Ruff linter; our own code, per CLAUDE.md.

terms.definition: Deploying the backend from the repo root rebuilt the API as the web app and caused a production outage. Deploy only from backend/.
terms.origin: Our project history, recorded in CLAUDE.md.
terms.note: Stated as the rule to follow, in plain words.

terms.definition: An existing generic security-audit skill that our appsec-review-asvs skill package builds on.
terms.origin: Listed among the skills available to our Claude Code sessions.

glossary.notes: Checked outside-origin claims against KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN, HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS and the graph2 research notes. Confirmed: Build Systems a la Carte (ICFP 2018), Machalica et al. ICSE-SEIP 2019, Aamodt and Plaza 1994, Kleppmann and Lamport, elastic-recheck, ReasoningBank, Gloaguen et al. Main correction: co-change 0.26 is precision in a list of ten (tune commits), not recall (n=209). Added [G]/[M]/[S]/[T]/[I] tags to figures. Added designed-not-proven wording to the knowledge store and library, and the scripted-search-not-agent note (n=228). Dropped n=278 (empty placeholder). n=232 and n=271 overlap (Monte-Carlo versus ensemble) but are not exact duplicates; both kept and cross-noted. A few definitions (n=242, 254, 245) run slightly over 30 words because they bundle several terms; the program may split them if a hard limit applies. Did not verify Zep/Graphiti ownership, Qihoo 360 and OWASP expansions beyond general knowledge; origins are phrased plainly.

added.definition: One running Claude Code conversation with its own context window and tools. Ours come as orchestrator, coordinator and lane sessions; each starts fresh and can be parked or resumed.
added.origin: Claude Code usage; the unit every harness rule is written for.

added.definition: Anthropic's coding agent that runs in a terminal or desktop app. Our harness is the set of rules, scripts and checks built around its sessions.
added.origin: Anthropic product; the tool all our sessions run in.

added.definition: The company that makes the Claude models and Claude Code. Its usage limit and price list set the budget the harness works within.
added.origin: Outside vendor; source of models, limits and list prices.

added.definition: Tokens a model spends reasoning before it answers. They count as output tokens and so as usage, even though the reasoning is not shown in the reply.
added.origin: Model behaviour; counted inside output tokens in our token measurements.

added.definition: A model's rung on the ladder from Haiku to Sonnet to Opus to Fable: higher tiers think better and cost more per token. We route work by tier.
added.origin: Anthropic naming; our routing memory note assigns jobs to tiers.

added.definition: The low-cost tier used for routine reading and checking, versus the high-cost tier kept for judgement. The escalation ladder moves work from the first to the second only when needed.
added.origin: Library design (LIBRARY-PATHWAYS); the cheap-call equivalent is measured against this pair.

added.definition: The branch holding the accepted state of the code. Work merges into it only after the check and a review; a deploy is cut from it.
added.origin: Git convention; FixFlow's default branch is main.

added.definition: A named line of commits that a slice or lane works on, kept apart from the main line until the work is reviewed and merged.
added.origin: Git; each lane and slice gets its own branch and worktree.

added.definition: One saved, named change to the code in git. Reviews bind to a specific commit, and a finding closes on a commit.
added.origin: Git; our verdicts name the head commit they were made on.

added.definition: A proposal on GitHub to merge a branch into main, with its changes, discussion and checks. Several of our design documents live as numbered PRs.
added.origin: GitHub; see PR #182 to #186.

added.definition: Bringing a reviewed branch into the main line. In harness v2 a script does it, through the merge queue, after one check.
added.origin: Git; harness v2 mechanism that removes root edits at merge.

added.definition: The last commit on a branch at the moment it merges. We want a reader to have read exactly this commit, not an earlier one.
added.origin: Bottleneck B17: 5 of 6 high-risk merges had an unread final head [M].

added.definition: One concrete defect or gap a reviewer or scan reports, with a path:line citation and a severity. It closes only on a test the harness runs.
added.origin: Review practice in the ship plan and testbed; tracked in the finding table.

added.definition: One pass in which a reviewer reads a branch and returns findings, followed by fixes. The harness aims to cap rounds at two.
added.origin: Testbed record: 2.8 rounds per slice [M]; fix-round contract target.

added.definition: A reviewer returning a slice to its author with findings to fix, instead of passing it to merge. Each send-back adds a review round.
added.origin: Testbed review loop; the fix-round contract limits how many are allowed.

added.definition: A pass that fixes findings. The contract: a test per finding that fails before and passes after, full gate before the fix commit, revert instead of patching, a fresh reviewer.
added.origin: Bottleneck B01 mechanism 9; to be replayed on recorded chains before live use.

added.definition: A reviewer or agent started without the author's earlier conversation, so it cannot inherit the author's assumptions. Costs a new fixed prefix each time.
added.origin: Refuter and fresh-reviewer practice; about 70k fixed tokens per agent [M].

added.definition: The six labels we give every idea: idea, designed, built, tested, in use, parked. It stops a design being described as a result.
added.origin: Compile's own honesty rule, matching the must-not-claim rules.

added.definition: The check run directly on Windows rather than in a Linux container. Slower (6.1 minutes [M]) and hit by the loopback socket error; the container run is the faster route.
added.origin: Bottleneck work on the gate; compare the container run at 3.8 minutes [M].

added.definition: The most memory one check uses at its worst moment. It was never measured; the second check slot waits on it.
added.origin: Bottleneck B07: slots are to be sized from one measured number.

added.definition: A database private to one lane's checkout, with its own port and compose project, so parallel checks cannot corrupt each other.
added.origin: Testbed isolation design (A8-08); restarted by the restart chain.

added.definition: A query of the knowledge store or library before exploring, triggered by an error, an escalation or a diff. It returns leads or abstains.
added.origin: Knowledge-store design; lookup-only calls are what the index replay measures.

added.definition: When a stored entry may no longer be true because the code changed. Handled by validity conditions and probes, not by time-based expiry.
added.origin: Knowledge-store design; time expiry is on the do-not-build list.

added.definition: Modelling a system as stocks, flows and feedback loops, then running it. We use it to describe the harness and the library, with loops R1 to R4 and B1 to B5.
added.origin: Owner's request for architecture as stocks, flows and loops with a runnable model.

added.definition: The range expected to hold the true value in 95 of 100 repeats of a test. A difference smaller than the interval cannot be told from noise.
added.origin: Statistics; used with the bootstrap in the held-out graph test.

added.definition: A map of the code whose edges are labelled by kind (import, caller, test-of, crosses-runtime) rather than file-level imports only. Tried in the second graph test design.
added.origin: Owner's objections to the first graph test; replacement test protocol.

added.definition: Software that stores nodes and edges and answers multi-hop queries natively, such as LadybugDB or DuckDB with graph support. Under test against SQLite.
added.origin: Graph-test research; engine choice is the owner's pending install decision.

added.definition: A zero-token test: build an import-and-caller index at each recorded window's start, count the lookup-only calls it would have answered. First candidate trial of phase 3.
added.origin: Harness v2 design, phase 3 and decision D23.

added.definition: A generated view of slices, verdicts and findings, each with the commit it became true at and the commit that replaced it. Replaces the hand-edited board.
added.origin: Harness v2 library first half; board target under 20 KB [T] from 221 KB [M].

added.definition: A script that closes or reopens a gate round without a model: for each closed P1 citing a test, it runs the test at the fix's parent and counts failures.
added.origin: Harness v2 script 2; checked by a replay on the record.

added.definition: A script reading the sessions' own tool-call records to show who read the final head, whether the gate ran before each fix, and root edits per merge.
added.origin: Harness v2 script 3; replayed over the 10 and 11 November merges.

added.definition: A file each slice commits listing what it claims, so a script can check every cited test exists, ran, and fails when its guard is removed.
added.origin: Bottleneck B12; over 20 recorded overstatements [M] motivate it.

added.definition: A rule that an environment fact reported by an agent or stated by me is checked by one command before it becomes a harness rule.
added.origin: Harness v2 mechanism 7, from five facts the bottleneck list got wrong.

added.definition: At sign-in, a list of sessions that were mid-work and where each branch stands. Sessions are released two at a time; a mismatched record parks itself.
added.origin: Bottleneck B03 and decision D06.

added.definition: Docker starts at sign-in, the databases in use restart themselves, and the check starts its own database if missing, so work resumes after a power-off without commands.
added.origin: Bottleneck B10 and decision D03; nothing restarted in the three idle days.

added.definition: A verified bundle of every branch, plus uncommitted work and transcripts, copied off the PC nightly. Protects against the unexpected power-offs and disk loss.
added.origin: Bottleneck B11; harness v2 phase 1.

added.definition: A small tool recording power, temperature and memory on the PC so the unexpected shutdowns can be diagnosed from data. I allowed one tool (decision D05).
added.origin: Bottleneck B05; harness v2 phase 1.

added.definition: Running the first-deploy checklist on a real host: fresh-machine restore, off-site push, an alert with a planted failure. Each step has a command, expected result and failing run.
added.origin: Bottleneck B19; harness v2 phase 4.

added.definition: A server rented for one day to rehearse deployment and rerun the load drill, using made-up data only.
added.origin: Bottlenecks B19 and B20; free steps come first.

added.definition: A test with many simulated users against the app: the 12-user drill [M] to be rerun on current main, then a bulk generator to 250,000 [T] stock movements.
added.origin: Bottleneck B20; harness v2 phase 4.

added.definition: Deciding what goes into a session's context and what stays out, so the model stays useful. Horthy's name for the craft behind our hot set and library ideas.
added.origin: Dex Horthy and HumanLayer; sweep recorded in PR #186.

added.definition: The Python web framework behind the FixFlow backend, with async SQLAlchemy and Alembic. Named here because the backend gate steps run against it.
added.origin: CLAUDE.md stack table; Python 3.12 backend.

added.definition: A self-contained piece of harness work a team member can pick up from the PDF, with its goal, steps and a test that says it is done.
added.origin: This compile's hand-off format for readers who were not in the sessions.

added.definition: A choice only I can make, such as installing a tool or allowing a sensor logger. Listed as D01 to D23 with a default and what it unlocks.
added.origin: Harness v2 decision table; the [owner] step in plans.

added.definition: The rule that all agent-adding changes share a single written token and lane budget: two lanes at a time, one change per window, state on disk.
added.origin: Harness v2 section 6; the refuter warned remedies together recreate the stops.

added.definition: A gate or review mechanism is accepted by replaying it on the recorded history first, record-only, before it may refuse anything live.
added.origin: Harness v2 standing principle with script before agent and one budget.

added.definition: In our work, a line of waiting items: the check slot queue with a printed position, the merge queue, or the phone's write queues. Context says which.
added.origin: Bottleneck B07 (fair queue); mobile queues in CLAUDE.md.

added.term: Maturity label: idea / designed / built / tested / in use / parked
added.definition: The same maturity scale shown as the six values a card may carry. A design is never reported as a result.
added.origin: Compile honesty rule; see Maturity scale.

Read-only check of every claim id in docs/program/evidence/harness-compile/data/gate/fixed-claims.md. There are no ids N29, N37-N39 or N42-N49 in that file.

The most important corrections:
- N32: the outside-mobile interval was copied from the memory note. The generated result file gives [−0.023, +0.075].
- N33: the baseline already includes personalised PageRank. Use the wording addendum 6 item 10 requires.
- N09: 'not published' is not in any source; the sources say 'unknown'.
- N14: 'about 40× [M]' is a derived number with no source behind it.
- N06, N21, N24, N41: tags were dropped ([E] on 'about a third', [M] on 38 of 48 and on the class counts, [G] on 'about 32').
- N51: 'coined' and 'popularised' go beyond the sweep.

Other fixes outside the claim list, from reading the build files:
- The graph recall caption says 'three graph engines', but SQLite is relational.
- The recall caption says 'changed files', but the recall counts files and definitions.
- The graphDiff 'shows' line says the gain over changed-together is clear overall. Outside mobile it is +0.001 [−0.051, +0.056], and both lower bounds sit below the 0.05 smallest effect.
- The ~70k per-agent tile is a clinic figure, printed next to FixFlow's ~60k.
- The 24 shutdowns are counted as of 11 Nov. FINDINGS counts 25 since 1 Oct, and SHIP-PLAN §7.4 records another power loss on 13 Nov.

changes.target: Waves line in package-cards.md ("Start now")
changes.change: Replace "six packages can start today" with a three-way split. (a) Start today, with no owner wait, no agents and no Docker gate: WP8's rate sheet from the record; WP11's merged decision board; WP1's copy and resume scripts (the owner's steps come after P0a); WP3's four zero-token, zero-check-time scripts (sealed replay, transcript audit, finding table, dry run with stand-in agents); WP5's budget proposal for D07, built from the saved baseline. (b) Prepared today but blocked on the owner: WP6 (the limitation list agreed, KS D1/D1b), WP7 (D23 before the index replay, the graph-engine install before any engine arm), WP10 (the merge of PR #185). (c) After the machine or the check: WP2, WP4, WP9.
changes.reason: As drafted, three of the six cannot deliver their first item without the owner. WP6's is an agreement with me plus the KS D1 audit, which is mine to start. WP7's index replay needs D23, which §5 says comes before the index replay, and its agent arm needs the pending graph-engine install. WP10's is the merge of PR #185, an open owner decision. FixFlow code lanes are running from today (2026-11-13), so the standing rule also bars agent lanes and the Docker gate.

changes.target: All agent-spending packages (WP3 replays, WP5 lever trials, WP6 pilot, WP7 agent arm, WP10 review and fixed-start measurement)
changes.change: Add a hard dependency on D07, the written token budget per window. D07 is decided first, from a proposal WP5 drafts from the saved November baseline. The proposal is the WP5 work listed as start-today.
changes.reason: Under the one-budget rule a token budget is written down before any launch, and §2 says its figure is set in phase 1. D07 is still unanswered in §5. Without it no package may launch an agent, yet only WP5's card names D07.

changes.target: One budget across packages
changes.change: Create one shared queue for agent-adding changes. WP5's governor owns it and WP11's board shows it. Every package that adds an agent (WP3 fresh reviewers and replays, WP5 effort trials, WP6 pilot, WP7 agent arm, WP10 measurements) books a window in this queue. No package launches on its own.
changes.reason: The standing rule is one agent-adding change per window and lanes two at a time. With five packages each adding agents and no shared queue, the rule cannot be kept. §6 warns that the remedies added together recreate the stops.

changes.target: All cards: a 'Before you start' block
changes.change: Give every card a 'Before you start' block that names: (1) the repository the package works in (the clinic testbed or FixFlow) and its path; (2) the branch to use (never main) and where the branch-only docs live (the scratchpad compile/src extraction; PR #182, #183 and #185 branches); (3) how to tell whether a FixFlow phase is running or waiting on its reviewer (the W0-results.md lane board); (4) the machine traps: no docker network create, use the default bridge or --network container:; never prune networks or restart Docker; MSYS_NO_PATHCONV needs C:/ paths; core.longpaths for scratch clones; no python on PATH, so run node .js.txt scripts; never touch the antivirus; (5) that lanes report and the coordinator writes the program files.
changes.reason: Harness v2 is for the clinic build and 'changes no rule of FixFlow's ship plan', yet the packages mix clinic work (WP1 phase 1, WP2's 230 s target, WP9's 11 November walk) with FixFlow work (ff-gates, ship plan §7, PR #185). No card says which repository it means. Each of these traps has already cost a session time.

changes.reason: The owner's D03 answer (11 November) was "Not now. Docker's start at sign-in stays off", and §1 already says the resume list's first line will be 'start Docker'. As written, the done-when contradicts a recorded owner decision.

division.six_can_start: Not as written. FixFlow code lanes started today (2026-11-13). The standing rule therefore bars harness agent lanes and the Docker gate, and D07 (the written token budget, needed before any launch) is still unanswered. Each of the six can start only its zero-token, no-gate part. WP8 (the rate sheet from the record) and WP11 (the merged decision board) can start fully today. WP1 can start its scripts (bundle-and-verify that captures the six uncommitted folders, the nightly copy, the resume list in the clinic repository), but its first deliverable, a verified copy on the encrypted drive, waits on owner steps that the design places after P0a. Three cannot deliver their first item without the owner. WP6 needs the limitation list agreed and the KS D1/D1b go. WP7's index replay needs D23 first, and its agent arm needs the graph-engine install and D07. WP10 needs the owner's merge of PR #185, and its binding review spends an agent. Two packages left out of the start-now wave can start today: WP3's zero-token, zero-check-time scripts (sealed replay, transcript audit, finding table, dry run with stand-in agents), and WP5's D07 budget proposal from the saved baseline. WP5's first deliverable as drafted (the November baseline) is already done according to the design's §1.
division.notes:
Read: docs/program/evidence/harness-compile/data/gate/packages.md, docs/program/evidence/harness-compile/data/gate/package-cards.md, docs/program/HARNESS-V2-DESIGN-2026-11.md §1, §2, §4, §5, §6 and §8, and the ship-plan memory note.

The cross-cutting issue is that harness v2 is a clinic-testbed design ('it changes no rule of FixFlow's ship plan'), while several packages (WP2's ff-gates, WP4's §7 lanes, WP9's lab, WP10's PR #185 and ship-plan process edits, WP11's P0a kit and W0-results) reach into FixFlow, where the coordinator owns the plan and lanes are live today. Every card should say which repository it works in. Every FixFlow-side output should be a proposal to the coordinator, never an edit.

Two cap conflicts a team member could apply wrongly: v2's 'two lanes at a time' is for harness work, while ship plan §7 runs up to about six to eight lane sessions; and ff-slot.sh has three slots, while v2 keeps the second clinic slot shut until the diagnosis. A machine-wide lock across both projects is needed because they share 31 GB of RAM.

Ownership is duplicated in five places: the index replay and the agent arm (WP7 card, WP8 ideas), the rates table (WP4 and WP8), fixed-start measurement (WP5 and WP10), the cold-resume trial (WP8 and WP10), and the single-writer rule (WP3 and WP4).

WP1's done-when contradicts my recorded D03 answer (Docker's start at sign-in stays off).

Cards missing a size or a 'Waiting on me' line: WP4, WP6 (unsized), WP7, WP8, WP10 and WP11.

A mature idea is not a finished deliverable. 'Earlier auto-compact window of 400,000 tokens' is maturity 5 as a build, but the memory note says it was never switched on, and its trial is D22, reported as an anecdote.
